articles.title: 58 arrested in triad crackdown as youth crimes spike
articles.excerpt: Police on Saturday arrested 58 people in a city-wide, anti-triad operation, disrupting gang networks exploiting the youth. The suspects rounded…
articles.fullText:
Police on Saturday arrested 58 people in a city-wide, anti-triad operation, disrupting gang networks exploiting the youth.

The suspects rounded up include core gang members as well as those aged below 18. They are alleged to have committed a series of offenses, including claiming to be triad members, inviting another person to become a triad member, false imprisonment and money laundering.

Chief inspector Chan Pak-ki said the arrests came after undercover officers infiltrated two triad groups amid a rise in youth crimes early this year.

“We found that these triad groups would obtain the youths' trust first. They might carry out simple initiation ceremonies," she said.

"After obtaining their trust, they lured them, through false promises that there was quick money to be made, into carrying out a lot of illegal acts.”

The force also busted a number of illegal gambling and drug dens.

Chan did not rule out further arrests, adding that the operation was still ongoing.

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Lan Kwai Fong expects monster finish to Halloween
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong's premier nightlife and party district Lan Kwai Fong is expecting business to jump about 50 percent this Halloween…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong's premier nightlife and party district Lan Kwai Fong is expecting business to jump about 50 percent this Halloween.

Turnover is already up at least 30 to 40 percent over the past two weekends, according to Anthea Cheung, Lan Kwai Fong Association director. She credited this growth to the Tourism Board's inaugural Hong Kong Halloween Month, which generated significant festive buzz ahead of this weekend's finale and attracted higher-than-expected interest.

Cheung said locals still made up around 70 percent of visitors to the district around which Halloween celebrations traditionally centre, with the rest coming from overseas and the mainland.

The number of arrivals from the Greater Bay Area have spiked with cross-boundary travel made easier, she added, with many of them dressing up for a night out.

Bars and restaurants, she pointed out, have kept some seats in reserve for walk-in customers since bookings for tables are already full.

“We expect about a 50 percent increase tonight – it’s Halloween proper, and it’s a weekend too," Cheung said.

"Our merchants are ready, they’ve stocked enough drinks and food for tonight’s celebrations.”

Looking ahead, the association wants more hotel, dining and transport package deals to draw visitors into staying longer and spending more.

As Lan Kwai Fong gears up to cope with crowds of revellers, immigration officers inspected Huanggang Port and Shenzhen Bay Control Point ahead of an expected late-night outbound peak on Saturday and Sunday by mainlanders here for Halloween night.

The Immigration Department urged travellers seeking a quicker crossing to avoid peak hours where possible, adding that it is coordinating with public transport operators to step up their service frequency.

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Chinese factory activity slips amid strong tech show
articles.excerpt: China's manufacturing activity moderated in October, with the purchasing managers' index falling to 49.3 as the high-tech and equipment manufacturing…
articles.fullText:
China's manufacturing activity moderated in October, with the purchasing managers' index falling to 49.3 as the high-tech and equipment manufacturing sectors maintained expansion, official data showed on Saturday.

The overall reading was down 0.8 percentage points from September, according to the National Bureau of Statistics.

Chief statistician Huo Lihui attributed the retreat to some demand being brought forward ahead of the National Day holiday this month and a complex international environment.

The production subindex stood at 49.8, down 1.9 points from September, while the new-orders subindex fell 1.1 points to 49.4, as both supply and demand moderated during the month.

The PMI for high-tech manufacturing stood at 51.3 while that for equipment manufacturing came in at 50.6, both remaining above the 50-point threshold that separates expansion from contraction.

The figures indicate that emerging industries continued to sustain growth momentum, supported by the ongoing development of new quality productive forces, Huo noted.

Manufacturing activity in several advanced industries remained robust.

Both the production and new-orders subindexes for railway, shipbuilding and aerospace equipment manufacturing, as well as computer, communications and electronic equipment manufacturing, stood at 53 or above, pointing to relatively strong supply and demand in these sectors.

Large manufacturers continued to report expansion, with their PMI standing at 50.2, despite a slight decline of 0.4 points from the previous month.

The PMI readings for medium-sized and small enterprises came in at 48.4 and 47.5, respectively.

On the price front, both major raw material purchasing prices and factory-gate prices remained in expansionary territory, although their growth moderated.

The purchasing price subindex stood at 56.8, down four points from September while the factory-gate price subindex eased 2.3 points to 51.7, partly reflecting recent declines in the prices of certain nonferrous metals and other commodities. (Xinhua)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: More experts 'applying to join building-repairs lists'
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn said government has received an encouraging response from consultants and contractors seeking inclusion in three…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn said government has received an encouraging response from consultants and contractors seeking inclusion in three pre-qualified lists under a new council that will soon be offering full-cycle building repairs.

The non-statutory Building Maintenance Support and Services Council – to be established by year-end – will gradually take over the Urban Renewal Authority’s building-upkeep subsidy schemes under its Smart Tender system.

Taking to the airwaves on Saturday, Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn said the government had received about 150 applications from inspection and supervision consultants as well as 350 applications from contractors.

"Why do I say it’s encouraging? Because the URA’s Smart Tender platform also had a pre-qualified list – now it has been taken down as we have this new one," she said.

"The number of applications this time, compared to the one that was taken down, saw an increase of two to three times.

"This means that there are more consultants and contractors who did not participate in the past. I took it as a vote of confidence in the future system."

While the council will prioritise around 1,800 maintenance projects that are already in the Smart Tender system, Linn said it would first focus on the 600 or so projects that had yet to undergo building inspections.

“As inspections have not been carried out on these buildings, we can – when the new service is rolled out – deploy an inspection consultant for them,” she said.

Most of the remaining buildings, she pointed out, have already recruited supervision consultants.

Initially, the government had been planning to put the URA or its subsidiaries in charge of the new support service.

However, Linn said, following through on that plan would have significantly increased the URA's burden as it was already handling many building maintenance-related works as well as redevelopment projects.

As for the new Public Housing Building Control Section that will replace the Housing Bureau’s Independent Checking Unit within a month, Deputy Financial Secretary Michael Wong said he was confident that it would bring about more fundamental changes.

About 300 staff from the unit, which has been found by an independent inquiry to be primarily responsible for failed supervision of major renovations at Wang Fuk Court in the runup to the fire, will move to the new section.

“We have held more than 10 training classes [for staff] so as to raise vigilance and awareness,” said Wong, who is also acting secretary for housing.

A dedicated team will oversee each major maintenance project, while a project liaison officer will handle all enquiries from owners’ corporations, he added.

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: HK may see strongest growth in five years: Paul Chan
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong could record its strongest full-year economic growth figure in five years in 2026, according to Financial Secretary Paul…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong could record its strongest full-year economic growth figure in five years in 2026, according to Financial Secretary Paul Chan.

Speaking on a radio programme on Saturday, he said the economy grew by 5.1 percent in the first half of the year and that strong export performance and investment growth continued into the third quarter.

"What I'm most pleased to see is that in terms of investment, the growth momentum in the first half of the year carried through into the third quarter," Chan said.

"Visitor numbers to Hong Kong are high, the streets are busy, and we're holding many mega events – such as the Wine and Dine Festival – plus many other big events and concerts.

"We have FinTech Week coming up. There's a chance that 2026 will be the strongest full-year economic growth in the past five years."

On next year’s budget, Chan said any relief measures would depend on economic performance.

He said the government would do its best but substantial infrastructure spending ahead meant authorities would need to manage public finances closely.

He also flagged external risks.

If geopolitical tensions and the Middle East conflict persist, oil prices could rise and feed into inflationary pressures, Chan stressed.

He expects interest rates to stay relatively high next year, which could affect the property market and the wider economy, and said the authorities would remain alert to financial risks.

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Buildings-repair body 'to operate on user-pays basis'
articles.excerpt: The new Building Maintenance Support and Services Council will operate on a non-profit basis but must recover costs on a…
articles.fullText:
The new Building Maintenance Support and Services Council will operate on a non-profit basis but must recover costs on a user-pays basis, Financial Secretary Paul Chan said on Saturday, as the government moves to set it up in response to the independent committee report on the Wang Fuk Court fire.

The council will guide owners through the full cycle of building repairs – handling tendering and evaluation on their behalf – for a fee.

Chan told a Commercial Radio programme that the non-statutory company, wholly owned by Financial Secretary Incorporated, must recover costs, as owners are responsible for maintaining private residential properties.

He said the fees would depend on the scope of the works and would cost roughly several thousand dollars per flat.

"We understand that Hong Kong has many old districts, and some buildings are quite old," Chan said.

"Many elderly people live there, and they may not be able to fully afford the fees. So in these areas, the government can provide some subsidies."

For better-off owners, professional guidance matters more than cash subsidies, so a one-size-fits-all subsidy ratio would not be appropriate, Chan pointed out.

He said a pre-screened list of professionals and contractors would be published for owners to choose from, describing it as government-checked to give owners greater peace of mind.

The government has earmarked HK$300 million for the plan, including HK$100 million as start-up capital and HK$200 million to subsidise owners.

The new body is expected to start operating by the end of the year, with recruitment for a chief executive already underway.

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Kane edges Mbappe by narrow margin
articles.excerpt: Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or by the smallest margin under its current voting system when he edged Kylian Mbappe…
articles.fullText:
Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or by the smallest margin under its current voting system when he edged Kylian Mbappe by 28 points, France Football which runs the awards, revealed on Friday.

The magazine published a breakdown of the votes in its Friday edition.

Bayern Munich's Kane, the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001, received 40 first-place votes from the 100 jurors and a total of 1,055 points. France captain Mbappe of Real Madrid was placed first 23 times and finished with 1,027 points.

The previous smallest margin was 41 when Rodri, then of Manchester City, edged another Real player Vinicius Junior by 41 points in 2024.

Last season, Paris Saint-Germain forward Ousmane Dembele totalled 1,380 points as he finished 321 points ahead of Lamine Yamal of Barcelona.

This summer, Yamal won a World Cup with Spain but he finished third in the voting on 881 points, 174 behind Kane.

The Ballon d'Or is awarded following a vote by journalists (one per country) representing the top 100 nations in the Fifa rankings for men, and the top 50 for women. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: HKEAA reports international exam data leak
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Examinations and Assessment Authority said on Friday that the personal data of 16,900 mainland residents applying for…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Examinations and Assessment Authority said on Friday that the personal data of 16,900 mainland residents applying for two international exams had been leaked.

The data included names, dates of birth, and email addresses.

The authority said it had discovered the incident on Thursday and reported it to the police and to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data.

It said there was so far no evidence that DSE or other exams had been affected.

The authority apologised and said it would take all feasible measures to mitigate the incident's impact. It said relevant examination organisers had been notified, and it was following up on arrangements to notify those affected.

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Millions cast early votes in US midterms
articles.excerpt: A record 47.9 million Americans have already voted in next week's US midterm elections, with participation surging in key battleground…
articles.fullText:
A record 47.9 million Americans have already voted in next week's US midterm elections, with participation surging in key battleground states and registered Democrats outpacing Republicans, figures showed on Friday.

The University of Florida's Election Lab had recorded 47,922,669 early votes nationwide by midday, surpassing the previous midterm record of 45.9 million cast ahead of Election Day in 2022.

The surge is especially pronounced in states with fiercely contested Senate races that could determine control of the chamber during the final two years of President Donald Trump's presidency.

In Texas, more than six million people had voted early by Wednesday, according to official figures, with in-person turnout running around 50 percent ahead of the same stage in 2022.

North Carolina's election board reported early voting up nearly 37 percent on the same point four years ago, while South Carolina surpassed its entire 2022 early vote total on Monday, with five days of early voting still to go.

In Kansas, where Republican Senator Roger Marshall faces a tough re-election fight, advance ballots were running around two-thirds ahead of 2022 last week, according to the secretary of state's office.

In states that record voters' party affiliation, registered Democrats have accounted for a substantially larger share of early ballots than Republicans.

Election Lab figures showed Democrats making up around 44 percent of early voters in those states, compared with 31 percent for Republicans and 25 percent for unaffiliated or minor-party voters.

University of Florida political scientist Michael McDonald, who oversees the Election Lab, has pointed to rising participation among Black and Hispanic voters in states that report racial and ethnic data, with particularly strong turnout in heavily Hispanic communities along the Texas-Mexico border.

In Georgia, where early in-person voting broke the state's midterm record on Thursday, women accounted for 56 percent of ballots cast by that day, compared with 44 percent for men.

"Georgians continue to head to the polls in record numbers because they trust the system," top elections official Brad Raffensperger said Thursday.

But experts warn against interpreting the figures as a prediction of the election outcome.

A voter's party registration does not reveal which candidates they supported, and tens of millions more Americans are expected to cast ballots on Tuesday.

In recent elections Republicans have tended to turn out in greater numbers on Election Day, potentially narrowing or reversing the Democrats' early advantage.

And higher early participation does not necessarily translate into higher overall turnout, since some voters may simply be casting ballots sooner than in previous elections. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: US markets hit by big tech sell-off
articles.excerpt: The sell-off for tech stocks on Wall Street worsened on Friday on fears that the frenzy around AI has sent…
articles.fullText:
The sell-off for tech stocks on Wall Street worsened on Friday on fears that the frenzy around AI has sent prices too high.

The S&P 500 dropped 140.32 points, or 1.8 percent, to 7,580.07, for its worst day since June.

The Nasdaq composite fell 747.72 points, or 2.9 percent, to 25,437.00, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 572.25 points, or 1.1 percent, to 51,770.31.

Intel sank almost 29 percent for its worst day since 1974 after its profit forecast was below analysts’ expectations.

Amazon’s latest profit report raised more worries about how much companies are spending on their AI Investments.

Treasury yields sank as investors searched for safer things to own, even though oil prices rose. (AP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: EU, Canada move closer in face of Trump isolationism
articles.excerpt: The EU and Canada announced an alliance on Friday aimed at cementing their own relations in the face of US…
articles.fullText:
The EU and Canada announced an alliance on Friday aimed at cementing their own relations in the face of US President Donald Trump's moves to tear up US ties with its old partners.

The EU said Canada will work closer with Brussels on anything from critical minerals to artificial intelligence, after a two-day summit in Montreal.

"The world's becoming more dangerous and divided. Our societies are being shaken by new storms," Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney told a press conference, mentioning eroding democratic norms and "the weaponization of trade".

"Together, Canada and the European Union are anchoring the ground. Anchoring our ground to uphold our values while forming a protective canopy under which our citizens can all thrive," he said after talks with EU chiefs Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa

Already sharing a free trade agreement, Canada and the EU have sought to move closer together since Trump's shock return to power.

Both Canada and the EU have been hit with US tariffs and territorial threats.

Ahead of the talks on Friday, Von der Leyen, the European Commission president, said Canada could not become a "full-fledged" EU member due to its geographical location, but the bloc wanted to bring it "as close as possible".

More broadly Canada and the EU are building what a statement called an "alliance for the future to create a common prosperity and economic security space."

As part of this, they signed a digital trade deal and a separate pact allowing the European Investment Bank to back Canadian critical mineral projects.

Canada is rich in rare earths and critical minerals Europe currently sources mostly from China but needs massive infrastructure investment to jump-start its mining industry.

Europe opened its supercomputing infrastructure to Canadian researchers, industry and start-ups.

The allies also agreed to deepen cooperation on satellite connectivity and navigation and artificial intelligence -- a field where they are playing catch-up with the US and China.

On Thursday, Ottawa announced a C$1.6 billion investment in the Canadian AI firm Cohere. The company has recently partnered with Germany's Aleph Alpha in a move that Carney said was an example of what Europe and Canada could do together.

The two parties launched work towards Canada's participation in EU initiatives like the Erasmus program, which allows university students to spend a semester abroad, and the Galileo satellite program -- an alternative to the American Global Positioning System (GPS). (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Stage is set for Legal Week
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong Legal Week 2026 will open on Monday, bringing together legal professionals, business leaders, policymakers, academics, and leading legal…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong Legal Week 2026 will open on Monday, bringing together legal professionals, business leaders, policymakers, academics, and leading legal organisations from around the world.

The participants will explore topics including international legal co-operation, international dispute resolution, foreign-related rule of law, lawtech and opportunities in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area.

Themed "Collaboration & Innovation: Legal Synergy for a Shared Future" this year, the event will be held over five days.

It will kick off with the "International Institute for Unification of Private Law (UNIDROIT) Centenary: Regional Conference for the Asia-Pacific and Opening Ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Liaison Office" on Monday.

The 3rd Asia-Pacific International Private Law Summit will be held on Tuesday.

In celebration of the 60th anniversary of the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL), an event titled "UNCITRAL’s Contribution to the International Transport of Goods in the Digital Economy – A Celebration of UNCITRAL@60 at Hong Kong Legal Week" will be held on Wednesday.

A highlight of this year's Legal Week, the Hong Kong LawTech Fest will feature dynamic exhibitions, live demonstrations and, on Thursday, the hosting of the LawTech Forum, with a focus on fostering collaboration between legal and technology professionals.

On the morning of the same day, the Fourth Legal Forum on Interconnectivity and Development will examine Hong Kong's role as an all-round international dispute resolution hub and its position in the country's development of foreign-related rule of law.

Closing the event on a high note, the Second Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Lawyers Forum will advance the "soft connectivity" of legal and dispute resolution practices in the bay area.

For live broadcasts, visit the event’s dedicated website or the Information Services Department’s webpage .

articles.title: Wine & Dine Festival draws crowds
articles.excerpt: Organised by the Tourism Board, the Wine & Dine Festival kicked off on Thursday, beginning a four-day run, at the…
articles.fullText:
Organised by the Tourism Board, the Wine & Dine Festival kicked off on Thursday, beginning a four-day run, at the Central Harbourfront Event Space and Tamar Park. This year's festival features more than 340 booths - a 10% increase over last year.

Many festival-goers have been dressing up in costumes to relish the fun and embrace this year’s theme: "Taste the World's Best".

The festival attracts lovers of wine and food from Hong Kong, the Chinese Mainland and overseas. One British tourist who had attended the event previously praised it as a vibrant, exciting reason to visit Hong Kong. He added that his itinerary in Hong Kong is always so packed that he can never complete everything he wants to do, prompting him to return repeatedly.

Meanwhile, a tourist from Guangzhou had made a special two-day trip to Hong Kong to enjoy a few drinks with friends, and remarked that the festival offers a much wider variety of wines at far more affordable prices compared to the Mainland.

Exhibitors have travelled from around 30 countries and regions, and the festival boasts new pavilions showcasing Australia, Canada and Korea.

After attending the event in previous years, one Korean exhibitor described having her own booth at the festival as a dream come true. Highlighting that Hong Kong is open to foreign markets - helping to bring international attention to products such as sake and French wine, for example – she hopes to make the most of the opportunity to promote Korean drinks.

Aside from beverages, of course, the event also offers an array of delicious food.

One local third-time exhibitor is offering a bold twist on Hong Kong’s iconic egg waffles, infusing these with 50-year-aged dried tangerine peel and Pu’er tea and promoting the delicacy as an exclusive "Only in Hong Kong" festival highlight. After visitors queued for hours last year, the booth's on-site cooking equipment has been doubled this time around, with the exhibitor anticipating a 20% surge in revenue.

The festival runs until 1am tonight and until midnight tomorrow night. Admission is $40, and tasting tokens can be purchased on-site to sample the wine and food.

articles.title: Amid fuel tax cut, German inflation slows
articles.excerpt: German inflation slowed more than expected in October, the first month of a government fuel tax cut, adding to evidence…
articles.fullText:
German inflation slowed more than expected in October, the first month of a government fuel tax cut, adding to evidence that Europe's largest economy could prove more resilient than anticipated despite disruptions linked to the war in Iran.

Gross domestic product increased slightly more than expected in the third quarter, though economists warned the expansion remained heavily reliant on government spending.

Inflation eased to 2.8 percent year-on-year in October from 3.3 percent the month before, preliminary data from the statistics office showed on Friday, below forecasts for 3.1 percent.

Easing energy price rises drove the slowdown, increasing by 12.2 percent in October versus 14.9 percent the month before, and indicated that the fuel tax cut that runs to year-end is having an effect.

Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, fell to 2.1 percent from 2.4 percent the month before.

The German data comes ahead of a euro zone inflation update due on Wednesday. Inflation in the bloc is expected to come in at 3.9 percent in October, slightly above September's 3.8 percent, according to economists polled by Reuters.

German GDP increased by 0.2 percent in the third quarter compared with the previous three-month period, according to preliminary data from the statistics office, slightly above a rise of 0.1 percent forecast by analysts polled by Reuters.

The data pointed to a fourth straight quarter of recovery in Europe's largest economy, helped by increased public spending, even as private sector momentum remained subdued.

Under Chancellor Friedrich Merz, government funding has surged since Berlin last year approved a €500 billion infrastructure fund and exempted much defence spending from its debt brake rules.

The economy grew by 0.3 percent in the second quarter and 0.4 percent in the first quarter, according to the office.

The fuel tax cut, which aims to cushion households from the surge in oil prices caused by the Iran war, will likely help the economy hold up in the fourth quarter as well, said Deutsche Bank analyst Marc Schattenberg.

However, with no sign of a lasting de-escalation in the Middle East, energy prices are unlikely to drop noticeably and will continue to stoke inflation in coming months, say analysts.

"It is clear that the inflation rate will hover around 3 percent for some time to come," said Alexander Krueger, chief economist at Bethmann HAL bank.

"Given this backdrop, an interest rate hike by the ECB cannot be ruled out."

The European Central Bank left interest rates unchanged on Thursday but clearly hinted at another hike in December.

While analysts broadly agree Germany is emerging from a prolonged slowdown, many stop short of calling the recovery self-sustaining because private investment remains weak.

A lack of sweeping reforms means Germany's attractiveness as a place to do business will remain impaired, preventing a significant recovery in private investment, Commerzbank chief economist Joerg Kraemer said.

Analysts pointed to the increased government spending on infrastructure and defence as the main driver of the recovery.

"Without this artificially initiated impulse, economic output would probably have stagnated," said Krueger.

Jens-Oliver Niklasch, economist at LBBW bank, said that next year would reveal whether the economic revival is sustainable or just a flash in the pan.

"For sustained, higher growth, investment would need to pick up more substantially, which, to date, has not been the case," he said.

The German government expects the economy to grow by 1.3 percent in 2026 and 1.1 percent in 2027, with the economy ministry saying earlier this month that the Iran war, and resulting high energy prices, is not hurting the economy as much as feared.

In a further positive sign, the Ifo economic institute's closely watched business climate index rose for a sixth straight month in October. (Reuters)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: US woman blames 'incompetence' for failed execution
articles.excerpt: Christa Pike said on Friday that she remains in constant pain and struggles to speak a month after surviving a…
articles.fullText:
Christa Pike said on Friday that she remains in constant pain and struggles to speak a month after surviving a lethal injection in the US state of Tennessee, a failure she blames on “incompetence”.

In her first public statement since the failed execution, Pike said she never contemplated a life beyond her execution date and was prepared to die in peace, but woke up alone and confused in a hospital bed.

“There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul,” Pike said.

Pike, 50, survived two doses of pentobarbital as the state tried to execute her on September 30 for the 1995 stabbing death of 19-year-old classmate Colleen Slemmer.

Pike was 18 when she and her boyfriend tortured and killed Slemmer, becoming one of the youngest women to be sentenced to death.

“I’m deeply hurt by the incompetence that has put so many people in this terrible position,” she said. “I continue to think about my victim’s family and the terrible pain and loss they have endured.”

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has called for an investigation into what happened during the failed execution and postponed the state’s other lethal injection scheduled this year.

Pike said she's thankful for the medical workers who saved her life and the people who showed her kindness.

“I don’t know why I survived that night. I don’t know what comes next. Some days, finding hope is harder than others. For now, I am trying to heal, one day at a time. And I am holding on to the love and kindness of so many people who have reminded me that I am not alone,” she said.

Pike’s attorneys have urged the governor to reduce her sentence to life imprisonment.

Lee told reporters this week that, “I suspect her sentence will be the same as before unless determined otherwise by the courts.”

Friday's statement was dictated to Pike's legal team from the infirmary at the prison where she is housed.

Pike was hospitalised in the immediate aftermath of the failed execution and then moved back to prison at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center. (AP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta shutting down
articles.excerpt: The Russian independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta said on Friday that it was winding up its remaining operations after a campaign…
articles.fullText:
The Russian independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta said on Friday that it was winding up its remaining operations after a campaign of state pressure in which a senior editor has been prosecuted and its financial support and premises have been taken away.

"We have been killed," the publication, set up with money from the Nobel Peace Prize of the last Soviet leader, Mikhail Gorbachev, said in a statement.

The paper halted its print edition inside Russia in 2022, but had continued to produce online content and operate from its office in central Moscow.

"On November 9, we will turn off the lights in the home where we have lived for 30 years, shut down our servers, and leave," it said.

"The newspaper no longer exists. The Russian authorities and the Russian security services have forced our editorial team to cease its operations."

There was no immediate comment from the authorities, which had designated the publication a "foreign agent".

But the Kremlin – which accuses foreign intelligence services of trying to stir up discontent inside Russian society – has said in the past that some censorship is necessary at a time when Russia is locked in what it describes as an existential struggle with the West over Ukraine.

The prominent war blogger Rybar offered a taste of how the publication is seen in some official circles, reposting a diatribe that accused Novaya Gazeta of systematically promoting an anti-Russian narrative and of relishing the difficulties faced by the Russian state.

Founded in 1993 in line with Gorbachev's vision of "glasnost" or openness, Novaya Gazeta ("New Newspaper") became one of Russia's most influential newspapers and defenders of democracy with its investigations into corruption and critical coverage of Russian politics.

Dmitry Muratov, its co-founder and long-time editor-in-chief, shared the 2021 Nobel Peace Prize, dedicating it to six colleagues who had been killed because of their work, including the investigative journalist Anna Politkovskaya, who wrote about Moscow's wars in the restive Chechnya region.

Like other media outlets not run by the state but critical of it, Novaya Gazeta came under increasing pressure after Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in 2022.

Sweeping censorship rules were introduced that mandated long jail terms for "discrediting" the Russian army or disseminating what the authorities deem to be fake news.

"Since the start of the 'special military operation' in Ukraine and the introduction of criminal charges for 'discrediting the Russian army', we cannot report on the most critical and tragic events of our time," the newspaper said. "Censorship applies to virtually every sphere of civic life."

Many of its own journalists and those from other outlets had fled Russia in 2022, it added.

Some of its former employees began a separate Latvian-based print and online publication called Novaya Gazeta Europe, which the Moscow authorities designated an "undesirable organisation", effectively banning it within Russia. It will continue to operate. (Reuters)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: HK$160k worth of sculptures stolen from City Hall
articles.excerpt: Police said a batch of sculptures was believed to be stolen from the City Hall in Central ahead of the…
articles.fullText:
Police said a batch of sculptures was believed to be stolen from the City Hall in Central ahead of the opening of an arts festival there.

Officers said they were alerted at around 2.30pm that the sculptures worth about HK$160,000 went missing.

The case has been classified as theft.

The Central district's criminal investigation team is following up on the case.

The opening of the Microwave International New Media Arts Festival was scheduled for Friday evening.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Xi welcomes visiting German, Swiss presidents
articles.excerpt: China has always viewed the European Union as a partner and is committed to developing China-EU relations with sincerity and…
articles.fullText:
China has always viewed the European Union as a partner and is committed to developing China-EU relations with sincerity and goodwill, President Xi Jinping told German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier during talks in Beijing on Friday.

History and reality have repeatedly shown that for China and the EU, cooperation outweighs competition and consensus outweighs differences, Xi said.

He added that as long as both China and the EU stay committed to the positioning of their partnership and maintain the tone of equal-footed dialogue, differences and problems can be resolved and will not hinder further development of China-EU relations.

Xi also said China's policy towards Germany is consistent, stable and predictable, and Beijing is happy to see Berlin play a greater role in European and international affairs.

Also on Friday, the president met with his Swiss counterpart Guy Parmelin in Beijing as the two countries signed a protocol on upgrading their free trade agreement.

The deal removes tariffs on almost all Swiss exports to the world's second-largest economy.

It grants 99.8 percent of Swiss exports duty-free access to the Chinese market over the next 10 years, up from around half of Swiss shipments previously.

Duties will be eliminated on all imports of Swiss watches, of which only one percent were previously tariff-free, though producers will still have to pay China's luxury consumption tax.

Swiss cheese and coffee, among other exports, will also see duties removed, bringing them in line with products such as chocolate and wine, which were already tariff-free.

The update also grants Switzerland greater access to the Chinese market in areas including manufacturing-related services, aircraft maintenance and maritime transport.

In exchange, it removes tariffs on 97.3 percent of Chinese agricultural exports to Switzerland, up from 80.1 percent prior.

"Together, we can inject valuable confidence and greater certainty into China-Europe economic and trade cooperation," Xi told Parmelin.

The upgraded trade agreement bucks a broader global shift towards ​protectionism. Observers are eyeing the Swiss deal as a potential litmus test between Beijing and other European economies. (Xinhua and agencies)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: The Download: GLP-1s and eating disorders, self-aware cities, and forever chemicals
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in…
articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse.

GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are one of the biggest biotech breakthroughs of the last decade. But to some clinicians, they can represent something sinister—a potential trigger for eating disorders.

A new report suggests the global incidence of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa shot up by 71% between 1990 and 2023. And clinicians are already seeing GLP-1s exacerbate the issue.

Here’s how they could make an already growing problem worse .

—Jessica Hamzelou

This story is from The Checkup, our weekly biotech newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Thursday.

Love is infrastructure

—“Love is Infrastructure” is a short fictional story by Charlie Jane Anders, author of a forthcoming novel titled Good Things Are Coming Your Way .

Mainspring and St. Barnabas are two neighboring cities with different personalities. They’ve never particularly liked each other, but that changes when both develop minds of their own, shaped by the votes of their residents.

As the cities begin to fall for each other, a third city enters the picture. Turnbull promises Mainspring a more efficient future, but its vision of urban life comes with a troubling price.

Read the full short story about self-aware cities, direct democracy, and a steamy romance.

This story is from the latest edition of our print magazine . Subscribe now to get every issue as soon as it lands.

Are we there yet? Cleaning up PFAS

Used for decades in everything from nonstick pans to firefighting foams, PFAS, or “forever chemicals,” are linked to increased risks of fertility challenges, developmental delays, cancer, and reduced immune response.

Scrubbing PFAS-contaminated soil could eliminate a list of woes for people and planet. The concept is still in its infancy, but we can limit their buildup by pulling the chemicals out of water systems.

Find out how close we are to ridding the world of forever chemicals .

—Sara Kiley Watson

This story is part of “Are we there yet?” , our series that takes stock of six technologies that have long promised to change the world—and scores them on a progress meter. We’re exploring each one in The Download, so stay tuned, and subscribe to read the rest of the stories in our new Impossible issue .

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 Binance has suffered the biggest crypto hack in history
The exchange says $6.3 billion in assets were affected. ( BBC )
+ Analysts blamed the hack on North Korea. ( Guardian )
+ The Bitcoin stolen will likely never be recovered. ( Bloomberg $)
+ Binance has suspended all deposits and withdrawals. ( NBC News )
+ How a pastor’s crypto scheme lost investors millions. ( MIT Technology Review )

2 Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was targeted by an alleged Chinese spy
The suspect is an executive at a Singapore data center firm. ( NYT $)
+ US intelligence believes she cultivated ties with Huang. ( Guardian )
+ Her company was investigated over alleged chip diversion. ( CNBC )
+ Nvidia says their dealings were “normal.” ( Bloomberg $)

3 Alphabet just shed $500 billion in market value
The record loss is due to AI taking a bite out of its search profits. ( CNBC )
+ Amazon and Intel further a further fall in tech stocks. ( Bloomberg $)
+ Hyperscalers are making a trillion-dollar gamble. ( MIT Technology Review )

4 The Pentagon suspects freezers at military bases were hacked
The malfunctions spoiled food. ( Reuters $)
+ They may be linked to similar hacks in French supermarkets . ( Gizmodo )

5 The US midterms could reshape the future of American science
A Democratic Congress could curb Trump’s science cuts. ( Nature )
+ Trump has already dealt big blows to science. ( MIT Technology Review )

6 Data centers are set to send US climate pollution skyrocketing
Gas plants could push power-sector emissions up 42% by 2030.( Verge )
+ Europe’s data centre workers face dangerous conditions. ( Guardian )

7 SpaceX is pulling away from NASA
The company is prioritising Starlink and AI. ( Ars Technica )
+ But Cape Canaveral is busier than during the space race. ( Axios )

8 Battery makers are finding a new market in the US
They’re pivoting from EVs to grid storage. ( WSJ $)
+ Batteries just broke another record in the US.  ( MIT Technology Review )

9 A humanist has received a religious exemption from using AI at work
He argued that using it undermined human flourishing. ( Gizmodo )

10 Psychics are fighting back against computerized clairvoyance
Human practitioners say chatbots lack the divine touch. ( Guardian )

Quote of the day

“Rizz is in more and more demand because it’s something that only people have.”

—Steven Strogatz, a mathematics professor at Cornell University, tells Business Insider that personal appeal will become more valuable as AI increasingly takes over intellectual work.

One more thing

The Bay Area’s animal welfare movement wants to recruit AI

In early February, animal welfare advocates and AI researchers arrived in stocking feet at Mox, a shoes-free coworking space in San Francisco. They gathered to discuss a provocative idea: if artificial general intelligence is on the horizon, could it prevent animal suffering?

Some brainstormed using custom agents in advocacy work, while others pitched cultivating meat with AI tools. But the real talk of the event was a flood of funding they expect will soon flow to animal welfare charities, not from individual megadonors, but from AI lab employees.

Some attendees also probed an even more controversial idea: AI may develop the capacity to suffer, which could constitute a moral catastrophe. We investigated why their ideas are gaining momentum—and sparking controversy.

—Michelle Kim & Grace Huckins

We can still have nice things

A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. Today, it’s a Halloween special. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line .)

+ Meet the “Picasso of Pumpkin Carvers” , bringing artistry to a Halloween tradition.
+ Mashup maestro Bill McClintock’s Ghostmashers is the ideal soundtrack for your All Hallows’ Eve party.

articles.title: Race to make bid-rigging criminal offence by April
articles.excerpt: Officials said on Friday they aim to criminalise bid-rigging by April as well as enhance enforcement through the establishment of…
articles.fullText:
Officials said on Friday they aim to criminalise bid-rigging by April as well as enhance enforcement through the establishment of an inter-departmental task force.

Competition Commission chief executive Rasul Butt said the watchdog would be consulting lawmakers over the proposed amendments “very soon” before seeking opinions from stakeholders.

“The government and, of course, the relevant authorities like the Competition Commission... will need to engage with some stakeholders,” he said.

“In terms of going to Legco to seek Legco's approval to pass the new amendments, the aim right now is April next year.”

The task force – comprised of representatives from the commission, the police force and the Independent Commission Against Corruption – will be led by Secretary for Security Chris Tang.

Tang said the fight against bid-rigging, currently only a civil offence, would be efficient and enhanced through the sharing of intelligence and databases by the task force.

“In fact in the past, our three different departments, namely police, ICAC and Competition Commission, we are all separately, vigorously investigating bid-rigging-related offences,” he said.

“But now we have a joint task force – we can share our intelligence, we can conduct more precise joint operations, and we can have more proactive elements in cracking bid-rigging activities.”

While Tang did not reveal how many members there would be in the task force, he stressed that setting it up would not require any additional resources.

He noted that under the coordination of the Home Affairs Department, task force members would attend owners' corporations meetings at high-risk buildings – meaning those with high project costs and a significant number of flats involved – to look for indications that bid-rigging might be involved.

Tang said the task force will also rely on intelligence, undercover operations and informers to crack down on malpractices.

Edited by Edmond Fong

Blue-chip shares on the mainland closed lower on Friday and booked their steepest monthly loss since early 2016, as a global selloff in AI stocks weighed on sentiment.

In Hong Kong, however, the benchmark Hang Seng Index ended 335 points, or 1.5 percent, higher for the day at 23,294 on turnover of HK$214.32 billion and was 0.9 percent up for the week.

The tech index rose 10 points, or 0.3 percent, to 3,754, although the gauge still hovered near its lowest in two years.

"At valuations of 10-11 times price-to-earnings after accounting for new AI investment, we think some stocks are increasingly treating the spending peak as a permanent earnings burden, while assigning limited value to a normalisation of future cash flows or successful AI monetisation," said Kenneth Fong, head of China internet research at UBS.

Financials led gains, up 1.3 percent, while mainland property developers rose 2.8 percent.

The China enterprises index put on 106 points, or 1.4 percent, to end at 7,862.

Across the border, the Shanghai Composite Index lost 52 points, or 1.44 percent, to close at 3,599 on turnover of 764.22 billion yuan while the blue-chip CSI300 Index fell 1.4 percent to close near a one-year low.

The CSI300 Index was down 8.5 percent for the month, its biggest monthly loss in more than a decade.

Over the last 12 weeks, it has lost 15 percent, the longest losing streak on record.

The Shenzhen Component Index fell 304 points, or 2.73 percent, to 10,833 on turnover of 910.23 billion yuan while the ChiNext Index plunged 103 points, or 4.13 percent, to 2,413 on turnover of 452.21 billion yuan.

AI-related shares led declines after a selloff in US technology stocks reignited concerns about the returns on heavy AI spending.

Shares in Google parent Alphabet, Amazon.com and Intel all fell on AI cash burn.

Memory chip giant SK Hynix fell more than seven percent.

CSI 5G communications, a gauge that measures the industry, slumped 6.2 percent.

Shares of Chinese optical module producer Eoptolink Tech tumbled 14 percent and were down 50 percent this month.

Against broad declines, consumer staple shares rose two percent as investors rotated into less risky sectors.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei fell 1,369 points, or 2.12 percent, to close at 63,290 for the day, led lower by chip-equipment heavyweights Advantest and Tokyo Electron.

For the week, the benchmark managed to gain one percent.

The broader Topix was down a milder one percent on Friday but flat for the week.

In Seoul, the Kospi closed down 206 points, or 3.48 percent, at 5,730 for the day and 16.2 percent for the month, after diving up to 5.7 percent earlier and triggering a sidecar trading curb. (Reuters/Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse.
articles.excerpt: GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are one of the biggest biotech breakthroughs of the last decade. But to some clinical psychologists, they…
articles.fullText:
GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are one of the biggest biotech breakthroughs of the last decade. But to some clinical psychologists, they can represent something more sinister—a potential trigger for eating disorders.

A new report suggests that the global incidence of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa shot up between 1990 and 2023—by a whopping 71%. By 2023, there were an estimated 18.1 million people living with one of these two disorders.

What’s worse is that the number is likely to be much higher than that once we factor in other eating disorders. And, disturbingly, those in the field are already starting to see GLP-1 weight-loss drugs exacerbating the issue.

Cheri Levinson is a clinical psychologist at the University of Louisville in Kentucky who has specialized in eating disorders for almost 20 years. She says she’s now seeing more patients with more severe symptoms than at any other time in her career, and that many of them are misusing GLP-1s. “This is the worst I’ve seen things,” she says.

Eating disorders are mental health conditions in which people’s eating behaviors impact their health. They include anorexia nervosa (defined by a fear of weight gain), bulimia nervosa (in which people binge and purge), binge eating disorder, and others.

It’s thought that some people have a genetic predisposition to certain eating disorders, but that some external factor is what triggers their onset. That might be stress, or social pressure to be skinny. Often, simply restricting food intake can trigger an eating disorder, says Levinson.

Eating disorders—along with the pressure to look thin—were already prevalent in the 1990s (the heroin chic era springs to mind). To find out how things might have changed since then, Ruhai Bai at the Children’s Hospital of Nanjing Medical University in China and his colleagues pulled together data from studies and surveys conducted on populations around the world. The team used statistical models to fill in any data gaps.

That research allowed the researchers to estimate the annual incidence of two eating disorders—anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa—for each of 204 countries and territories between 1990 and 2023. They also estimated the impact those disorders had on global health by calculating their disability-adjusted life years (one DALY represents a year of healthy life lost).

The findings, published in JAMA Psychiatry on Wednesday, are unsettling. Between 1990 and 2023, there was a 71% increase in the incidence of those two eating disorders, the team found. Those conditions had a huge impact on global health, too. In 2023, they “cost the world the equivalent of about 3.83 million years of healthy life,” says Bai.

Bai and his colleagues expect these figures to continue to rise. In 2023, an estimated 18.1 million people had either anorexia nervosa or bulimia nervosa; by 2050, the team predict, the two conditions could affect 21.8 million people.

It gets worse. Those two conditions represent less than half of all eating disorders, says Levinson, who was not involved in Bai’s study. The true impact of these disorders is “probably three times the rate that they’re reporting,” she says.

Bai and his colleagues didn’t explore the reasons for this rise (although Bai points out that it can’t be entirely explained by population growth). So how did we get here?

Social media may have played a role. “Social media comparisons, influencers, challenges, diet trends can all be precipitating … events for an eating disorder,” says Cynthia Bulik, a clinical psychologist at the University of North Carolina, who was not involved in the new study. Bulik has been studying and treating eating disorders since the early 1980s. “Between 1990 and 2023 there has clearly been an upsurge of those types of environmental exposures,” she says.

Many social media users are exposed to filtered and modified images of skinny influencers who may have undergone cosmetic surgery or extreme dieting and who are promoting “thinspiration” or “fitspiration” content. But users with eating disorders appear to be more likely to engage with this content—and to be fed more of it as a result.

When researchers at the University of Melbourne investigated this phenomenon a couple of years ago, they found that the algorithms of TikTok users with eating disorders delivered 4343% more “toxic eating disorder videos” than those of users who didn’t have the disorders. They also got more content focused on dieting or exercising. Many were fed over 1000 problematic videos per month. Bulik describes social media as “quicksand” for people with, or at risk of, eating disorders.

The covid-19 pandemic—and the social isolation that accompanied lockdowns—also appears to have contributed to the rise in eating disorders. Research conducted in 2021 found that the number of people hospitalized with eating disorders in the US doubled between 2018 and 2020 .

Researchers don’t yet have good data on how trends in eating disorders might have progressed since 2023. But anecdotally, things seem to be getting even worse. “There are more eating disorders, more severe eating disorders… and we’re seeing earlier ages of onset,” says Levinson. “We’re seeing eight- and nine-year-olds with eating disorders.”

“From what I’m hearing and seeing, I am not going to be surprised if that number isn’t at least doubling again,” she adds.

Levinson particularly worries about the impact of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, which have exploded in popularity in recent years. A Gallup survey conducted earlier this year suggested that 15% of Americans had used one of these drugs for weight loss. And they’re becoming more accessible—drug companies are working on new formulations that are both easier to take and more effective, and many people can buy versions of these drugs from compound pharmacies or dubious online sources.

In a small study published earlier this year, Levinson and her colleagues found that 30% of people with eating disorders had used GLP-1 drugs. The drugs might benefit some of those people. But 10% appeared to have misused the drugs. And Levinson thinks that figure is also an underestimate.

Levinson says she and her colleagues have seen children develop eating disorders after being prescribed GLP-1s for medical reasons. They’ve seen others—even children as young as 11—buy versions of these drugs over TikTok.

“We’re very concerned that GLPs will lead to even faster and more extreme weight loss in people with anorexia nervosa, and that patients will come to us in even more advanced stages of illness that become difficult to reverse,” says Bulik.

Both Bulik and Levinson are continuing to study the impacts of these drugs in eating disorders. In the meantime, both urge medical professionals to consider the risks GLP-1s might pose to people with those disorders. Bulik contributed to a set of research and clinical guidelines , published earlier this month, that recommends doctors screen for eating disorders before prescribing the drugs, for example. The guidelines also recommend more patient education and more robust monitoring of people who take GLP-1s.

If you think you or someone you know might have an eating disorder, you can find information and support at the National Eating Disorders Association .

This article first appeared in The Checkup,  MIT Technology Review’s  weekly biotech newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Thursday, and read articles like this first,  sign up here .

The Transport Department has warned that traffic around the Huanggang control point and San Tin Road will be very heavy on Friday night and over the next two nights, as Halloween celebrations and other events in Hong Kong and Kowloon are expected to end around midnight.

In a post on its social media page, the department said the Huanggang checkpoint provides dedicated public transport lanes, allowing franchised buses, cross-boundary coaches and green minibuses to travel via San Sham Road directly to the port.

It said road markings have been strengthened and the dedicated lanes extended to improve effectiveness.

During peak traffic periods, four franchised bus routes heading to the Huanggang port via the San Tin Public Transport Interchange will enter the interchange directly from a junction of the San Tin section of Castle Peak Road helping to divert traffic away from the busy San Tin roundabout.

Its Emergency Transport Co-ordination Centre will monitor traffic conditions around the clock and take appropriate measures as needed, it said.

articles.title: Tip-offs 'helping stub out construction-site smoking'
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Labour and Welfare Chris Sun called on the public on Friday to continue to provide information to help…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Labour and Welfare Chris Sun called on the public on Friday to continue to provide information to help enforce the full smoking ban on construction sites and buildings undergoing major renovations.

The call came as he revealed that citizen tip-offs had led to a disproportionately high number of successful prosecutions since the new rules took effect three months ago.

Sun said the Labour Department has issued 87 fixed-penalty notices since the ban was introduced, of which 27 – about one third – were based on information provided by citizens.

There are currently, he pointed out, four contractor cases involving five summonses going through prosecution proceedings.

The department has conducted more than 6,900 inspections over the past three months, he said, of which about 430 were triggered by complaints or tip-offs.

"The proportion of inspections is certainly not large, but the success rate is very high, because you see, among our fixed-penalty notices, approximately one third of them were issued because some citizens kindly provided us with photos, videos and information, enabling us to conduct inspections promptly," said Sun.

He also apologised again over the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire, whose independent report was released by the government on Thursday.

Sun pointed out that he had to, as a politically appointed official, support the chief executive and be accountable to him.

The chief executive, he said, had made clear his requirements and he would follow them, stay on the job and strive to implement the government's reform agenda.

Edited by Tony Sabine

The Communist Party of China has stressed the need to promote party building in emerging sectors in a resolution adopted at a plenary session of the Central Committee, an official said on Friday.

The party will step up efforts to expand and deepen the coverage of party organisations and work in new types of economic and social organisations, as well as among groups in new forms of employment, so as to strengthen its appeal, cohesiveness and influence in emerging fields, said Huang Jianfa, deputy head of the organisation department of the committee.

New types of economic organisations encompass non-public-sector enterprises and businesses operating in emerging areas and cover a broad range of entities, including industry associations, chambers of commerce, social service agencies and community-based organisations.

New forms of employment have emerged alongside the growth of the internet and digital economy, including workers such as food-delivery couriers, ride-hailing drivers and online marketers, many of whom rely on digital platforms for their work.

articles.title: Crypto platform Binance confirms US$6.3bn hack
articles.excerpt: Hackers stole US$6.3 billion from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what analysts say is the biggest crypto hack…
articles.fullText:
Hackers stole US$6.3 billion from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what analysts say is the biggest crypto hack ever, an attack that could prompt investors to rethink the risks of owning digital assets.

The hackers behind the raid had alleged ties to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis.

The attackers targeted Binance wallets on 10 blockchains and shifted most of the funds in about 20 minutes, TRM Labs said in a statement.

Binance said it worked with partners to freeze the affected assets with about US$3 billion located so far.

It did not mention the status of the remaining US$3.3 billion, and its co-founder Yi He said the exchange would cover "all hacking losses".

Binance said its deposits were unaffected and it expects to resume withdrawal services in the next 48 hours.

TRM said several features of the attack matched earlier heists linked to the DPRK, including a 2025 hack of crypto exchange Bybit that the US Federal Bureau of Investigation had attributed to Pyongyang.

"We make this judgement with high confidence," it said in a statement.

The DPRK’s mission in Geneva and its embassy in China did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

The incident could be the world's biggest crypto heist, according to analytics firm Chainalysis and other industry experts.

"It's the biggest hack in history," said Aravind Srinivasan, head of large crypto market maker GSR's systematic OTC business.

Markets reacted immediately in Asian trading on Friday.

Bitcoin dropped more than three percent to a six-week low of US$76,368 and ether fell more than three percent to a two-month low of US$2,178.

BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down five percent over the past 24 hours at US$709.70, according to market aggregator CoinGecko.

Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global slid 4.8 percent while those of bitcoin buyer Strategy fell nearly six percent in extended US trading.

An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of its engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said.

"The incident stems from multiple factors. Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said.

Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for crypto, which had already been under pressure due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.

"It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges, as well as counterparty, solvency and liquidity risks," said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong Kong.

Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about US$162.8 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange's 2025 annual report.

"User funds remain safe," Binance said in a statement.

Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, which is a reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches, according to its website.

"It's becoming very hard to counter hacks as AI can find vulnerabilities faster than you can fix them," said Bernardo Brites, CEO of Trace Finance, a payments and stablecoin infrastructure company.

"My view is that users will move away from smaller and medium-sized exchanges, (it is) becoming too risky to park your money somewhere that couldn't cover a hack of meaningful size."

Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly US$1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than US$800 million.

World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said on Thursday it had worked with cryptocurrency custodian BitGo to freeze funds stolen in what it described as a Binance hack.

Binance's Yi said US$27 million in stablecoins and about US$2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.

Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly US$200 million in funds, Yi said.

Jack McDonald, senior vice president of stablecoins at Ripple, said the company was closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and was freezing affected funds and coordinating with relevant parties.

The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts.

Last year, attackers stole US$2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs.

In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly US$350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry's vulnerability to hackers.

Authorities have warned that organised crime groups are increasingly using cryptocurrencies to move funds across borders outside the traditional financial system.

Binance.US, a separate cryptocurrency exchange, said it was not affected by the security incident.

Coinbase said it was unaffected and was monitoring the situation. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Major renovations to get dedicated checks by new unit
articles.excerpt: A Housing Bureau unit found to have been primarily responsible for failed supervision of major renovations at Wang Fuk Court…
articles.fullText:
A Housing Bureau unit found to have been primarily responsible for failed supervision of major renovations at Wang Fuk Court in the runup to the fire will be replaced within about a month by a new body, Deputy Financial Secretary Michael Wong said on Friday.

About 300 staff at the bureau's Independent Checking Unit will move over to the new Public Housing Building Control Unit, which will have a project-based workflow.

Making the announcement, Wong, the acting secretary for housing, said under the new workflow system, each major maintenance job would get a dedicated team and a project liaison officer as a one-stop contact for owners’ corporations, instead of splitting inspection, structural checks, minor works and site monitoring across different desks.

A directorate-grade officer, he added, would shortly be seconded from the Buildings Department to the new unit to guide day-to-day work and keep enforcement standards aligned.

"We believe there are several things that will bring a substantial improvement in the quality of our future services," Wong said.

"First, we're changing our basic regulatory model to a project-based approach.

"Also, communication with the Buildings Department – which was originally set at once every 12 months – has recently been changed to once a quarter."

Wong added the authorities would, through training, make relevant personnel more vigilant and give them a deeper understanding of the relevant guidelines.

He said he believes this can help greatly improve the quality of future work.

Edited by Altis Wong

articles.title: New council to take over URA's role in building upkeep
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn on Friday said the government would set up a new council by the end of…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn on Friday said the government would set up a new council by the end of the year to help homeowners through the full cycle of building repairs – offering a paid service to handle tendering and evaluation on their behalf.

Her announcement came after the independent committee investigating the Wang Fuk Court fire called, in its report, for enhanced support services that would be run by a new operator with a clearer, more interventionist mandate.

Speaking a day after the report’s release, Linn said the new Building Maintenance Support and Services Council would be a non-statutory body and take over, in phases, building-upkeep subsidy schemes presently being run by the Urban Renewal Authority (URA).

Unlike the URA's Smart Tender platform, which helps owners solicit bids but does not assess them, the council will arrange for tenders and evaluate them for owners and recommend up to three suitable bids.

Owners using government maintenance subsidies must choose from those recommended bids.

The council will also assign pre-engaged inspection consultants instead of requiring a fresh tender for each inspection, help appoint supervision consultants and contractors, monitor the supervision consultant during works, and give owners independent advice if contractors propose major scope or cost changes.

Linn said the fuller service could cost several thousand dollars per flat, versus the few hundred being charged under the Smart Tender platform.

Commenting on the charges for the fuller service, Linn pointed out that the new council would provide a paid service to help owners meet their duty to inspect and maintain private property.

Owners, she stressed, remain responsible for major repairs and the government is only stepping in because many of them lack the technical know-how.

Linn was also asked whether the council should take responsibility if trouble came up.

"Now that we have a new council recommending the consultants and contractors, it also has a role overseeing their performance. In case the council is being lax in its monitoring duty, then the council will have liability," she said.

"Likewise, if turn of events show that the council has overlooked some important matters when recommending certain consultants or contractors, then I'm sure the council will also have to take on civil liabilities under the service contract they have signed with the owners."

The council is expected to operate on a self-financing basis.

The government has reserved HK$300 million, Linn said, adding that the figure is made up of HK$100 million in seed funding and HK$200 million to ease fees for needy owners.

She said the council's priority would be the around 1,800 maintenance projects already in the Smart Tender system that had yet to appoint a contractor and were waiting for the new service.

At the news conference, Linn was also asked whether she had considered resigning over the fire.

She said she had thought about it but added that the decision was not simply down to her personal preference; as a senior member of the administration, she also had a duty to continue in her job to carry out the chief executive's directions.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Japan keeps rates steady as inflation hits 2pc target
articles.excerpt: The Bank of Japan kept interest rates steady on Friday but declared victory in a nearly 14-year battle to hit…
articles.fullText:
The Bank of Japan kept interest rates steady on Friday but declared victory in a nearly 14-year battle to hit its price target and signalled vigilance against inflationary risks, suggesting scope to hike borrowing costs as soon as December.

With underlying inflation having roughly hit two percent, the central bank must focus on anchoring it around the target, it said, stressing anew that its policy has entered a new, more hawkish phase open to raising rates once every few months.

The pivot aligns the BoJ with its US and European counterparts eyeing near-term rate hikes to battle inflationary risks from the AI boom and the Iran war-induced energy shock.

"Underlying inflation is at a level generally consistent with our price target, and is expected to remain at around that level," it said in a quarterly outlook report.

"Against this backdrop, it will be important to examine the degree to which underlying inflation is anchored around two percent."

At the two-day meeting ending on Friday, the BoJ maintained its policy rate at 1.25 percent in a widely expected move, forgoing a back-to-back hike to spend more time scrutinising the effects of past rate hikes on lending conditions.

Hajime Takata, a hawkish member of the bank's board, dissented over the decision to hold rates, instead proposing unsuccessfully a hike to 1.5 percent.

In a surprise move, the central bank also said it will accelerate the pace of its sales of exchange-traded funds from January to 860 billion yen per year from the current 330 billion yen.

Markets are focusing on governor Kazuo Ueda's post-meeting briefing for clues on the timing and pace of future rate hikes.

In the report, the bank revised up its core consumer inflation forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2028 to 2.6 percent from 2.4 percent projected three months ago.

Declaring victory in hitting its two percent inflation target marks a turning point for the BoJ, which has spent most of its history battling low or negative price growth since gaining legal independence from the government in 1998.

Under former governor Haruhiko Kuroda, the bank deployed massive monetary stimulus in 2013 to pull Japan out of deflation and fire up inflation to the two percent target.

Even after ending its mix of unorthodox easing steps in 2024, the bank has trodden cautiously in raising rates on the view underlying inflation – or price moves excluding one-off factors and driven by domestic demand – remained below target.

With stubbornly high energy costs and rising import prices from a weak yen adding to inflationary pressures, the bank raised rates in September after delivering a hike in June – a shorter interval than the roughly twice-a-year hikes in 2024 and 2025. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: CPC outlines four areas in anti-corruption drive
articles.excerpt: The Communist Party of China (CPC) outlined four areas of focus for combating corruption in a resolution adopted at the…
articles.fullText:
The Communist Party of China (CPC) outlined four areas of focus for combating corruption in a resolution adopted at the fifth plenary session of the CPC Central Committee, a senior anti-graft official said on Friday.

The four areas are maintaining a tough stance against corruption, strengthening checks on and oversight over the exercise of power, fortifying the cultural-ethical foundations for championing integrity and disdaining corruption, and enhancing coordinated efforts to prevent corruption by rooting out audacity, opportunity, and desire.

"Conducts and discipline problems are long-term recurrent and stubborn, persistent efforts are needed to tackle them," said Zhang Fuhai, deputy secretary of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection of the CPC and deputy head of the National Commission of Supervision.

He made the remarks at a press conference on the guiding principles from the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the CPC in Beijing.

Since the 18th National Congress of the CPC in 2012, discipline inspection and supervisory organs across the country have filed 8.105 million cases and punished 7.922 million people, including 963 officials registered at and supervised by the CPC Central Committee, according to Zhang.

"We will intensify anti-corruption efforts in areas with a high concentration of power funds and resources focus on corruption that involves both political and economic elements collusion between officials and business people, and capital infiltrating into the political realm dig deep into new and disguised manifestations of corruption and tackle on a regular basis misconduct and corruption that occurs at people's doorsteps," he said.

The plenum, which concluded on Thursday in Beijing, adopted the Resolution of the Central Committee of the CPC on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance. (Additional reporting from Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Investment firm PAG buys 51pc of Evergrande unit
articles.excerpt: Asia-focused investment firm PAG will acquire a 51 percent stake in Evergrande Property Services Group, a unit of debt-laden developer…
articles.fullText:
Asia-focused investment firm PAG will acquire a 51 percent stake in Evergrande Property Services Group, a unit of debt-laden developer China Evergrande Group, for HK$4.03 billion, the two said in a joint announcement on Friday.

The acquisition marks a major step in liquidators' efforts to sell assets and recover funds for creditors of China Evergrande, which received a combined US$46 billion in creditor claims.

The sale follows a competitive auction run by the liquidators, according to the filed announcement.

PAG said in the filing that Evergrande Property's business generated stable, recurring revenue from a diversified portfolio of managed properties across China.

PAG said taking control of the listed services unit would remove uncertainty tied to the liquidation of China Evergrande and CEG Holdings, and could strengthen market confidence.

PAG will fund the acquisition and the offer, if fully accepted, with acquisition financing and equity committed by PAG Fund IV, the filing said.

The offer values the 5.52 billion shares at HK$0.8359 each, a 29 percent discount to Evergrande Property's last closing price on Wednesday.

The stock was suspended on Thursday pending the announcement and dropped 13.5 percent after trading resumed on Friday.

The offer values Evergrande Property Services at about HK$9.04 billion, compared to a market capitalisation of roughly HK$11.08 billion after the shares dropped to HK$1.025.

PAG will also pay 500 million yuan at completion for certain taxes, transaction fees and other liabilities of CEG Holdings, according to the filing.

Following completion of the deal, PAG will be required to make an unconditional offer for the remaining 5.3 billion shares in the company.
