Goldman Sachs is advising PAG on the acquisition and potential mandatory offer, while UBS and Citic Securities are joint financial advisers to China Evergrande and CEG Holdings.

The deal remains subject to Chinese antitrust approval, among other conditions.

The parties can terminate the agreement if these conditions are not met or waived by February 12, 2027, according to the filing.

China Evergrande, once China's premier property developer, defaulted on most of its US$300 billion in liabilities following Beijing's sweeping crackdown on the property sector six years ago.

The liquidators of China Evergrande and CEG Holdings informed Evergrande Property a year ago that they were seeking to sell the 51.016 percent stake, according to the filing.

PAG intends to keep Evergrande Property listed in Hong Kong and does not plan major changes to its operations or workforce, apart from nominating new directors at the earliest time permitted under takeover.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK stocks up amid fears over returns from AI build-out
articles.excerpt: Tech shares slumped in Asia on Friday, the yen rose and bonds surged towards their biggest monthly gain in nearly…
articles.fullText:
Tech shares slumped in Asia on Friday, the yen rose and bonds surged towards their biggest monthly gain in nearly three years as investors scurried to safety against worries that huge and rising AI spending may not deliver sufficient returns.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened up 52 points, or 0.23 percent, at 23,011.

The China enterprises index rose 23 points, or 0.31 percent, to 7,779 while the tech index fell 23 points, or 0.63 percent, to 3,720.

Up north, the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index opened down 45 points, or 1.25 percent, at 3,605.

The blue-chip CSI300 headed for its largest monthly fall in a decade, after nearly four months of AI stocks tanking on fears that a slowdown in demand for chips and other data centre equipment could crush revenues.

The Shenzhen Component Index fell 267 points, or 2.4 percent, to 10,871 while the ChiNext Index plunged 3.29 percent to 2,434.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 315 points, or 0.49 percent, down at 64,344 and was 1,742 points lower at one stage before noon as the tech-heavy 225 benchmark tracked overnight losses on Wall Street and was given additional impetus by late earnings from Amazon.com and Intel that showed massive cash burns.

In Seoul, the Kospi dived 177 points, or 2.99 percent, to open at 5,760 before continuing its downward spiral to be 313 points down at one stage before noon, triggering at one point a sidecar trading curb and halting algorithmic trading for five minutes.

The weakness in Asian markets came as shares in Google parent Alphabet fell 12.6 percent on Wall Street and slid a little further after hours, to wipe out a withering US$500 billion in market value, as massive AI spending turned the company's cash flow negative.

An aftermarket plunge of 23 percent in Intel shares and a drop of seven percent in Amazon stocks, as they too burn through cash, drove Nasdaq 100 futures down 1.4 percent and sent stocks of chipmakers around Asia into a tailspin.

"The market isn't necessarily questioning whether the AI buildout can be financed," said Pepperstone analyst Chris Weston.

"It's increasingly questioning whether shareholders will earn an adequate return on the enormous capital being deployed."

Nerves were also frayed by a potentially record-breaking hack at Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, which drove down bitcoin, other cryptocurrency prices and stocks including rival exchange Coinbase.

Investors' rush into bonds was further spurred further by the Federal Reserve's Wednesday decision to keep US interest rates on hold, with no firm projection of when it might need to hike next.

Benchmark 10-year US Treasury yields fell by more than seven basis points in Tokyo trade on Friday to 4.91 percent for a fall of some 37 bps through October – the largest one-month drop since December 2023.

The risk-averse mood strengthened haven currencies such as the yen, pushing the currency up about 0.2 percent to 157.47 per US dollar. (Reuters/Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Netanyahu ahead after elections but short of majority
articles.excerpt: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp finished ahead of the opposition, but remained well short of a majority, final results…
articles.fullText:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp finished ahead of the opposition, but remained well short of a majority, final results from Israel's general election showed on Friday, setting the stage for tough coalition talks or potentially another vote.

Netanyahu's coalition of right-wing and far-right parties won 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats, with his Likud Party remaining the largest faction with 27 seats.

The opposition bloc, led by centrist Gadi Eisenkot, secured 48 seats.

The results from the Central Elections Committee also cemented the emergence as potential kingmakers of the Arab party groupings Raam and the Joint List, with the two winning a combined 19 seats.

The fragmented outcome sets the stage for difficult negotiations to form a government that could last weeks, with no single bloc able to reach the 61-seat threshold needed and the prospect of another election remaining if talks fail.

The final tally came after Netanyahu's camp spent Thursday amplifying unproven allegations that Arab-Israeli groups received foreign funding to influence the vote, accusations rejected by both Arab-majority lists and Qatar.

Israel's Shin Bet domestic security service said it was investigating suspected irregularities, but stressed the probe was not intended to "cast aspersions or place blame on an entire sector that went out to vote in a democratic and lawful manner".

The electoral commission also sought to calm tensions, with its acting director general Dean Livne saying any suggestion of widespread issues was "entirely groundless".

The controversy centred on allegations that Raam received money from Qatar, the energy-rich Gulf powerbroker that has channels to Hamas, to finance vote-buying operations.

"The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel's elections have been stolen!" Netanyahu's Likud Party said on Thursday.

Raam leader Mansour Abbas denied any wrongdoing and welcomed an investigation, while the Joint List accused Netanyahu and his allies of conducting a "campaign of incitement" out of fear of Arab voters' growing political influence.

Eisenkot said: "It's already clear that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on a coordinated, organised campaign seeking to delegitimise the results of the election." (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: 'Wang Fuk recommendations will be carried out swiftly'
articles.excerpt: Most of the 120 recommendations from the independent committee report on the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire could be implemented…
articles.fullText:
Most of the 120 recommendations from the independent committee report on the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire could be implemented within a few months, Chief Secretary Eric Chan said on Friday.

"To implement the 120 recommendations as soon as possible, I believe, will help to quickly reduce the possibility of similar problems occurring again in the future. This is very important," he said during an RTHK programme.

Chan said the recommendations are very comprehensive and the government must draw lessons from the incident to reform and improve existing systems.

The chief secretary will lead a steering committee to review each of the 120 proposals, and drive and monitor the implementation of measures.

Chan said the committee would meet soon and assign each recommendation to the relevant departments.

Where a recommendation involves multiple departments, he said, the lead department responsible for overseeing implementation would be identified.

Each department would be required to submit a report to him on how the recommendation would be implemented or improved, and he would oversee the timeline for implementation.

"There are several principles. First, it must be done very rigorously; second, it must be done very promptly; third, it must be effective — effectively achieving the goal," he said.

The chief secretary said some recommendations are already being rolled out.

He expressed hope that six bills, including amendments to the Fire Services Ordinance and the Competition Ordinance, could be submitted to the Legislative Council within the year.

Once enacted, he said, these laws would give enforcement and regulatory bodies sufficient powers to carry out their work.

On the proposal to set up a central database to share information, such as underperforming contractors, among government departments, Chan said preparation work may take a few months due to the need for data conversion and platform design.

He expects the system could be initially launched around May or June next year, and that the government would then be able to better serve the public.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Four tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz: Iran
articles.excerpt: Four tankers caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to navigate the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's armed forces said —…
articles.fullText:
Four tankers caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to navigate the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's armed forces said — a day after the US military said it cleared key routes through the waterway.

"Over the past 24 hours, three violating oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking mines while attempting to pass through the unauthorised southern route of the Strait of Hormuz," Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps said in a statement.

Later on Thursday, Iran's army reported that another tanker had caught fire east of the strait, after hitting mines while "operating in a restricted and dangerous area".

The initial three vessels had "switched off all their radar and navigation systems" and disregarded warnings from the IRGC navy, the statement said.

It was not immediately clear when the incidents occurred or which flags the tankers were flying.

In recent weeks, Iran has reported multiple vessels striking sea mines, prompting US Central Command (Centcom), which runs military operations in the region, to reaffirm on social media its insistence that all mines in "primary transit routes" have been cleared.

On Thursday, Hossein Mohebi, the spokesman for the IRGC challenged the claim, saying on X: "Prove your Hormuz mine-clearing claim with independent evidence, not statements!"

Since the outbreak of the war on February 28, Iran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

The United States has in response imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait.

On Sunday Centcom said it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.

In their statement on Thursday, the Guards said "the unauthorised route through the Strait of Hormuz is mined, and that vessel owners and crews are responsible for transiting these routes and should not pay attention to Centcom's delusions on social media". (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Australian mushroom killer loses appeal
articles.excerpt: Australian mushroom murderer Erin Patterson lost a bid to overturn her convictions and had a harsher sentence imposed on Friday…
articles.fullText:
Australian mushroom murderer Erin Patterson lost a bid to overturn her convictions and had a harsher sentence imposed on Friday, failing to prove she was wrongfully jailed for killing three people with a poisoned lunch.

Patterson was found guilty last year of murdering her husband's parents and elderly aunt, deliberately lacing their beef Wellington meal with highly toxic death cap mushrooms.

The 52-year-old maintained her triple murder convictions were a "miscarriage of justice", urging the Court of Appeal in Victoria state to either set her free or have the case heard again.

The court found the killings were "carefully planned and deliberate", and there were insufficient grounds to try the case again.

"This offending was extraordinarily cold and calculated," judge Stephen McLeish said.

"It stands to be denounced in the strongest terms."

Patterson has also been convicted of the attempted murder of her husband's uncle, a small-town local pastor who survived after weeks in hospital.

The court not only threw out Patterson's appeal, it also found that her original jail sentence did not match the gravity of her crimes.

Patterson was initially eligible to apply for release after 33 years.

The court ruled that she should not be eligible for parole, meaning Patterson is likely to die in prison.

Patterson did not front the trial in person, instead watching proceedings via video link from a maximum security prison on the outskirts of Melbourne.

Her lawyers had alleged a litany of irregularities in the trial, including an "oppressive" cross-examination and unfair decisions on the admission of evidence.

Prosecutors argued that the non-parole period of 33 years imposed by the judge was "manifestly inadequate".

They said the judge erred in finding there was a substantial chance Patterson would be held in solitary confinement for years to come, and this "infected" his decision on parole.

Patterson's trial last year drew podcasters, film crews and true crime fans to a courthouse in the rural town of Morwell, a sedate hamlet in Victoria better known for its prize-winning roses.

Audiences from New York to New Delhi followed every twist of what many now simply call the "mushroom murders".

The motive of the killings remains a mystery.

A 12-person jury found Patterson guilty in July last year of murdering her husband Simon's parents, Don and Gail Patterson, as well as his aunt, Heather Wilkinson, at her home in the Victorian farming village of Leongatha.

She was also found guilty of attempting to murder Heather's husband Ian, a pastor who fell gravely ill but eventually recovered. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Assets frozen after possible Binance hack
articles.excerpt: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, on Thursday said it had frozen US$3 billion in crypto assets as it investigated…
articles.fullText:
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, on Thursday said it had frozen US$3 billion in crypto assets as it investigated a potential security breach, with stablecoin issuers Circle and Tether freezing related assets.

"Binance will cover all hacking losses," Binance co-founder Yi He said, without providing more details about the incident.

The market impact of the possible hacking, which could be the largest-ever crypto heist according to analytics firm Chainalysis, was felt immediately in early Asian trading on Friday.

Bitcoin dropped about two percent to a six-week low of US$77,646 and ether fell around two percent to a two-month low of US$2,238.76.

BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down more than eight percent over the past 24 hours at US$694, according to market aggregator CoinGecko.

Crypto exchange Coinbase Global slid 4.8 percent while those of bitcoin buyer Strategy fell nearly six percent in extended US trading.

Binance said the amount frozen could increase as it worked with law enforcement agencies, token issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and other industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets.

Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs the company, said in a post on X that the incident "looked like a hack."

Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has more than 335 million registered users globally and had about US$160 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange's 2024 annual report.

Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, according to its website, which is a reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches.

"It's becoming very hard to counter hacks as AI can find vulnerabilities faster than you can fix them, said Bernardo Brites, CEO of Trace Finance, a payments and stablecoin infrastructure company.

"My view is that users will move away from smaller and medium-sized exchanges, (it is) becoming too risky to park your money somewhere that couldn't cover a hack of meaningful size."

Tether said it had frozen nearly US$1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than US$800 million.

Binance said it was conducting security checks and would resume withdrawals once the issue was fully resolved.

It added user funds remained safe and that teams were reviewing the incident.

The exchange also temporarily suspended trading on its Binance Alpha platform as a precaution.

World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said on Thursday it had worked with cryptocurrency custodian BitGo to freeze funds stolen in what it described as a Binance hack.

Binance's Yi said US$27 million in stablecoins and about US$2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.

Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly US$200 million in funds, Yi said.

Jack McDonald, senior vice president of stablecoins at Ripple, said the company was closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and was freezing affected funds and coordinating with relevant parties.

Miguel Morel, CEO of blockchain intelligence firm Arkham, said data indicated that billions of dollars appeared to have been hacked from Binance by an unknown actor, though the exact cause had not been confirmed.

Morel said the incident began around 4.30 pm EDT and appeared to be ongoing.

The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts.

Last year, attackers stole US$2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs.

In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly US$350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry's vulnerability to hackers. (Reuters)
_____________________________
Last updated: 2026-10-30 HKT 09:55

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Djokovic eliminated in Basel in blow to ATP Finals bid
articles.excerpt: Novak Djokovic fell in the second round of the ATP 500 tournament in Basel on Thursday when Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff…
articles.fullText:
Novak Djokovic fell in the second round of the ATP 500 tournament in Basel on Thursday when Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff staged a comeback to win 6-7 (4/7), 7-5, 7-6 (7/5).

The 39-year-old Serb thereby misses valuable points in the race to qualify for the ATP Finals in November.

Struff peppered Djokovic with aggressive serving during a tense 2hr 35min slugfest.

After winning the opening set in a tie-break, with neither player dropping serve, Djokovic faltered on his own serve at 6-5 in the second set, allowing Struff to level the match.

The 24-time Grand Slam winner lost the decisive tie-break in the third set as Struff landed a first career victory over Djokovic after eight previous defeats.

The ATP Finals in Turin in November are reserved for the top eight players in the race rankings, excluding Jannik Sinner, who has withdrawn with a knee injury.

The standings are based on results achieved during the current season.

Seven-time ATP Finals champion Djokovic currently occupies 11th place in the race but can take consolation from the defeat of ninth-ranked Spaniard Rafael Jodar, also eliminated in the second round in Basel by Monaco's Valentin Vacherot.

France's Arthur Fils, seventh in the race, defeated American Alex Michelsen 4-6, 6-3, 7-6 (7/5).

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Russian drone strike kills 14 at Ukraine train station
articles.excerpt: A Russian drone slammed into a busy railway platform in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro on Thursday, killing at least…
articles.fullText:
A Russian drone slammed into a busy railway platform in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro on Thursday, killing at least 14 people in what President Volodymyr Zelensky called a "horrific" attack that demands action by Kyiv's allies.

The strike came as Ukraine and Russia kept to a fragile local ceasefire in the ravaged city of Oleshky – under Russian occupation since 2022 and where residents have faced months of food, water and medicine shortages.

While the truce held into a third day, at least 20 people were killed and more than 70 people injured, according to local officials, in strikes across the country.

The strike on Dnipro station hit a platform "where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing", Zelensky said.

By Thursday afternoon, Dnipropetrovsk regional governor Oleksandr Ganzha said the death toll had risen to 14 with another 14 people wounded, six of them in severe condition with "multiple shrapnel wounds".

One injured was an 11-year-old boy, while one man had "both legs amputated", according to the governor.

Zelensky slammed the attack as "horrific" and insisted that "sanctions against Moscow and its war machine must not be eased for as long as this Russian war continues".

Images released by Ukrainian emergency services showed bodies on the platform, rescuers helping victims and two burnt-out passenger trains with their windows shattered.

French President Emmanuel Macron reacted with outrage to the attack, stressing the need for "far more than a localised ceasefire" like the one in Oleshky.

European Union council president Antonio Costa called for greater pressure on Russia after the latest "cruel and devastating series of Russian strikes against civilians".

"The EU will continue to increase the pressure on Russia and to support Ukraine until a just and lasting peace is achieved," he added.

"We call on all our international partners to do the same."

Ukraine's air force said it intercepted three jet-powered drones in one daytime attack, but that a fourth evaded its defences and hit the station.

After the attack, Zelensky renewed his criticism of a deal struck between US President Donald Trump and Russia's President Vladimir Putin to ease some US sanctions on Russia allowing Moscow to release diesel onto global markets.

"How many such terrorist strikes has Russia carried out against our people since sanctions were lifted on some Russian oligarchs and the energy sector, instead of de-escalating," he asked.

"It is important that America does not remain silent about the killings – this is very important," he added in a separate statement.

At least six other people were killed across Ukraine in separate Russian attacks, according to local officials.

An attack on the city centre of Chernigiv, north of Kyiv, killed two 15-year-old girls and wounded nearly two dozen other people, including four children, the head of the city's military administration, Dmytro Bryzhynsky, said.

A drone slammed into a multi-storey residential building in the central city of Kremenchuk, killing three people and wounding several – including a six-year-old – the local governor said.

Russia has intensified drone and missile attacks in recent weeks, hitting energy sites in what Kyiv says is a bid to plunge the country into cold and darkness throughout the winter.

The Kremlin this week vowed not to let up the overall pace of the war even as the sides prepare to restart stalled talks under US mediation. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: DPRK's Kim calls for drone dominance
articles.excerpt: The Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) has test-fired attack drones, missiles and a multiple rocket launcher at a weapons…
articles.fullText:
The Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) has test-fired attack drones, missiles and a multiple rocket launcher at a weapons demonstration, state media KCNA reported on Friday, as leader Kim Jong Un called for faster development of drone and AI technology for military use.

The event came a day after Seoul said Pyongyang had fired "around a dozen" short-range ballistic missiles off its east coast, though it was not immediately clear whether the launches were linked to the demonstration.

At the event, Kim stressed the "aim to seize the absolute superiority in the drone technology is an indispensable option in the light of the ever-changing patterns of modern warfare," according to KCNA.

He added: "Strength precisely means peace and peace is guaranteed only by strength."

The demonstration featured suicide attack drones, multipurpose drones firing air-to-surface missiles, cruise missiles and 600mm multiple rocket launchers. KCNA said the drones and cruise missiles hit an island target with 100 percent accuracy.

The event follows a slew of recent weapons tests by Pyongyang, including a new precision-guided torpedo system and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile, both of which were said to employ AI technology.

South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said its military detected around a dozen short-range ballistic missiles fired from the Wonsan area of the DPRK towards the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan.

The missiles flew about 250 kilometres, and "South Korea and the United States are conducting a detailed analysis of their exact specifications", Seoul's military said, adding it had stepped up surveillance of possible additional launches.

Seoul's National Security Office, meanwhile, said the launches violated UN Security Council resolutions, labelling them "serious acts that do nothing to help manage the current situation". (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: U.S. to China after demolition report: ‘End interference in Tibetan religious life’
articles.excerpt: Demolition of monks’ quarters aimed at reducing their population and making assimilation easier, sources tell RFA.
articles.fullText:
The U.S. government Thursday urged China to stop interfering with Tibetan religious freedom after sources in eastern Tibet told Radio Free Asia that Chinese authorities began demolishing monks’ quarters at a monastery there.
Authorities on Oct. 25 and 26 began demolishing about 200 monks’ residences at Dza Sershul Thekchen Dargyeling Monastery in Sershul County in the Kardze (Ganzi in Chinese) Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, sources there told RFA, speaking on the condition of anonymity for security reasons.
“Everything is over now,” the source said. “We are losing everything.”
A U.S. State Department spokesperson told RFA on Thursday that the demolitions in Sershul reflect broader Chinese government efforts to bring spiritual institutions, religious education, and monastic life under government control.
“We call on Beijing to end its interference in Tibetan religious life,” the spokesperson said. “Tibetan Buddhists should have the right to practice their faith freely, educate their clergy and choose their religious leaders, including the Dalai Lama and the Panchen Lama, without government interference,” the spokesperson said, referring to Beijing’s past and likely future interference with the established succession customs of the two most important figures in Tibetan Buddhism.
The demolition in Sershul is not isolated, but part of a larger campaign to reduce monk populations at Tibetan religious institutions. RFA reported in August that authorities resumed demolition of the Larung Gar Buddhist Academy. Activists noted the timing – China’s new Ethnic Unity and Progress Law – had just come into effect the previous month.
The law focuses on reshaping ethnic identity, changing the legal framework around language, expanding state oversight of religion, and extending the law’s reach beyond China’s border.
Dza Sershul Thekchen Dargyeling Monastery in an undated photo.
(Citizen photo) The source in Tibet said that authorities are planning further restrictions that would prevent monks from staying at the monastery after the demolitions.
“Tibetan religion and culture are being destroyed,” the source told RFA, adding that there is little recourse for those opposed to the demolitions.
“No matter how much local people speak out, the authorities do not listen,” the source said. “They do not remember, they ignore us. We have no solutions and we don’t know what will happen.”
RFA contacted the relevant county-level officials in Sershul for comment, but the official who answered the phone did not respond to RFA’s questions and hung up.
Promoting “ethnic unity”
The demolitions and reductions of the monk population are clearly intended to assimilate Tibetans so that they accept Chinese identity, Tenzin Lekshay, spokesperson for the Central Tibetan Administration, or CTA, the Tibetan government-in-exile based in Dharamsala, India, told RFA.
“This is a mask used by the Chinese government under the recently enacted Ethnic Unity Law to assimilate Tibetans and destroy Tibetan religion, culture, and language,” he said. “This is not the first time. We have also seen young monks forcibly expelled from monasteries and sent to China’s colonial boarding schools .”
Though Beijing claims the boarding schools are aimed at providing education to a scattered population, critics have noted that their actual goal is assimilation.
“We strongly condemn the Chinese government’s continued attempts to shut down monasteries and schools established by Tibetans while claiming its authority over Tibet and seeking to eradicate Tibetan national identity,” Tenzin Lekshay said. “It is time for the Chinese government to acknowledge and trust that Tibetan religion and culture are beneficial to China and the world and that the destruction of Tibetan religion and culture will have negative consequences for both China and the world.”
He said that the Chinese government’s actions, which violate international law, would undermine Beijing’s ambition to establish itself as a global leader.
The entrance to Dza Sershul Thekchen Dargyeling Monastery in an undated photo.
(Citizen photo) Tibetan monasteries are central to preserving Tibetan culture and religious identity, Sangay Kyab, Chinese liaison officer at the Tibet Bureau, the CTA’s representative office in Geneva, Switzerland, told RFA.
“Tibetan culture and religion are central to the identity of the Tibetan people. China’s policy and goal is to destroy everything that keeps Tibet alive,” he said. “Since China invaded Tibet, there have been successive campaigns against Tibetan monasteries, often under the pretext of reforming them.”
He explained how monks and nuns are subjected to political education aimed at making monasteries conform to the Chinese Communist Party’s ideology.
“The main goal is to restrict the study and practice of Tibetan Buddhism and undermine the Tibetan people’s ability to unite,” he said. “The incident at the monastery is connected to the Chinese government’s broader policies toward Tibet, and there is a risk that similar incidents could occur elsewhere,” he said.
Restrictions in Tibet threaten Tibetan Buddhist heritage, warned the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom, an independent, bipartisan U.S. government commission that monitors religious freedom abroad and makes policy recommendations to the U.S. government.
“Demolition of Tibetan monasteries is just one tactic in a wider effort by Chinese authorities to sever the people of Tibet from their Tibetan Buddhist heritage, including the forced assimilation of ethnic minorities through the draconian ‘Ethnic Unity’ law that came into effect in July,” commission chair Asif Mahmood told RFA.
He cited the resumption of demolition at Larung Gar in Sichuan province in July as another example of restrictions on Tibetan Buddhist religious freedom.
“Buddhist monks in these circumstances have faced persistent threats of harassment, expulsion from their monasteries, imprisonment, and worse,” he said.
China is trying to destroy Tibetan Buddhism at its roots, Bhuchung K. Tsering, head of the Research and Monitoring Unit at the Washington-based International Campaign for Tibet, told RFA.
“Monasteries across Tibet are required to follow the orders of the Chinese Communist Party and serve its objectives,” he said. “The Chinese government claims that Tibetans enjoy freedom of religion, but the reality is the opposite of its claims that it is promoting Tibetan Buddhism,” he added.
Translation and additional reporting by Tenzin Dickyi, edited by Tawang for RFA Tibetan. Edited by Eugene Whong for RFA English.

articles.title: Germany's Zverev becomes tennis World No. 1
articles.excerpt: Alexander Zverev accelerated his ascension to number one in the world rankings for the first time in his career on…
articles.fullText:
Alexander Zverev accelerated his ascension to number one in the world rankings for the first time in his career on Thursday as he beat Tallon Griekspoor 6-4, 7-5 to reach the quarter-finals of the Vienna Open.

The 29-year-old German was already assured of finishing the season top of the ATP rankings but, in the absence of current incumbent Jannik Sinner, two-time Grand Slam champion Zverev will now take that crown in next week's updated standings after winning his opening two matches in the Austrian capital.

Long seen as tennis' nearly-man, Zverev has enjoyed a stellar 2026, breaking his major duck by picking up the titles at the French and US Opens.

Now he has broken further ground by becoming only the 30th man to claim top spot since the rankings were first published in 1973.

He will be aged 29 years and 196 days when Monday's new rankings are published, making him the second-oldest first-time number one after Australian John Newcombe.

Due to a knee injury, Italy's Sinner decided to end his season at the start of October, opening the way for Zverev to dethrone him.

And the big-serving Hamburg native ensured he did just that ahead of the season-ending ATP Finals next month by seeing off Martin Landaluce and Griekspoor in his opening two matches in Vienna.

Zverev needed to save four match points against Spain's Landaluce in his first-round match on Tuesday, but was much more comfortable as he defeated Griekspoor in straight sets to write his name into the history books.

He raced out of the blocks on Thursday, breaking the 30-year-old Dutchman in the very first game and then confidently serving his way into a one-set lead.

The second frame went to 5-5 before Zverev pounced on Griekspoor's serve to get his nose in front.

The match met an unexpected stoppage as Zverev brought up match point when a smash off the German's racquet caused part of the electronic board behind Griekspoor to malfunction.

But once the umpire covered the problematic panel up with a towel, Zverev then sealed his new ranking with an unreturnable serve. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Everton progress to League Cup quarter-finals
articles.excerpt: Everton swept into the League Cup quarter-finals with a 3-1 win against Newcastle on Thursday as they booked a clash…
articles.fullText:
Everton swept into the League Cup quarter-finals with a 3-1 win against Newcastle on Thursday as they booked a clash against giant-killers Fleetwood.

David Moyes's side took the lead through James Garner's first-half goal at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Hayden Hackney doubled the lead with his first goal since his close-season move from Middlesbrough.

Everton striker Thierno Barry netted in the second half and Dan Burn's reply for Newcastle came far too late to stop the Toffees ending their three-match winless run.

Chasing their first League Cup final appearance in 43 years, Everton will travel to fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in the week commencing December 14.

The "Cod Army" caused one of the biggest shocks in League Cup history on Tuesday when they beat Premier League champions Arsenal in a penalty shoot-out after a 1-1 draw at Highbury.

Everton have never won the League Cup, losing their two final appearances in 1977 and 1984.

Everton fans do not need reminding that it is 31 years since the club won the FA Cup in their most recent trophy triumph.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a noted Everton fan, is old enough to remember that success and he was cheering from the stands as Moyes's men made light work of their last-16 tie.

Newcastle will have the chance for revenge when the sides meet again in the Premier League at St James' Park on Monday.

Everton dropped a pre-match bombshell, saying Jack Grealish was unavailable for selection "due to a breach of club discipline".

Grealish, beset by criticism of his behaviour off the pitch, was reported to have taken an unauthorised absence from training.

But the on-loan Manchester City winger's absence was no problem for his team-mates.

Newcastle tested Jordan Pickford early on when Joe Willock's low drive was palmed away by the Everton goalkeeper, who repelled Fabian Schar's long-range strike moments later.

Garner steadied Everton's nerves with a clinical opener in the 34th minute.

Hackney teed up Garner just inside the area and the midfielder stretched to guide a fine finish into the far corner for his first goal since January.

Everton had hit their stride and Hackney struck on the stroke of half-time.

At the climax of a blistering Everton counter-attack, Barry hooked a cross into the six-yard box and Hackney timed his run perfectly to volley past Lukas Hornicek.

Frustrated Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle sent on Joelinton, Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa at the interval.

Wissa had an immediate chance after sprinting onto Willock's pass, but he misjudged the high bounce and ended up heading straight at Pickford.

It was a costly miss as Barry put the result beyond doubt in the 69th minute.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall provided the cross and Barry lashed home from close range for his seventh goal this season.

Burn scored with a header from Willock's 88th-minute cross, sparking a brawl between several players.

But Newcastle's brief show of defiance was too little, too late as Everton moved a step closer to Wembley. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Garcia confirms Liv exit, bids for Ryder Cup return
articles.excerpt: Sergio Garcia will target an 11th Ryder Cup appearance in Ireland next year after he became the latest leading golfer…
articles.fullText:
Sergio Garcia will target an 11th Ryder Cup appearance in Ireland next year after he became the latest leading golfer to confirm he was leaving the struggling Liv Golf circuit.

The breakaway league is attempting to relaunch after filing for bankruptcy protection.

But that has not stopped several players from announcing their intention to return to the established USPGA and European circuits.

European players such as Garcia have also been told signing with the new-look Liv would make them ineligible for European tour membership and so rule them out of the Ryder Cup – the biennial team event against the United States.

Garcia is also the all-time leading points scorer in Ryder Cup history, with the 46-year-old Spaniard having amassed 28.5 points in 10 appearances.

In an X post on Thursday, the 2017 US Masters champion also referenced his conduct at Augusta National this year, where he was issued with a code-of-conduct warning after he broke his driver on the second hole.

"This off-season, I'm working really hard on my game and putting a big focus on a strong mindset and my mental health," said Garcia.

"Next season, I'll be playing on the DP World (European) Tour. This tour has been a huge part of my career from the very beginning, and I'm proud to call it home again.

"I'm also keeping my options open for a return to the PGA Tour."

Garcia added: "I left Augusta last year disappointed with myself and my actions, and I'm ready to show what I've learned and where I am mentally.

"Augusta has given me some of the greatest moments of my life, and I'd love nothing more than to chase another green jacket at such a special place...Another goal is to make that Ryder Cup team and to be an asset to the guys in whatever capacity that may be. In golf, everything is earned and nothing is given. Let's get to work."

Liv's future is uncertain after it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States following the withdrawal of financial support from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, their long-time backers.

Last week, England's Ian Poulter and Tyrrell Hatton both announced they were leaving Liv, even though new lead investor BC Partners Credit has pledged an initial funding commitment of a potential US$300 million to help the circuit relaunch in 2027.

Earlier this month, two-time major champion Jon Rahm reached a separation agreement with Liv.

Rahm was Liv's largest unsecured creditor with US$7.5 million owed when Liv filed for bankruptcy. The 31-year-old Spaniard was thought to have been owed much more after signing a deal worth a reported US$300 million to leave the PGA Tour for Liv in December 2023. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Trump hardens stance on Brazil election 'disgrace'
articles.excerpt: US President Donald Trump on Thursday stepped up criticism of Brazil's "disgraceful" presidential election, declining to say whether he recognised…
articles.fullText:
US President Donald Trump on Thursday stepped up criticism of Brazil's "disgraceful" presidential election, declining to say whether he recognised leftist Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's victory over right-wing ally Flavio Bolsonaro.

Senator Bolsonaro fled to the United States to start a self-imposed exile on Wednesday and insisted that he is his country's rightful leader despite his defeat in the presidential run-off.

"I think the election was a disgrace in Brazil," Trump told reporters when asked if he accepted incumbent Lula's victory, as the US leader headed on a midterms campaign trip.

"I don't want to comment on it right now, but I thought the election was a very great embarrassment to the people of Brazil," Trump added.

"I watched the election. I let it be. I was asked not to take sides by the president, the current president. I didn't take sides, but when I watched what went down in Brazil, it was a disgrace."

Trump pointed to the reaction of the Brazilian stock market, which dropped after Lula's victory, adding: "I thought it was a very disgraceful situation for Brazil."

The US leader's stance appeared to have hardened from as recently as Wednesday, when he said Brazil's election was "very strange" but added that he "won't get involved" in Flavio Bolsonaro's claim to the presidency.

Bolsonaro's defiance on arrival in Florida on Wednesday signalled continued upheaval for Brazil, where Lula won a dramatic run-off election on Sunday.

"I am the elected president, and the criminals who stole Brazil's election are part of a criminal organisation that has established a tyranny," Bolsonaro said in the statement published on his X account, slamming "electoral fraud."

Trump's administration has strong links to Bolsonaro and his hard-right father Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest in Brazil after attempting to overturn his own electoral loss to Lula in 2022.

The US president's reaction has meanwhile sparked speculation about how he will react to a possible Republican loss of Congress in tight US midterm elections that take place next week.

Trump, 80, has ramped up allegations of election fraud, reviving memories of his baseless refusal to accept his 2020 election defeat and the subsequent attack on the US Capitol by his supporters on January 6, 2021.

Details of how Bolsonaro, accompanied by his wife and daughters, made it to US soil are still emerging.

He is under investigation in his home country over alleged corruption and money laundering.

With his current parliamentary immunity about to expire, he was ordered to surrender his passports but left anyway, reaching the United States via Argentina and Ecuador.

The US Department of Homeland Security – which under Trump has led a major campaign against what it calls an immigrant "invasion" from Latin America – said in a statement that the Bolsonaro family members were inspected and cleared "with applicable immigration laws and procedures."

Lula, who won Sunday's election with 51.8 percent of the vote, called Bolsonaro's departure a "shameful" act. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: 'Star Trek', 'X-Men' star Patrick Stewart dead at 86
articles.excerpt: Patrick Stewart, the British Shakespearean actor who became a Hollywood megastar through roles in the "Star Trek" and "X-Men" franchises…
articles.fullText:
Patrick Stewart, the British Shakespearean actor who became a Hollywood megastar through roles in the "Star Trek" and "X-Men" franchises, has died at his home in Los Angeles. He was 86.

His death on Wednesday came after a "brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to an official statement on his social media accounts.

"His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre," the statement said.

The actor, who hailed from the northern English region of Yorkshire, trod the boards in Britain with the Royal Shakespeare Company and the National Theatre in London, and worked on British television.

But he rocketed into the pop culture history books in his mid-40s when he was cast as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation," and then again as Professor Charles Xavier in multiple "X-Men" and related Marvel films.

"He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction's most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise," the official statement said.

Stewart was 47 when he debuted as Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation," the first live-action television spinoff of the trailblazing sci-fi series from the late 1960s.

He effectively filled the boots of William Shatner's Captain Kirk from the original show – to resounding success, both in the TV series and in several films.

Picard became known for a few catchphrases including "Make it so" and "Engage!"

But his move to America in 1987 was initially greeted with disdain by the Los Angeles Times, who wrote him off as an "unknown British Shakespearean actor."

Stewart later dubbed suggestions he was "slumming it" by moving into US television offensive.

He once called his Shakespearean bona fides "nothing but a preparation for sitting in the captain's chair of the Enterprise."

Stewart found further acclaim in many films of the "X-Men" series, debuting in 2000 as Professor Charles Xavier, the founder and mentor of the mutant superhero team.

"For more than 25 years, he brought a gravitas and profundity to the role, earning fans across the globe," Marvel Studios said on Thursday.

Longtime co-star Hugh Jackman, who played Wolverine, remembered Stewart as both "one of the greats of stage and screen" and "a tremendous friend and man."

Stewart is to make his final on-screen film appearance as Professor Xavier in "Avengers: Doomsday," set for release in December.

"What a heartbreaking week it has been," posted Shatner.

Stewart's death marked the second in days from the "Star Trek" universe, following that of Walter Koenig, who played Chekov in the original series.

Shatner said Stewart – who most recently played Picard in 2023 – brought "intelligence, grace and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did."

Stewart earned four Emmy nominations but never won. He did nab a spoken word Grammy, for his narration of "Prokofiev: Peter And The Wolf."

And even as he found success in Hollywood, Stewart's love of theater, and the bard in particular, never left him.

Between filming, he would return to the stage, winning two Olivier awards.

Shakespeare, Stewart said, "feels like a friend, someone who just went out of the room to get another bottle of wine."

The Royal Shakespeare Company called him "a colossus of both stage and screen and one of the finest classical Shakespearean actors of his generation."

Stewart was born on July 13, 1940 in the small West Yorkshire town of Mirfield, the third of three brothers in a working-class family.

His father, back from World War II and perhaps suffering from PTSD, would often beat Stewart's mother – which prompted Stewart to later work with the charity Refuge, which specialises in domestic abuse.

The actor left school at 15, and studied at Bristol Old Vic Drama School beginning in 1957, making his professional acting debut two years later.

Prematurely balding, Stewart missed out on many of the young romantic leads but quickly slotted into theater life, joining the RSC in 1966 and staying there until 1982.

Any misgivings Stewart had about taking the Picard role in the "Star Trek" universe were mollified by the thought it would be a one-season failure.

He was wrong.

"It changed my life," he said.

Knighted in 2010, Stewart married three times: to Sheila Falconer, with whom he had two children; briefly to "Star Trek" producer Wendy Neuss; and most recently to American singer Sunny Ozell, 38 years his junior. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: US stocks slip as Google drags down Nasdaq
articles.excerpt: Wall Street stocks retreated on Thursday, led by the tech-focused Nasdaq after disappointing results from Google parent Alphabet exacerbated concerns…
articles.fullText:
Wall Street stocks retreated on Thursday, led by the tech-focused Nasdaq after disappointing results from Google parent Alphabet exacerbated concerns over whether the global technology boom can be sustained.

Shares of Alphabet finished down more than 12 percent, resulting in around a US$480 billion hit to the tech giant's market value in a bruising session.

European bourses had advanced earlier in the day, with the European Central Bank leaving interest rates unchanged after the Federal Reserve maintained US borrowing costs on Wednesday.

The euro dipped after Christine Lagarde announced she would step down as the ECB's president in February, but then rose after her press conference.

The drop in Alphabet weighed on all three major US equity indices, led by the tech-focused Nasdaq, which lost 1.4 percent.

The Alphabet slump came after it reported disappointing growth in both advertising revenue and revenue from its search business.

The company also said it would continue to increase capex spending significantly in 2027 after estimating the 2026 level as between US$195 billion to US$205 billion.

"I would broadly think of all of this as a long-range planning process, not a short-term allocation exercise," Google CEO Sundar Pichai told analysts of the company's investment splurge.

But markets were unnerved by the plan.

The Alphabet report "is renewing concerns about AI investment returns, helping push the Nasdaq sharply lower," said a note from Briefing.com.

Shareholders "want clear evidence that all of this investment will eventually translate into stronger profits," Angelo Kourkafas of Edward Jones said.

But Kourkafas noted that the weakness in equities was not broad-based, with Eli Lilly and MasterCard among the companies that gained after earnings reports.

"Money is not exiting equities. It's just moving around and rotating," Kourkafas said.

Government data showed US economic growth in third quarter came in at a better than expected 3.4 percent, with authorities citing solid consumer spending as a factor.

The US Federal Reserve's preferred gauge for inflation – the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index – rose by 3.6 percent year-on-year in September, an increase from the previous month.

The reports came a day after the Fed kept interest rates flat despite elevated inflation.

As expected by economists, the ECB meanwhile left its benchmark rate unchanged at 2.5 percent, after having already lifted it twice this year.

The decision came just hours after Lagarde announced she would step down early, in February 2027.

Lagarde gave little away about her next moves at Thursday's press conference, saying only she wanted to be able to speak more freely on matters outside of monetary policy.

This will stoke expectations that the former French finance minister, who served in centre-right governments, could campaign in the presidential elections, although she has previously ruled out running for the presidency herself.

Eurozone inflation rose to a three-year high of 3.8 percent in September, driven by surging energy costs amid the Middle East conflict, but the ECB stressed core inflation – excluding food and energy costs – was under control.

"While the full effects of the energy shock are still unfolding, underlying inflation has remained broadly stable so far," Lagarde said.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 1.4 percent, to 26,185, the S&P 500 fell 0.3 percent, to 7,720, and the Dow also fell 0.3 percent, to 52,343. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Spain demands answers as rail disaster toll rises
articles.excerpt: Spain began demanding answers on Thursday after the toll from the country's second high-speed train collision this year rose to…
articles.fullText:
Spain began demanding answers on Thursday after the toll from the country's second high-speed train collision this year rose to 69 people, with scores injured and distraught relatives desperately seeking news about their loved ones.

One of Europe's deadliest rail disasters this century struck south of Madrid on Wednesday morning when a service by state operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to private Spanish company Iryo.

Manuel San Emeterio, whose 54-year-old brother Pepe is missing, came to the central city of Toledo to provide DNA samples to the Civil Guard after finding out about the accident through a smart-watch notification.

"The uncertainty is the worst thing that you deal with, everyone is dealing with it," he said. "But I think there's something that counters it, which is hope... we must never lose it."

Toledo has received 52 of the corpses, overwhelming its morgue's capacity of 30 and forcing the army to set up an improvised facility.

Forensics experts in green jackets, a black funeral car and army vehicles moved in and out of the site, equipped with red marquees and refrigerated containers.

Sniffer dogs and thermal drones searched for bodies at the crash site outside the central village of Urda, around 130 kilometres south of Madrid.

The toll was 69 on Thursday, according to the transport ministry's website and regional authorities.

Among the victims was Fatima Banez, a former labour minister for the main conservative Popular Party (PP), Spain's CEOE business association confirmed on Thursday.

Jose Miguel Fernandez, a parish priest in Urda, joined the emergency services in offering support to families still waiting to learn the fate of their loved ones.

"Many of them were calm, others were nervous and desperate. They wanted to know straight away and get news" of their loved ones, he said.

Flags flew at half-mast on public buildings with official ceremonies and public events cancelled or scaled back on the first of three days of national mourning.

A minute of silence was observed up and down the country, including at Spain's busiest train station Atocha in Madrid, where some mourners shed tears.

Wednesday's accident happened on a key line linking Madrid to the southern city of Seville, which was also the scene of a collision in January that killed 46 people.

It has raised fresh questions about safety on Spain's high-speed rail network, the second-largest in the world after China's.

Toledo resident Marcos Ibanez, who works in tourism, said he had avoided high-speed trains "for a long time because of this."

"I've gone through the place where the accident happened several times... and you never know when it might be your turn," the 28-year-old said. "Most people are pretty fed up."

During a visit to the disaster site, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who faces a general election on November 29, pledged "to establish every last detail of this tragedy and strengthen safety measures to ensure it never happens again."

King Felipe also intervened in the debate after visiting injured victims at a Toledo hospital, calling for measures "to ensure this does not happen again."

Transport Minister Oscar Puente said on Wednesday that an automatic control system went down on 69 kilometres of track, causing all trains there to be stopped.

But the control centre decided to "resume traffic in circumstances that, from our point of view, are inexplicable," Puente said, with the Renfe train travelling 25 kilometres before striking the Iryo.

The control centre "had more than enough time to verify the error, and they did not fix it," he added.

The head of train driver union Semaf, Diego Martin, said "attention is wrongly being focused on searching for culprits" when workers were using "degraded systems."

Renfe train drivers went on strike on Thursday "to defend rail safety," saying previous commitments on the issue had been broken. The industrial action had been called before Wednesday's crash.

Sanchez's main rival, PP leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo, accused Puente of "frivolity" by trying to pin the blame on one control centre operator.

Toledo resident Ibanez agreed that Puente should shoulder the blame, "because someone in politics has to take responsibility." (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Building repair reforms unveiled
articles.excerpt: (To watch the full press conference with sign language interpretation, click here .) The Housing Bureau will establish the Public…
articles.fullText:
(To watch the full press conference with sign language interpretation, click here .)

The Housing Bureau will establish the Public Housing Building Control Section (PBC) within the next month to replace the Independent Checking Unit, launching a new project-based regulatory regime to strengthen the oversight of large-scale maintenance and renovation works in courts and estates.

The Development Bureau and the Housing Bureau today jointly announced the details of the comprehensive reform measures, which are based on the findings of the independent committee’s report on the fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po.

The PBC will strengthen and focus regulation of existing buildings and maintenance works across all public rental housing (PRH) estates, subsidised sale housing courts and related facilities sold or divested by the Housing Authority (HA). It will also regulate new public housing development projects (including PRH and subsidised sale housing) developed by the HA, as well as relevant works for existing, non-divested PRH estates.

Announcing the measures at a press conference this morning, Deputy Financial Secretary & Acting Secretary for Housing Michael Wong said this new project-based model will provide macro-level co-ordination and comprehensive management of large-scale maintenance and renovation projects in housing courts and estates. He noted this will target high-risk, large-scale maintenance works to improve overall project co-ordination, communication and risk control.

Where individual public housing courts or estates carry out major building maintenance and renovation works regulated under the Buildings Ordinance, the Head of the PBC will set up a project-specific team to handle related works matters in an integrated manner. The team will assign a dedicated liaison officer to proactively contact the relevant Owners' Corporation and provide necessary assistance.

In tandem, the Government will establish the Building Maintenance Support & Services Council (BMSSC) to provide more proactive support to owners in maintaining properties.

Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn noted that the BMSSC will provide end-to-end services with standard fees calculated on a cost-recovery basis. The preliminary estimate of the cost is several thousand dollars per household.

The Government has earmarked $100 million in this year’s Budget as start-up capital for the BMSSC to cover initial staff expenditure and operating expenses, with the council expected to achieve self-financing in the long run. An additional $200 million has also been earmarked to provide fee concessions to owners in need.

The Government aims to set up the BMSSC by the end of this year, with project tendering for owners commencing within the first quarter of 2027.

articles.title: Bill seeks to protect cetaceans
articles.excerpt: The Wild Animals Protection (Amendment) Bill 2026 was published in the Government Gazette today, enhancing the protection of cetaceans appearing…
articles.fullText:
The Wild Animals Protection (Amendment) Bill 2026 was published in the Government Gazette today, enhancing the protection of cetaceans appearing in Hong Kong waters.

The bill proposes to grant the Director of Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation the power to designate temporary marine restricted areas (TMRAs) within Hong Kong waters when necessary to protect cetaceans.

The measure is to safeguard the health or well-being of cetaceans in these designated areas, as well as to impose restrictions or prohibitions on persons, vessels, and activities within the TMRAs. It also introduces new offences and enforcement powers against non-compliance with control measures within the TMRAs.

The Government noted that the presence of cetaceans, especially whales, often attracts significant public attention and draws people to approach them for viewing, adding that the presence of people and vessels near an injured or stranded cetacean may cause disturbance or distress, hinder rescue operations, and pose risks to the safety of other marine users.

The proposed amendment aims to empower the Government to implement appropriate control measures in a swift and flexible manner when necessary, with a view to enhancing the protection of cetaceans and safeguarding the safety of other marine users.

The Government consulted the Nature Conservation Subcommittee of the Advisory Council on the Environment, and the Legislative Council Panel on Environmental Affairs on the bill on June 30 and July 10 this year, respectively, and panel members expressed support for the proposed amendments. Other relevant stakeholders also generally supported the legislative proposal.

The bill will be introduced into LegCo for its first and second reading on November 11.

articles.title: 100k private flats projected
articles.excerpt: The projected private flat supply for the next three to four years is 100,000 units, up 4,000 from the previous…
articles.fullText:
The projected private flat supply for the next three to four years is 100,000 units, up 4,000 from the previous estimate.

The Housing Bureau said today there were 19,000 unsold units in completed projects as of the end of September.

There were also 62,000 units under construction, excluding those pre-sold by developers; and 19,000 units from disposed sites where construction may start at any time.

The number of flats under construction in the third quarter this year was 2,800, while 1,700 units were completed during the same period.

articles.fullText:
The Strive & Rise Programme began recruiting 4,000 mentees for its fifth cohort today, and applications will close on November 19.

Secondary One to Secondary Four students from underprivileged families, particularly those living in subdivided units, can submit their applications through the programme’s mobile app.

Formulated and implemented by an interdepartmental task force led by the Chief Secretary, the programme comprises three key elements – mentorship, personal development plans and financial support.

The one-year intensive foundation training includes mentorship and a structured programme covering orientation, basic training, mentor-mentee interaction, diverse group activities, Mainland study and exchange tours, and more.

It aims to help mentees broaden their horizons, build self-confidence, develop a positive outlook on life, explore more possibilities for personal development, set goals for the future and strive for upward mobility.

Each mentee will be provided with start-up financial support of $5,000. Mentors will assist and guide mentees in developing positive financial planning concepts and implementing their personal development plans.

Upon successful completion of the programme, mentees will receive a scholarship of $5,000 and automatically become members of the Alumni Club.

For enquiries, interested students may approach their schools or the non-governmental organisations assisting the Government in implementing the programme.

The Immigration Department (ImmD) today announced that the visa-free period of stay in Hong Kong for APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) holders will be extended from 60 days to 90 days starting November 1.

To enjoy the visa-free stay, cardholders must have obtained pre-clearance from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

The ImmD noted that the APEC Business Mobility Group recently announced that five participating economies of the ABTC Scheme – the People’s Republic of China; Hong Kong, China; Indonesia; the Philippines; and Singapore – will extend the maximum stay for visiting ABTC holders to 90 days to enhance the card's effectiveness.

While each of the five economies will determine its own implementation timeline, the Mainland will roll out the new arrangement on November 1. The Hong Kong SAR is implementing the extension concurrently to align with the Mainland’s timeline.

Currently, 19 economies participate in the scheme: Australia; Brunei Darussalam; Chile; the People’s Republic of China; Hong Kong, China; Indonesia; Japan; the Republic of Korea; Malaysia; Mexico; New Zealand; Papua New Guinea; Peru; the Philippines; Russia; Singapore; Chinese Taipei; Thailand; and Vietnam.

ABTC holders who have obtained pre-clearance from these participating economies are entitled to a visa-free stay of no less than 60 days.

articles.title: New measures to combat bid-rigging
articles.excerpt: The Government today announced a series of reform measures using a three-pronged approach to rigorously combat bid-rigging and other syndicate-led…
articles.fullText:
The Government today announced a series of reform measures using a three-pronged approach to rigorously combat bid-rigging and other syndicate-led criminal activities in building maintenance and renovation projects.

Under existing legislation, bid-rigging is primarily addressed through the civil regime under the Competition Ordinance, while criminal enforcement can only target other offences arising during the process. To tackle this, the Government will introduce a series of legislative amendments, step up law enforcement co-ordination and enhance frontline prevention.

The Government proposes amending the Competition Ordinance to criminalise four types of serious anti-competitive conduct involving tenders for building maintenance and renovation projects, holding the individuals and undertakings concerned criminally liable. These four types of conduct comprise bid-rigging, price-fixing, market sharing and output restrictions.

To tackle collusion comprehensively across all stages, the proposed regulatory scope will cover tendering for works contractors as well as related preparatory arrangements, such as engaging consultants at the preliminary stage.

To enhance deterrence, the new criminal offence will carry a maximum penalty of 10 years' imprisonment and a fine. The maximum fine will be the highest of $10 million, three times the total value of the commercial gains derived from the contravention, or an amount calculated at 50% of the undertaking’s local turnover for each year the contravention occurred.

The overall civil regime under the Competition Ordinance will be enhanced in parallel to strengthen penalties and improve enforcement effectiveness.

Additionally, the Government proposes designating the new criminal offence as a specified offence under the Organised & Serious Crimes Ordinance and the Independent Commission Against Corruption Ordinance. This will strengthen the investigative powers of the law enforcement agencies, enabling the Police Force, the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) and the Competition Commission to collaborate more effectively.

These agencies will be able to leverage specific powers to target syndicates.

Through a Witness Order, the Secretary for Justice may apply to the Court of First Instance for an order requiring a relevant person to answer questions or furnish information. Through a Production Order, the Secretary for Justice or an authorised officer may apply to the Court of First Instance to require a specified individual, entity or public officer to provide material or permit access to it within a specified period.

Furthermore, the prosecution may apply for an enhanced sentence, allowing the court to impose a substantially heavier penalty based on the seriousness of the case, the extent of harm inflicted on the community, or the prevalence of the offence. The court may also issue a confiscation order to recover money or property from convicted criminals, which covers all realisable property belonging to the defendant, including real property, stocks and vehicles.

The Government will also step up the co-ordination of law enforcement actions on all fronts. The Chief Executive has tasked the Secretary for Security to lead the establishment of a joint task force to combat bid-rigging in building maintenance and renovation projects.

Comprising representatives from the Police Force, the ICAC and the Competition Commission, the task force will combat syndicates through intelligence sharing, joint operations and preventive measures.

The Hong Kong Tourism Board and Vinexposium, a leading global organiser of wine and spirits trade events, have signed a memorandum of understanding to establish a five-year strategic partnership.

Under the agreement, Hong Kong will secure exclusive hosting rights for Vinexpo Asia for five consecutive years starting next year. The first annual event under this partnership is scheduled to take place at the Convention & Exhibition Centre, from June 8 to 10 next year.

The signing ceremony was witnessed by Secretary for Culture, Sports & Tourism Rosanna Law and Tourism Board Chairman Peter Lam.

Mr Lam thanked Vinexposium, describing the decision as a powerful endorsement of Hong Kong’s unique advantages as an international trade centre.

“More importantly, it demonstrates the confidence that global business and event organisers continue to place in Hong Kong. Under this new partnership, we also take Vinexpo Asia beyond the exhibition halls and make it a city-wide event,” he said.

Vinexposium Overseas Events Director Deborah Sanchez noted that Hong Kong has always held a special place in Vinexpo Asia's global strategy.

“Over nearly three decades here, we have built trusted relationships, strong networks, and an unwavering commitment to this market. And today, what our industry needs is stability, clarity and long-term visibility,” she said.

“By establishing Vinexpo Asia here as an annual permanent gathering, we are giving our exhibitors and our international buyers a clear, reliable anchor to plan ahead, invest and grow together. One city, one annual meeting point, one powerful platform connecting the world of wine and spirits across Asia,” she added.

“And now, building on three decades of trust, we are now taking this commitment even further.”

articles.title: US economy posts stronger Q3 growth
articles.excerpt: The US economy grew at a healthy 3.4 percent annual pace from July through September, accelerating from the second quarter…
articles.fullText:
The US economy grew at a healthy 3.4 percent annual pace from July through September, accelerating from the second quarter on strong consumer spending and investment in artificial intelligence.

The expansion in third-quarter gross domestic product – the nation’s output of goods and services – was faster than the 2.2 percent growth registered from April through June, the US Commerce Department said on Thursday.

Consumer spending rose at a brisk 3.8 percent clip in the third quarter, and business investment was up sharply, reflecting the AI boom.

The American economy – by far, the world’s biggest – has proven resilient in the face of higher energy prices caused by the fighting with Iran.

Economists had expected GDP to grow 3 percent in the third quarter, according to a survey of forecasters by the data firm FactSet.

US growth has been lifted by an AI investment boom. Business investment, excluding housing, was up 12.7 percent in the third quarter. Investment in information processing equipment surged 37.4 percent, in software 9.6 percent and in research and development 7.5 percent.

However, housing investment, hurt by high mortgage rates, dropped 3.3 percent and has now fallen six of the last seven quarters.

Thursday’s report was the first of three Commerce Department estimates of third-quarter GDP growth. (AP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

The Shenzhen Bay control point will extend its opening hours on Friday and Saturday to help facilitate cross-boundary traffic.

Clearance time at the crossing will be extended to 2am from midnight, as the number of travellers is expected to surge due to a series of events staged in Hong Kong including Halloween festivities, the Wine and Dine Festival and mega concerts.

The government said on Thursday that it reached a consensus with Shenzhen authorities for the arrangement, so as to alleviate the expected surge in passenger and vehicular flows at the round-the-clock Huanggang port and San Tin Highway.

SAR authorities have also coordinated with cross-boundary coach operators to extend their service hours serving Shenzhen Bay.

Franchised bus operators, for their part, will arrange two special overnight bus routes to ply between the port and Yuen Long/Tin Shui Wai and Tuen Mun respectively.

“The implementation of the special arrangement to extend the clearance hours at the Shenzhen Bay Control Point helps divert late-night cross-boundary passenger and vehicular flows and facilitates travel for residents of both places and visitors,” a government spokesman said.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.excerpt: The government said on Thursday it won't proceed with a lighting project on the Peak that drew opposition from residents…
articles.fullText:
The government said on Thursday it won't proceed with a lighting project on the Peak that drew opposition from residents.

The Hong Kong Tourism Board (HKTB) will remove the installations as soon as possible and restore the site to its original condition, according to a paper submitted by the board and the Tourism Commission to the Central and Western District Council.

“As we have just started moving forward, we have only carried out part of the work. We haven’t started operating or doing maintenance and repair work. So the resources we have used are limited," tourism minister Rosanna Law told reporters.

"These are resources that were allocated to the Tourism Board a long time ago.”

Law also said the light fittings that are to be removed could be useful for other HKTB projects.

According to the document, the project had been planned for the area around Lugard and Harlech roads on the Peak, where there would be small-scale lighting installations at designated spots along a walking trail.

Upon learning the concerns from the public, the government and HKTB arranged site visits with both lawmakers and district councillors, and looked into various enhancement measures.

For instance, the board considered reducing the number of scenic spots along the trail from 10 to seven and shortening the project’s duration from one year to the end of February. It also planned to slash the number of trees used for hanging light fittings by more than half to 24.

Still, the government noted that the proposed amendments might not be able to fully ease concerns of residents and trail users.

“On the other hand, following a significant reduction in the project’s scale, even with efforts to retain the most distinctive design elements, we are wary that it could be difficult to fully realise the original design concept and lighting effect,” the document read.

This would compromise the overall experience and appeal of the project, it added, and might not meet its expected results of encouraging travellers to revisit the SAR and stay longer through infusing traditional attractions with new elements.

Edited by Edmond Fong
