Additionally, the Government will overhaul the operational and regulatory system for building works, restructure regulatory departments, establish a centralised data system and reform the complaint mechanism.

“In addition to the 120 recommendations, we will do more – such as revamping the complaints system, ensuring that complaints are not just handled at departmental level but will be upgraded to the central system, with senior officials in the centre using assistive artificial intelligence to identify repeated problems, to identify probable complaints we do not think are handled to the best degree as we would like,” Mr Lee said.

A steering committee led by the Chief Secretary will be set up to review each recommendation, drive implementation and monitor the submission of proposed legislative amendments across six pieces of legislation to the Legislative Council.

Separately, the Chief Executive has activated the Administrative Responsibility Two-tier Investigation Mechanism under the Heads of Department Accountability System. The case has been referred to the Public Service Commission to conduct an investigation into the alleged deficiencies and failings of the civil servants concerned. The probe is expected to be completed within three months.

The Government added that the full report will be released after all relevant criminal proceedings have concluded.

articles.title: CE congratulates plenary session
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee today expressed his warm congratulations on the successful conclusion of the Fifth Plenary Session of the…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee today expressed his warm congratulations on the successful conclusion of the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) in Beijing.

The session deliberated and adopted the Resolution of the Central Committee of the CPC on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance.

Mr Lee said he was encouraged and inspired by the session, noting that exercising full and rigorous self-governance bears on the CPC's leadership capability and the country's governance capacity. He emphasised that this holds important guiding significance for the governance of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Since assuming office, the Chief Executive has built a government team focused on a result-oriented approach, consistently emphasising that reform is a continuous, ongoing endeavour.

“The Hong Kong SAR Government must closely integrate the spirit of the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee with Hong Kong's actual circumstances, continue to improve and reform itself, continuously enhance governance efficiency, strengthen the development of the governance team, and improve institutional mechanisms to better respond to public concerns,” Mr Lee said.

“The Hong Kong SAR Government will take forward such measures as incorporating the requirement of full rigour throughout the entire process of the Hong Kong SAR's governance, and better co-ordinating development and security.”

In addition, the Hong Kong SAR Government remains fully committed to implementing Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, transforming the strategic plans into tangible outcomes to drive high-quality development across the city.

The Chief Executive added that the Hong Kong SAR Government will continue to fully and faithfully implement the principle of "one country, two systems". Supported strongly by the central authorities, the Government aims to unite all sectors of the community to earnestly study and implement the spirit of the plenary session.

By leveraging the strength and value of "patriots administering Hong Kong", Mr Lee stated that Hong Kong will fulfil its responsibilities, seize opportunities and contribute to the country's continuous progress in building a great nation and achieving national rejuvenation on all fronts through Chinese modernisation.

articles.title: Shenzhen Bay to extend hours
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today announced that passenger and vehicle clearance services at the Shenzhen Bay Control…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today announced that passenger and vehicle clearance services at the Shenzhen Bay Control Point will be extended by two hours until 2am on October 30 and 31. The arrangement follows a consensus reached with Shenzhen authorities to facilitate festival traffic.

A substantial rise in visitor arrivals and late-night cross-boundary trips is anticipated over the Halloween weekend, which coincides with major local events including the Hong Kong Wine & Dine Festival and mega concerts.

The Hong Kong SAR Government expects the busiest period for northbound traffic at Huanggang Port to be between 11pm and 2am overnight, warning of heavy congestion around the port area and San Tin Highway. The extended hours at Shenzhen Bay aim to divert this late-night flow.

Cross-boundary coach operators have co-ordinated with the Hong Kong SAR Government to extend northbound services utilizing the Shenzhen Bay Control Point.

For local public transport services, franchised bus operators will run two special overnight bus routes – NB2 and NB3 – during the early morning hours. These will connect the Shenzhen Bay Control Point and Yuen Long/Tin Shui Wai and Tuen Mun respectively.

Clearance arrangements at Huanggang Port will remain unchanged.

Travellers are advised to check real-time updates – including average passenger and private car waiting times – via the Security Bureau’s “Easy Boundary” platform or the Transport Department’s “HKeMobility” mobile application to plan their journeys and avoid delays.

articles.title: Team formed to probe fire failings
articles.excerpt: The Public Service Commission today announced the formation of an investigation team to examine alleged deficiencies and failings in overseeing…
articles.fullText:
The Public Service Commission today announced the formation of an investigation team to examine alleged deficiencies and failings in overseeing the fire risks associated with the works at Wang Fuk Court.

The move follows a referral by Chief Executive John Lee to activate the Administrative Responsibility Two-tier Investigation Mechanism under the Heads of Department Accountability System. The team will probe whether the relevant departments failed to properly discharge their duties and responsibilities regarding fire risk oversight.

As identified in the report submitted by the independent committee set up in relation to the fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, the departments under review include the Housing Bureau’s Independent Checking Unit, the Buildings Department, the Fire Services Department and the Labour Department.

Tasked with collecting evidence, the team will investigate the responsibilities of the individual officers concerned, examining whether they neglected their duties or contravened departmental guidelines, the Civil Service Code and civil service administrative regulations.

The team is also mandated to advise the Government on appropriate disciplinary or administrative actions against officers with alleged failings, in accordance with departmental guidelines, the Public Service (Administration) Order, the Public Service (Disciplinary) Regulation and other relevant regulations.

Chaired by Commission Chairman Maisie Cheng Mei-sze, the team also comprises Commission members Ann Kung Yeung Yun-chi and Adrian Wong Koon-man.

Ms Cheng stated that the team will spearhead the investigation, directly participating in and supervising the entire process.

“We will take the committee report and the voluminous information which has been made public earlier as a starting point, uphold the principles of fairness and impartiality in the course of ascertaining the facts as well as sorting out and clarifying the administrative responsibilities of the civil servants concerned, including whether they had failed their duties and contravened relevant departmental guidelines, the Civil Service Code and civil service administrative regulations,” she added.

To support its work, the team has established a support office under the Investigation Regulation.

The Government has progressively deployed personnel from various grades to join the preparatory work since August. Over the past few weeks, the team has studied extensive material released by the independent committee to facilitate the investigation.

Moving forward, the support office will assist the team by requesting information from the relevant departments and arranging professional, rigorous meetings with the civil servants involved.

articles.title: Priority given to buses at Huanggang this weekend
articles.excerpt: The government warned that private cars crossing into Shenzhen via the Huanggang checkpoint during peak hours this weekend could face…
articles.fullText:
The government warned that private cars crossing into Shenzhen via the Huanggang checkpoint during peak hours this weekend could face waits of more than an hour, as priority would be given to those arriving by public transport.

Late-night outbound passenger flow surged last weekend, with scores of visitors leaving the city after attending a concert in Kai Tak or Halloween festivities elsewhere.

In a press briefing on Wednesday, Chief Secretary Eric Chan said more than 1,000 vehicles passed through Huanggang within two hours last Saturday, far exceeding its capacity of 360 vehicles per hour.

With more concerts scheduled this Friday and Saturday, plus the Wine and Dine Festival at the Central Harbourfront, authorities are bracing for another hectic weekend at the port.

Chan said northbound traffic at the crossing is expected to peak between 11pm and 2am from October 30 to November 1.

All inspection counters and vehicle lanes will open during those times to facilitate the travel peak.

Chan said priority will be given to public transport, while private cars will be diverted to a holding area when necessary, with possible waiting times of more than one hour.

He also urged travellers not to patronise unauthorised ride-hailing services.

"We will take law enforcement action because this is no good for the passengers. There is a risk in case of accidents – the insurance will not cover the damage," he said, adding that three arrests were made in the past two days.

Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan said cross-border coach operators would ramp up services this weekend, with frequencies of up to five minutes.

Secretary for Security Chris Tang said an emergency monitoring and support centre will start operating at noon on Friday to coordinate between government departments.

Eric Chan once again appealed to travellers to consider staying overnight.

"Rather than being stuck in traffic, why not spend an extra hour at Lan Kwai Fong?" he said.

Edited by Raymond Yeung

articles.title: The Download: dead startups fueling AI and interspecies communication
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in…
articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models

When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup, he didn’t think its data was worth much. But he’s since turned the company’s digital archives into tens of thousands of dollars, selling its codebase and workspace data.

He’s part of a growing market in which companies that help shut down startups sell their data to AI labs. Demand has grown as training labs hit the limits of public and synthetic datasets, with buyers seeking real-world records to help train AI agents. But the sales raise legal and ethical questions.

Read the full story on the AI labs buying up the remains of failed startups .

—Matthew King

Are we there yet? Interspecies communication

Humans are far from the only species with a gift for gab, and our furry, feathered, and finned friends could have a lot to tell us.

Decoding how animals communicate with one another could reveal the inner lives of other species—and give humans a window onto how they see the world. A growing arsenal of devices and advances in AI have made it easier to study their howls, squeaks, and clicks, but making sense of it all remains complex.

Find out how close we are to interspecies communication .

—Cassandra Willyard

This story is part of “Are we there yet?” , our series that takes stock of six technologies that have long promised to change the world—and scores them on a progress meter. We’re exploring each one in The Download, so stay tuned, and subscribe to read the rest of the stories in our new Impossible issue .

MIT Technology Review Narrated: what it would take to build a city on the moon

The US and China are racing to build bases on the moon, with NASA hoping to establish a small lunar city by the end of the century. But the moon is a tremendously hostile place to set up camp.

A sprawling lunar base must be safe for its inhabitants, protected from falling asteroids, endless cosmic radiation, razor-sharp lunar dust, and torturous temperature swings. It also must be somewhat self-sustaining.

That will require autonomous robots, nuclear power, and a way to use the moon’s resources to keep the base operating. But the chief obstacle may be one of political will .

This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts . Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released.

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

The FEC filing system went offline a week before the midterms. ( Reuters $)

3 Greenhouse gas levels keep reaching new records worldwide
Carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide are all on the up. ( New Scientist $)
+ Trump is making it easier for fossil fuel companies to leak methane. ( Verge )
+ The IPCC is fighting for survival. ( Nature )
+ How to study a swiftly melting climate disaster. ( MIT Technology Review )

4 Monkeys’ brains have revealed new clues about consciousness
Their neural activity encodes images that escape their awareness. ( Nature )
+ Bees’ feelings are also changing views of consciousness. ( New Scientist $)
+ Debates over AI consciousness are a trap. ( MIT Technology Review )

5 Chinese scientists have developed a catalyst to make Mars rocket fuel
It converts Martian atmospheric carbon dioxide into liquid methanol. ( SCMP )

6 Tech billionaires have teamed up against California’s wealth tax

7 Delaware plans to let AI agents run entire businesses
The proposal could let owners evade responsibility for harm. ( Ars Technica )

8 Palmer Luckey has unveiled plans for American-made military laptops
Anduril will build rugged PCs in Ohio using Qualcomm chips. ( WSJ $)

articles.excerpt: Former vice premier and state councilor Liu Yandong passed away due to illness at the age of 81 in Beijing…
articles.fullText:
Former vice premier and state councilor Liu Yandong passed away due to illness at the age of 81 in Beijing on Wednesday afternoon, according to Xinhua News Agency.

Liu also served as a member of the Political Bureau of the 17th and 18th Central Committees of the Communist Party of China (CPC), and a vice chairperson of the 10th National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference.

Liu was "an excellent Party member, a time-tested and loyal communist fighter, and an outstanding leader in the CPC's united front work and in the fields of education, science and technology, health, and children and women work in China," an official statement said.

Chief Executive John Lee expressed his profound sorrow over Liu's passing, and extended his condolences to her family.

"[Former Vice Premier Liu] served as a member of the Preparatory Committee of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region under the National People's Congress and deputy leader of the Central Coordination Group for Hong Kong and Macao Affairs, and had always cared for and supported the long-term stability and prosperity of Hong Kong," a statement read.

Lee recalled Liu's multiple visits to the SAR, where she reached out to people from different sectors and fully demonstrated her care for Hong Kong and its people.

"I am sincerely grateful for her contributions to promoting the development of Hong Kong in such areas as education, economy and sports," Lee added. (Additional reporting by Xinhua)

articles.title: Tech stocks soar pushing regional bourses higher
articles.excerpt: Technology firms surged in Asia on Wednesday after blockbuster earnings from chip giant SK hynix helped boost optimism in the…
articles.fullText:
Technology firms surged in Asia on Wednesday after blockbuster earnings from chip giant SK hynix helped boost optimism in the AI trade ahead of results from Wall Street titans Microsoft and Alphabet.

Oil prices rose as investors kept tabs on Israel's election results, which could determine the future of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's war against Iran.

In Hong Kong, the stock market ended higher, with the benchmark Hang Seng Index up 0.23 percent to close at 23,094 points.

The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index gained 0.32 percent to 7,791 points, and the Hang Seng Tech Index jumped 1.40 percent to 3,853 points.

On the mainland, the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index finished up 0.91 percent to 3,681 points while the Shenzhen Component Index closed 2.02 percent higher.

Turnover of stocks covered by these two indices totalled about 1.63 trillion yuan, up from 1.46 trillion yuan on the previous trading day.

Shares in robotics, semiconductor chips and AI-generated animated dramas were among the top gainers, while stocks in the pork and insurance sectors fell against the broader upward trend.

The ChiNext Index, tracking China's Nasdaq-style board of growth enterprises, gained 3.4 percent.

The STAR Composite Index, which reflects the performance of stocks on China's sci-tech innovation board, closed 3.2 percent higher.

Elsewhere in Asia, Tokyo stocks closed mixed.

Artificial intelligence-related shares extended gains as worries about the profitability and sustainability of massive investments in the sector eased, but rising crude oil futures prompted selling in the broader market.

The benchmark Nikkei stock index, climbed 685 points, or 1.08 percent, to finish at 63,954.

The broader Topix index, meanwhile, slipped 5.66 points, or 0.14 percent.

Heavyweight AI- and semiconductor-related shares tracked their US counterparts higher, with upbeat details in the initial public offering prospectus of AI giant Anthropic drawing buyers to the Tokyo market for a second straight session.

Meanwhile, SK hynix, which has been at the forefront of the chip boom, said on Wednesday that third-quarter operating profit soared 632 percent to US$62.8 billion thanks to explosive demand for its advanced semiconductors.

The firm said it had now posted record revenue and operating profit for six straight quarters.

"While Wall Street argues over whether the AI arms race can keep financing itself, SK hynix has just reminded the market that somebody on the other side of all that capex is receiving the cheque," wrote Stephen Innes at SPI Asset Management.

Shares in SK hynix soared almost 11 percent and South Korean rival Samsung, which reports on Thursday, added nine percent.

That pushed Seoul's Kospi index up more than six percent at the close. (AFP/Xinhua)

articles.title: China takes Mbappe's apology for Mao comment seriously
articles.excerpt: Beijing on Wednesday said it took seriously an apology from Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe after he made comments about…
articles.fullText:
Beijing on Wednesday said it took seriously an apology from Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe after he made comments about former leader Mao Zedong.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing on Wednesday: "We take seriously the apology the individual concerned has made."

The French footballer's recent comment, in which he appeared to mock the founding leader of the People's Republic of China, resulted in major Chinese brands dropping their sponsorship deals with the player, and saw Spanish football suspended from television.

The ministry responded by said that hurting the feelings of the country's people would meet "unanimous rejection".

Mbappe later apologised.

"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset.

"This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry," he added.

articles.title: HK's exports surge nearly 65pc in September
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong’s exports and imports both rose for September, according to data released by the Census and Statistics Department on…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong’s exports and imports both rose for September, according to data released by the Census and Statistics Department on Wednesday, with the increase in exports marking the fastest monthly year-on-year growth in more than four decades.

The value of total exports of goods surged by 64.9 percent compared to a year earlier to HK$762.6 billion in September.

It followed a year-on-year increase of 53 percent in August.

The value of imports also went up by 57.8 percent over a year earlier to HK$808.9 billion last month.

A trade deficit of HK$417.7 billion – equivalent to seven percent of the imports value – was recorded in the first nine months of the year.

A government spokesman said AI-related electronic products continued to drive the city’s trade performance, and the growth in exports marked a double-digit growth for the 20th straight month.

It noted that exports to all major destinations have surged remarkably.

“Looking ahead, Hong Kong's merchandise trade performance will continue to benefit from the prevailing wave of robust AI-related investment and the resilient global economic growth,” the statement read.

“Nonetheless, external uncertainties warrant close monitoring, including the Middle East conflict, trade protectionist measures by major economies, and risks associated with the rapid expansion of global investment in AI.”

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Rays win thriller to stay alive in World Series
articles.excerpt: The Tampa Bay Rays staged a dramatic extra-innings rally to keep their World Series dream alive on Tuesday, walking off…
articles.fullText:
The Tampa Bay Rays staged a dramatic extra-innings rally to keep their World Series dream alive on Tuesday, walking off a 4-3 victory against the Milwaukee Brewers to avoid a clean sweep.

Tampa Bay's Ben Williamson singled a ground ball to right field in the bottom of the 12th inning to complete a thrilling comeback at Tropicana Field that ensures a game five on Wednesday.

"Just shows the resiliency of this group," Williamson said afterwards.

"We continue to fight and that's been the motto this series and this whole season."

Milwaukee had looked to be heading for a 4-0 series triumph after rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt launched a solo home run in the 12th inning to give the Brewers a 3-2 lead on the night.

But with their season on the line, the Rays flipped the script, igniting a fightback when a throwing error by Brewers' third baseman Joey Ortiz allowed Junior Caminero to reach first base.

The Brewers brought in reliever Shane Drohan to replace Antonio Senzatela, but the Rays continued to prosper with catcher Liam Hicks singling to send Caminero to third base with no outs.

Jonny DeLuca then singled to drive in a run to make it 3-3, and shortly after that leveller Chandler Simpson singled to load the bases with no outs.

Pinch hitter Williamson then came in and steered a ground ball to right field to score the winning run. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: South China Sea tensions cause China to ‘recall’ teachers from the Philippines
articles.excerpt: Experts caution against xenophobia, but point to links between educational exchange and advocacy of China’s claims.
articles.fullText:
South China Sea tensions are turning Chinese-language education into a security issue in the Philippines, straining civilian ties and exposing schools’ dependence on foreign teaching support, analysts told Radio Free Asia.
At the beginning of this month, reports surfaced that around 150 teachers, mostly instructors of Mandarin Chinese who worked in schools that serve the Philippines’ Chinoy , or ethnic Chinese, communities, were returning to China after Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. and other officials cautioned that educational exchanges with Beijing could potentially lead to national security threats.
The exodus was the result of the teachers’ families requesting that they return to China according to the Federation of Filipino-Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry, a commercial organization serving ethnic Chinese communities in the Philippines. The federation and the Chinese Embassy approved the requests.
In a report on the SeaLight webpage , the maritime transparency project’s executive director Ray Powell characterized the exodus as an organized recall by Beijing that uses “Filipinos of Chinese heritage” as “a card to be played.”
China and the Philippines have become increasingly at odds over their territorial disputes in the South China Sea, and Beijing has been known to use “gray zone” tactics – pressure that can include anything except armed conflict – to advance its claims.
“China’s gray-zone pressure at sea and its political warfare ashore are intertwined, and this episode shows the connective tissue,” Powell told RFA.
The number of affected teachers could be higher than initially disclosed. China’s Ambassador to the Philippines Jing Quan put it closer to 180 while delivering an address to the 20th anniversary celebration of the Confucius Institute at Ateneo de Manila University.
China's Ambassador to the Philippines Jing Quan addresses the 20th anniversary celebration of the Confucius Institute at Ateneo de Manila University Oct. 13, 2026.
(Embassy of the People's Republic of China in the Republic of the Philippines) Jing also rejected allegations that Chinese-language education amounted to political infiltration, calling them “baseless and absurd.”
But Powell said in his report that he and Teodoro had concerns about China-linked education programs being tied to China’s United Front Work Department – the strategy and network by which Beijing projects its political influence overseas.
Reports and rhetoric
Maritime confrontation provided the backdrop, while specific developments involving a Chinese university helped trigger the scrutiny of the programs, Aniello Iannone, a lecturer in international relations and general secretary of the ASEAN Studies Center at Indonesia’s President University, told RFA.
“The spark came from a university symposium and a think-tank report,” he told RFA.
Iannone was referring to the symposium hosted in late June at Jinan University in Guangzhou, China, where scholars advanced a claim that Batanes, the Philippines’ northernmost province, belonged to China through Taiwan .
In July, Powell published a report on the SeaLight website that provided evidence linking Jinan University to training teachers for Chinese-language schools in the Philippines – 43 of 56 Filipino teacher trainees sent to China in 2024 through the Philippine Chinese Education Research Center, he said in the report.
The Filipino trainees were not the mainland Chinese teachers who were recalled, Powell told RFA.
“I haven’t found these programs directly teaching Beijing’s South China Sea claims, and I won’t allege it,” he said.
Instead, he argued that affiliated organizations can support Beijing’s objectives through broader political messaging, including appeals for peace and dialogue that he interprets as encouraging acceptance of Chinese pressure at sea.
Powell views the teacher recall as political pressure that directs anger over disrupted lessons toward Beijing’s critics. But he said he had not seen the teachers’ return linked to any Philippine concession over the South China Sea.
Iannone said the available evidence required more careful distinctions.
“Before acting, authorities should separate a structural link, such as who trained a teacher, from conduct, such as what was taught, and publish what they find,” he said.
Lessons from the U.S. backlash
The controversy in the Philippines echoes concerns that drove a backlash against Confucius Institutes in the United States, but the mechanisms differ.
Confucius Institutes are Chinese government-backed partnerships with overseas universities that provide Chinese-language teaching and cultural programs. Their funding arrangements and ties to Beijing raised concerns in the United States about transparency, academic freedom and potential political influence on campuses.
A 2023 U.S. Government Accountability Office report found that the number of institutes at American universities and colleges had fallen from about 100 in 2019 to fewer than five today. Schools most commonly cited potential losses of federal funding and external pressure as contributing to closures. Many also reported reduced language-learning opportunities afterward.
Undergraduate student Moe Lewis, left, shows her watercolor painting of peony leaves at a traditional Chinese painting class at the Confucius Institute at George Mason University in Fairfax, Virginia, May 2, 2018.
(Matthew Pennington/AP) The Philippine teacher-placement programs involved in the recall are distinct from Confucius Institutes.
Iannone said the American experience can be seen primarily as a warning about how funding pressure and governance concerns can drive decisions even when allegations of misconduct remain unresolved.
He proposed a public register of educational agreements, funding and staffing covering every foreign government supporting Philippine education, alongside full local control over curriculum and hiring.
Funding alternatives would also be necessary, he said. Greater scrutiny alone would not solve schools’ dependence on overseas teachers.
“A more durable setup would train Filipino Mandarin teachers at home, draw on more than one partner – Taiwan included – and put every agreement on the public record,” he said.
Communities caught in the middle
The consequences could extend beyond disrupted classes.
Iannone warned that public debate could blur distinctions between Chinese state institutions, Chinese-language schools and people of Chinese heritage.
“What worries me more is how quickly the language slides, from PRC state bodies to ‘Chinese schools’ to ‘the Chinese,’” he said.
Teodoro, the most well-known Philippine government official who expressed concerns over the educational exchanges, prefaced them with a warning against xenophobia and said that the information the government had on the exchanges did not necessarily constitute wrongdoing.
A map showing the location of the five Confucius Institutes in the Philippines.
(RFA) But prolonged suspicion of China or Chinese could affect Filipinos who earned degrees in China, potentially damaging their careers if employers or institutions began treating their education as evidence of disloyalty,” Enrico Cau, a Taipei-based independent security researcher, told RFA.
He cautioned against assuming that changes in outlook after studying abroad necessarily resulted from organized political influence.
“Mindset shifts in those cases can result from spontaneous changes of mind, rather than from deliberate attempts to influence them,” he said.
Cau nevertheless considers a broad rupture unlikely. Educational exchanges form only one part of a relationship sustained by business networks, institutional connections and extensive personal ties, he said.
He described competing approaches within Philippine policy: a confrontational effort to check Chinese assertiveness and quieter diplomacy seeking to preserve economic and civilian relationships.
“These two souls seem to coexist in some way, producing a mix of constructive and dissonant results,” he said.
Powell said the recall could discourage oversight or prompt schools to seek different partners. He would not predict which outcome would prevail.
Iannone argued that preserving educational ties required arrangements able to withstand continued maritime confrontation.
“The influence concerns should be investigated properly, which means findings the public can actually read,” he said. “Otherwise the Philippines risks spending a great deal of political energy on Mandarin teachers while the harder problems at sea stay where they are.”
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Carrick to stay as Utd boss for Chelsea clash: reports
articles.excerpt: Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United for this weekend's Premier League match away to Chelsea…
articles.fullText:
Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United for this weekend's Premier League match away to Chelsea, according to media reports on Tuesday.

Carrick's future at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation after a miserable run of eight games without a win.

Sunday's 3-0 humbling at home to Bournemouth left the English giants just one point above the Premier League relegation zone.

But the BBC, Sky Sports and Britain's Press Association all reported that former United and England midfielder Carrick would take the team to Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

Carrick arrived at United's Carrington training ground on Tuesday to oversee a routine training session.

The BBC cited sources as saying the 45-year-old would be given a chance by the United hierarchy to turn things around.

Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after overseeing an impressive revival as caretaker boss following United's struggles under Ruben Amorim.

The club recovered to finish third in the Premier League, earning a return to the Champions League.

But United have won just two of 12 matches in all competitions so far this season, with a return of seven points from eight league games representing their worst start to a league season in 40 years.

Carrick avoided directly answering questions about his future following the Bournemouth loss.

The United boss acknowledged the crowd at full-time as fans chanted his name in a show of support for the beleaguered manager, but they vented their anger at the players and club hierarchy.

United great Wayne Rooney, who played alongside Carrick at Old Trafford, took aim at the players following a string of poor performances.

"The players haven't got a leg to stand on. What's not fair is the performances they are giving," he told the Stick to United podcast.

"I looked at the fans, you could see the pain and anger in their faces when those players are walking around the football pitch." (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Arsenal stunned in League Cup by fourth-tier Fleetwood
articles.excerpt: Arsenal suffered one of the most humiliating defeats in their history as the Premier League champions were stunned by fourth-tier…
articles.fullText:
Arsenal suffered one of the most humiliating defeats in their history as the Premier League champions were stunned by fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in a League Cup penalty shoot-out on Tuesday.

Mikel Arteta's side crashed out 5-3 on penalties in an incredible fourth round upset after the tie finished 1-1 in normal time.

Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes had his penalty saved by Jay Lynch in the shoot-out and Conor Haughey scored Fleetwood's winner.

Aaron Loupalo-Bi's first-half goal had put Fleetwood ahead before Viktor Gyokeres equalised after the interval.

Arsenal's 16-year-old rising star Max Dowman was sent off for violent conduct in the closing stages.

Arteta paid the price for prioritising Sunday's Premier League trip to Liverpool as his decision to make nine changes backfired spectacularly.

No one would have predicted Arsenal's embarrassment regardless of Arteta's selection gamble.

They had moved level on points with Premier League leaders Manchester City after a 2-0 victory over Everton on Saturday.

But instead of extending their run of 11 wins from their 13 previous games, Arsenal returned to north London red-faced after a loss that ranks among the darkest days in the club's glittering history.

Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor wept tears of joy as disbelieving fans flooded the pitch to celebrate their club's astonishing victory.

Only Myles Lewis-Skelly and Viktor Gyokeres kept their places from the Everton game, with teenagers Dowman and Marli Salmon starting, while 18-year-old winger Ceadach O'Neill made his debut.

Languishing in 18th place in League Two, Fleetwood had lost their previous two league games against Exeter and Cheltenham, yet they showed no signs of being intimidated by their illustrious visitors.

After an eight-minute delay due to an unauthorised drone flying over the stadium, Arsenal were caught cold on a windy night by the Irish Sea.

Fleetwood are nicknamed the 'Cod Army' in reference to the town's fishing industry, so it was somewhat fitting that a mistake from Salmon netted their opener in the 21st minute.

Salmon's lack of experience was brutally exposed when Loupalo-Bi muscled his way past the 17-year-old with ease, racing into the penalty area to plant a low finish past debutant keeper Illan Meslier.

Arsenal monopolised possession after that shock, but Arteta grew visibly agitated with their lack of cutting edge.

Arteta sent on Martin Odegaard at half-time and Gyokeres bagged Arsenal's equaliser five minutes later.

It was a scrappy effort that left Fleetwood feeling aggrieved as Gyokeres wrestled with his marker before poking O'Neill's ball past Lynch from close-range.

Dowman saw red in the 85th minute, dismissing for kicking out at Harrison Neal after a strong challenge from the Fleetwood midfielder.

Although it looked a harsh decision, Arteta was unimpressed with Dowman, giving him a stern word as the midfielder trudged off.

Both teams scored their first three penalties in the shoot-out, but Guimaraes was denied by Lynch and Haughey held his nerve to seal the biggest shock in League Cup history. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: The Download: Anthropic’s IPO, smarter power grids, and exercise pills
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in…
articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

Will the real Anthropic please stand up?

After weeks of frenzied speculation, Anthropic has filed its IPO prospectus. The 335-page document (100 pages or so are focused on risks) lays out the company’s unique view of the technology it is building and how it believes it will change the world.

But Anthropic has been honing its storytelling skills for years. Its public messaging is a master class in narrative capture, presenting it as different things to different people: an AI safety organization, a profit-driven megacorp, and a group hell-bent on creating superhuman technology.

These roles come with huge tensions. Will the IPO reveal the company behind the mask, or lean deeper into the myth-making? Take a new glimpse inside Anthropic .

—Will Douglas Heaven

This story is from The Algorithm, our weekly AI newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Monday.

How solid-state transformers could help power the AI boom

Transformers are a crucial but nearly invisible part of the US grid, helping efficiently move power across long distances. But they’re complicated and in short supply, and their basic design hasn’t changed much in about a century.

As electricity demand rises from EVs, data centers, and more, researchers and companies are looking to modernize these grid staples. Solid-state versions could help ease supply concerns and cut power losses.

The technology is still in development, but it could become a crucial part of our future grid.

Find out how solid-state transformers could help meet rising electricity demand .

—Casey Crownhart

Are we there yet? Exercise in a pill

We all know exercise is good for us. It builds muscle, strengthens bones, lowers blood pressure, and boosts mood. By deciphering how movement benefits the body, researchers hope to develop medicines that can offer some of the same perks, without the workout.

The idea isn’t to replace exercise but to bring its upsides to people who struggle with frailty, disability, or chronic illness.

Discover how close researchers are to developing an exercise pill .

—Cassandra Willyard

This story is part of “Are we there yet?” from the new Impossible issue of MIT Technology Review . The series takes stock of six technologies that have long promised to change the world—and scores them on a progress meter. Over the next six days, we’ll explore each one in The Download.

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 Anthropic has filed for its blockbuster IPO
The listing could determine the future of the AI investment boom. ( CNBC )
+ The filing warns of catastrophic AI risks and huge compute costs. ( BBC )
+ And exposes safety failures and a month-long training pause. ( Reuters $)

+ Microsoft plans $190 billion in AI spending this year. ( NYT $)

+ Here’s how tech transformed babymaking. ( MIT Technology Review )

10 Grok says its AI-generated Odyssey is “not historically accurate”
The bot itself admitted Elon Musk’s filmmaking plan has failed. ( Wired $)

Quote of the day

“It’s as if they’re making a promise and crossing their fingers behind their backs.”

—Kate Brennan, who leads policy at the AI Now Institute, tells the New York Times that the voluntary safety pledges AI executives recently made are toothless and unenforceable.

One more thing

MCKIBILLO

The problem with thinking you’re part Neanderthal

There’s a theory that many of us have an “inner Neanderthal.” The idea is that Homo sapiens and its cousin species once bred, leaving some people today with a trace of Neanderthal DNA.

This DNA is arguably the 21st century’s most celebrated discovery in human evolution. But in 2024, a pair of French geneticists called into question the theory’s very foundations.

They proposed that what scientists interpret as interbreeding could instead be explained by population structure—the way genes concentrate in smaller, isolated groups.

articles.title: Industrial Intelligence: The next growth opportunity for manufacturing
articles.excerpt: Every manufacturer has its own industrial intelligence. Some is documented, and some resides in the knowledge of experienced workers. Consider…
articles.fullText:
Every manufacturer has its own industrial intelligence. Some is documented, and some resides in the knowledge of experienced workers.

Consider an experienced operator preparing to restart a line after a changeover. The machine settings matter, but so does knowing how a particular material behaves, what happened during the previous shift, and when an apparently minor variation deserves a closer look. A procedure can describe the sequence, but successful execution depends on the judgment that comes from experience and the organization’s accumulated know-how.

That combination is industrial intelligence: a manufacturer’s accumulated know-how, operating practices, production data, and understanding of its own business.

The opportunity now is to make more of that intelligence available wherever decisions are made, then connect it to the physical world of manufacturing. The strategic destination is not more agents, but rather to turn the existing business intelligence into an engine for profitable growth.

Individual knowledge can be translated into organizational advantage

Expertise has limited reach when it stays with one person, inside one system, or within one plant. Leaders now must determine how to extend that reach without stripping away the context that makes the knowledge useful.

For example, an engineer evaluating a process change needs more than a production record. They need to understand the circumstances behind it: the equipment configuration, the quality requirements, and the trade-offs an operator made. Connecting those elements can help people apply experience beyond the place where it originated.

When individual knowledge becomes widely accessible, innovation can spread to the maintenance workshop, the planning office, the engineering team, and the production floor. More people can contribute because more people can work with what the organization knows.

But access to knowledge is only part of the opportunity. Manufacturing ultimately is physical, and it depends on materials, machines, and products.

When intelligence participates in action

Physical AI describes systems that can perceive conditions, reason about them, and take action within the physical world. By connecting machines and processes, manufacturers get a clearer view of what is happening on the factory floor. Agents can then reason on top of that information to identify patterns, predict problems, and determine the best course of action. Physical AI brings business intelligence into the physical process, allowing machines and systems to respond to changing conditions.

Consider a robotic-handling operation encountering variation in the parts arriving at its station. Vision can help the system assess a part’s position. A model informed by the material and task can help determine an appropriate movement. Connected controls can then execute an adjustment within validated limits. The value is not merely seeing the variation; it is responding appropriately.

The same principle applies to quality operations. When Toyota Industries connected previously fragmented paint shop data, engineering and operations teams were given the context needed to understand defect drivers. The company reports that analysis cycles fell from five days to under four hours, while its pilot reduced relevant paint defects by about 25%. The breakthrough was not simply identifying another signal; it was helping people understand why defects were occurring and respond before the outcome was locked in.

This is the type of situation where industrial intelligence has become essential. Data may reveal what is happening, but industrial intelligence provides the context for what should happen, which constraints cannot be breached, and when uncertainty requires human judgment.

Simulation offers a way to examine proposed actions before applying them to equipment. Manufacturers can explore how a change might affect a process in a digital environment. That does not remove the need for physical validation, but it creates room to learn without treating the production line as the first experiment.

Responsible deployment, therefore, begins with operational discipline. Leaders need to establish clear authority or what systems may change, reliable connections to equipment, defined safety boundaries, and a record of decisions and actions. People must be able to recognize uncertainty, intervene, and bring equipment to a safe state. Trust rests on those practical arrangements, not on confidence in a model alone.

More capable machines, more capable people

Manufacturing has long combined human ingenuity with increasingly capable tools. Physical AI extends that relationship. Intelligent equipment can take on suitable repetitive or physically demanding tasks, while agent-assisted operations can help people navigate information-intensive decisions and changing conditions.

The aim is not to make machines smarter; it is to see what people can build when knowledge can travel, intelligence can act, and ambition has more room to become reality.

Rockwell Automation illustrates the point. At its Singapore plant, technicians use a maintenance copilot that combines manufacturing data, machine manuals, and knowledge captured from experienced workers. This system has reduced the time required for new workers to learn how to troubleshoot hundreds of machines from nine months to three. An engineer could explore more process alternatives before committing to a change. An operator could help improve the system’s response rather than repeatedly managing the same exception.

This type of progress requires investment in equipment but also in people: training, time to learn, and playing a meaningful role in shaping how systems work. Machines become more capable so people can become more capable.

Industrial Intelligence is the answer to sustainable growth

Industrial intelligence connects what a manufacturer knows: the experience of its people, the signals from its operations, and the lessons accumulated over time. Physical AI gives that intelligence a way to act in the physical world, turning knowledge into decisions and decisions into action.

The next challenge for industry is not simply to produce more, but to grow without adding complexity at the same rate. Intelligence can help manufacturers turn experience into scalable capability—improving productivity, accelerating innovation, expanding capacity, and enabling people to solve problems that were previously difficult to tackle.

The next frontier of industry is not smarter machines or more automated factories; it is businesses that can continuously learn, adapt, and act. The opportunity is to turn the intelligence embedded in every operation into a compounding advantage for growth.

Watch the video series to learn how industrial customers are unlocking intelligence across the value chain, and join Microsoft at Microsoft Ignite to see what’s next for Industrial Intelligence.

articles.title: Foreign Ministry chides Mbappe over Mao comments
articles.excerpt: The Foreign Ministry in Beijing on Tuesday said that hurting the feelings of the country's people would meet "unanimous rejection"…
articles.fullText:
The Foreign Ministry in Beijing on Tuesday said that hurting the feelings of the country's people would meet "unanimous rejection" after football star Kylian Mbappe's comments about former leader Mao Zedong.

The French footballer's recent comments, in which he appeared to mock the founding leader of the People's Republic of China, resulted in two major Chinese brands dropping their sponsorship deals with the player.

"We have seen the relevant reports. Words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with unanimous rejection from all sectors of Chinese society," Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing.

"Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments," drinks giant Dongpeng said in a statement, adding that "with immediate effect we are terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe".

Mengniu, China's largest dairy producer, also cut ties with the Real Madrid forward.

Mbappe apologised for his comment in a statement put out later on Tuesday.

"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset.

"This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry." (Additional reporting by AFP)
