articles.title: Brewers rout Rays to reach brink of World Series sweep
articles.excerpt: With a devastating 16-hit batting performance and masterful pitching by Robert Gasser, the Milwaukee Brewers routed Tampa Bay 10-1 on…
articles.fullText:
With a devastating 16-hit batting performance and masterful pitching by Robert Gasser, the Milwaukee Brewers routed Tampa Bay 10-1 on Monday, reaching the brink of a World Series sweep.

Left-handed starter Gasser threw six shutout innings, allowing only one hit with a walk and three strikeouts in facing the minimum 18 batters.

"It was awesome," Gasser said.

"We're going to enjoy tonight. It was a great team win. But we've got work to do."

Jackson Chourio, a 22-year-old Venezuelan outfielder, went 4-for-5 at the plate, scored twice, stole a base and also drove in a run in the Brewers' historic eight-run fifth inning to humble the Rays.

All eight runs came with two outs in the inning, a World Series record, and Milwaukee batters made seven consecutive hits, a playoff first.

"It was special for sure," Chourio said through a translator.

"We've been preparing for this day. We've known it was coming. We have one more to lock in for tomorrow to complete the mission."

The Brewers seized a 3-0 lead in Major League Baseball's best-of-seven final and can win the first title in team history with a triumph in game four on Tuesday at Tropicana Field.

"There's still one more game to go for us to win," Gasser said.

"I know everybody is eager to do it and we're going to show up tomorrow ready to go."

Gasser became the first lefty to face the minimum over six innings in a World Series clash since Sandy Koufax of the Los Angeles Dodgers in 1965.

The Rays managed a run in the ninth but only three hits in the game.

Chourio raced home from second base on a Christian Yelich single in the third inning to score the first run and William Contreras drove in another with a hit to right field for a 2-0 lead.

The Brewers, whose only prior World Series was a 1982 loss to St. Louis in seven games, had two one-run wins to start the Series but overwhelmed Tampa Bay with a barrage in the fifth.

Chourio singled, stole second and advanced to third on a Contreras single that loaded the bases as Rays starter Freddy Peralta, who had played for Milwaukee the past eight seasons, was lifted for relief pitcher Cam Booser.

Brice Turang followed with a two-run single up the middle, Garrett Mitchell added a single to score Contreras, and Cooper Pratt followed with a two-run double to left field for a 7-0 Brewers lead.

Sal Frelick doubled in Pratt for an 8-0 Milwaukee edge, bringing on Rays reliever Cole Sulser, who promptly surrendered a single to David Hamilton to drive in Frelick for a 9-0 lead.

Chourio concluded the stunning streak with a double to right field to score Hamilton for a 10-0 Brewers lead.

Gasser, meanwhile, had to wait an extra 45 minutes before returning to the mound, watching the amazing streak with glee.

"It was special. I had a smile on my face the whole time," Gasser said.

"It was just surreal when something like that happens."

Chourio's eight hits through three games are the second-most in World Series history after nine by Billy Hatcher for Cincinnati in 1990.

"My mentality is to stay on top of the ball and hit line drives," Chourio said.

"I consider myself more of a hitter than a home run hitter."

Chourio became the youngest player to ever begin a World Series with three multi-hit games, delivering singles in the first, third and fifth innings on Monday. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Chinese industrial profits see sharp rise to 14.4pc
articles.excerpt: China's industrial profits grew at a faster pace in September, though a deepening divergence across the economy continued to weigh…
articles.fullText:
China's industrial profits grew at a faster pace in September, though a deepening divergence across the economy continued to weigh on business earnings.

Profits at industrial firms rose 14.4 percent from a year earlier last month, quickening from a 4.2 increase in August, data from the National Bureau of Statistics showed on Tuesday.

Profits were up 15.5 percent in the first nine months, compared with a 15.7 percent increase in the January-August period.

While export-oriented firms brace for greater uncertainty, as expanding trade surpluses heighten the risk of external pressures, firms tied to domestic demand continue to grapple with subdued consumption, casting a shadow over the sustainability of profit growth.

The sectoral divide remained pronounced.

Profits in the computer, communication, and other electronic equipment manufacturing category soared 103.8 percent in the first nine months, whereas the furniture manufacturing sector posted a 51.3 percent decline, making it one of the weakest performers and highlighting the uneven nature of China's economy.

A stronger-than-expected 4.5 percent expansion in the third quarter put China within reach of its annual growth target of 4.5 to five percent, but disparities across different parts of the economy suggest the recovery remains unbalanced, with persistent weakness in some sectors continuing to erode corporate profitability.

That pressure has become increasingly visible at the company level.

Net profit at the world's largest electric vehicle battery maker, CATL, slowed sharply in the past quarter, as intense competition in the EV battery market squeezed margins at a time when China's auto sales were in a downturn.

Industrial profit figures cover firms with yearly revenue of at least 20 million yuan from main operations. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Kane, Putellas win top honours at 2026 Ballon d'Or
articles.excerpt: Harry Kane became England's first Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years in his native city of London on Monday, beating…
articles.fullText:
Harry Kane became England's first Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years in his native city of London on Monday, beating out stiff competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

Alexia Putellas claimed the women's prize for a third time to extend Spain's domination of the award, thanks to her role in leading Barcelona to last season's Champions League before moving to London City Lionesses.

The first ever Ballon d'Or ceremony on English soil got off to an inauspicious start as the London traffic caused a delay of nearly an hour, with many of the star names arriving late.

But there was a happy ending for the hometown hero as Kane collected the crowning glory of his career to date.

The 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double.

He also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup.

"Without you guys (his Bayern Munich teammates) and the rest of the team it wouldn't be possible, the way you guys push me, the way we compete. So thank you very much," he said after collecting the award.

Kane's medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs since he arrived at Bayern in 2023.

He was on the losing side for Tottenham in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and twice tasted bitter defeat in the final of the European Championship with England.

But his remarkable goalscoring consistency has earned him the highest individual award in football.

"Making the move to Bayern Munich was a big step in my career," Kane told AFP earlier. "Some people saw it as a risk but for me it was always about improving and seeing if I could get better around the teammates, the team, the club and it has pushed me onto another level.

"Being a number nine for Bayern and England you are expected to score goals and to do that the number of times I did last year is something I'm really proud of," he added.

Winner in 2021 and 2022, Putellas's third Ballon d'Or caps her return back to the top of the women's game after an anterior cruciate ligament injury derailed her rise four years ago.

Putellas succeeds Spain teammate Aitana Bonmati, the winner the past three years who was sidelined by a leg break for most of last season.

"Ever since I suffered the injury, I've been trying to enjoy every moment as if it were my last, because you never know if it'll happen again," Putellas told AFP in an interview last month.

"I never felt that the (Ballon d'Or) trophy was 'mine'... Having already experienced it once, I'm able to enjoy it even more now," she added.

Yamal made the boldest fashion statement of the contenders with a pink flower on the front of his black suit.

The Barcelona winger scooped up the first award of the night for young talent of the year for the third consecutive time.

But the 19-year-old fell short of becoming the youngest ever Ballon d'Or winner after he failed to produce his best form during Spain's World Cup success.

Mbappe got the better of Yamal with two goals as Real Madrid edged Barcelona 2-1 in El Clasico on Sunday.

But his wait to win the Ballon d'Or goes on despite his prolific year for France and Real Madrid.

Luis de la Fuente beat out Paris Saint-Germain's Luis Enrique and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to be named men's coach of the year after leading Spain to World Cup glory.

"I'm really privileged to work with a team of such high quality on a professional and human level," said de la Fuente.

Barcelona's Pere Romeu scooped the prize for women's coach of the year.

Arsenal's Bukayo Saka won the Socrates award for his humanitarian work.

Paris Saint-Germain missed out on any of the main individual awards despite winning a second consecutive Champions League, but did have the consolation of men's club of the year.

Spanish duo Unai Simon and Cata Coll were named best men's and women's goalkeeper. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Online post purportedly by Chinese students calls for restoring term limits for Xi
articles.excerpt: Letter appeared on website registered in South Korea with Singapore mailing address, RFA investigation reveals.
articles.fullText:
Updated on Oct. 27, 2026 at 3:45 p.m. ET
Read a version of this story in Chinese
An “open letter” purportedly signed by students from multiple Chinese universities appeared on a Chinese language website on Monday, calling for the restoration of term limits for the Chinese president, but an investigation by Radio Free Asia was not able to determine if it originated from within China.
The letter, which was no longer accessible on Tuesday, had also called for the promotion of democratic constitutional amendments and the guarantee of space for citizens to discuss national affairs, appeared the same day as the opening of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party, or CCP.
RFA’s investigation revealed that the “Siyuan Lake BBS” website hosting the message listed “KR” as its country/region code, indicating South Korea, in its registration information. Its mailing address was listed as “16 Collyer Quay,” a skyscraper in Singapore’s central business district. The administrator’s email address was registered on a server of Chinese tech giant Tencent.
Based on the above information, RFA was unable to determine whether the Chinese language website is located within China. As for which organization or company manages it, this cannot be verified at present.
A Radio Free Asia investigation revealed the website to be registered to a Singapore address in South Korea.
(ICANN Lookup) The “open letter,” posted at 3:18 p.m., was titled “A Joint Appeal from a Group of University Students in the Republic.” It was addressed to the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress, and members of the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, and was written against the backdrop of commemorating the 160th anniversary of the birth of Sun Yat-sen, the founder of modern China at the end of its last imperial dynasty.
The article cites past statements by Sun Yat-sen, Mao Zedong, and Deng Xiaoping regarding democracy, oversight of power, and leadership systems, and questions China’s 2018 constitutional amendment that removed the two-term limit for the president and vice president, paving the way for Xi’s third term as president, which began in 2023.
The letter argues that political stability should stem from predictability in the system and advocates for “limiting the time limit on power and subjecting it to oversight.”
Three Main Demands
The open letter put forward three main expectations:
Restore Term Limits: Abolish the indefinite extension of the term of office for the President of the People’s Republic of China and restore the term limits explicitly stipulated in the Constitution to ensure the orderly transfer of power; clear term limits should also be established for the highest leadership positions of the Party.
Initiate Democratic Constitutional Amendment: Convene a national constitutional amendment conference, steadily and gradually expand the people’s substantive participation in public power, improve the election, supervision, and recall mechanisms, and put into practice the unfinished goal since the 1911 Xinhai Revolution—returning power to the people—step by step.
Safeguard Space for Public Discussion: Safeguard the space for citizens to discuss national affairs in accordance with the law, encourage young people of the Republic to speak the truth, and listen to criticism as well-intentioned suggestions.
The article also states:
“We have no intention of confrontation, much less to create antagonism. We are just a group of young people who grew up reading Dr. Sun Yat-sen’s last words, and with the sentiment that ‘the revolution has not yet succeeded, comrades must continue to strive,’ we are willing to fulfill the responsibility of a scholar for the long-term future of this country.”
Unverified signatures and origin
The post lists 14 universities, including Peking University, Renmin University of China, Tongji University, Xi’an Jiaotong University, Xiamen University, and Nankai University, and notes that the petition is ongoing. However, the list only includes the names of the universities and does not provide any individual signatures or proof of signature.
An online post on Oct. 26, 2026, purportedly by Chinese students calls for restoring term limits for Chinese President Xi Jinping.
(RFA Mandarin) As of midnight Beijing time on October 27, the website showed that this article had only been viewed by 656 people and received 1 like. The author on the page is listed as “Lin Ziyi,” with an account level of “LV.1.” The website indicates that this is “Lin Ziyi’s” first article. The article does not provide the names, number, contact information, or other verifiable information of the students who signed the article.
RFA has not independently confirmed the author’s identity, whether the signatories are indeed students, or whether students from the listed schools actually participated.
The website is divided into several topics, with the “Open Letter” posted in the “Complaints and Casual Chat” section. The website is entirely in simplified Chinese and appears to be a typical campus job search or lifestyle information website.
A closer look
The bottom of the page states that it is a “non-official campus forum,” and a closer look reveals that its URL ends with “.com” instead of the usual “.cn” which is China’s internet domain.
Radio Free Asia further investigated the website’s registration information and found that the IP address used by the website was “43.155.168.161”. Further verification with ICANN revealed that the website’s registration information showed the “country/region” code as “KR”, which corresponds to South Korea. The mailing address was listed as “16 Collyer Quay” in Singapore, but the administrator’s email address was registered on a Tencent server (@tencent.com), and the mobile phone number and WeChat account left by the administrator were also Chinese numbers.
A Radio Free Asia investigation revealed the website to be registered to a Singapore address in South Korea.
(ICANN Lookup) ‘Conscience of intellectuals’
While the authenticity of the petition remains to be verified, its content reflects the conscience of intellectuals, Taiwan’s Mainland Affairs Council Minister Chiu Chui-cheng said at the Legislative Yuan on Tuesday.
Chiu also recalled that as early as 2017, Chinese scholars had expressed their opposition to Xi Jinping’s disruption of the leadership succession system.
At that time, the Chinese scholars stated bluntly, “We, the intellectuals of mainland China, absolutely cannot accept this re-election,” referring to a provision that granted him a second term under conditions that would allow him to serve a third in 2023. They indicated that if the leadership succession system were undermined, 95% of Chinese intellectuals would oppose it.
However, Chiu said that as the CCP later established a “one-man rule” leadership structure, the mechanism for intellectuals to correct their mistakes has “completely disappeared.”
Edited by Charlie Dharapak and Eugene Whong.
Update adds Chiu’s comments to the Legislative Yuan and information about the website’s disappearance.

articles.title: Kim Jong Un’s unprecedented day-trip to China shatters Pyongyang’s Korean War myths
articles.excerpt: Visit to army memorial acknowledges China’s role in the war, downplayed by North Korea’s version of history.
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Korean
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un’s weekend visit to China over the newly completed New Yalu River Bridge was largely symbolic, and acknowledged a history that Pyongyang has downplayed for three generations, experts told Radio Free Asia.
North Korea is drawing closer to China and Russia while keeping the U.S. at arm’s length. Kim Jong Un’s one-day trip to China is the latest sign.
During Saturday’s unprecedented one-day car trip to Dandong, China, across the border from North Korea’s northwestern city of Sinuiju, Kim inspected a bus factory, met with high-ranking Chinese officials, and visited a monument that commemorated China’s entry into the Korean War.
The timing was significant. The visit was on the eve of the 76th anniversary of the Chinese People’s Volunteer Army’s Oct. 25, 1950 first combat against South Korean and U.N. forces in the war, which would rage on for another three years as the Chinese-backed North and U.S. and U.N. backed South fought to what is largely considered to be a stalemate.
The state-run Korean Central News Agency noted that after Kim and the North Korean delegation toured the Memorial Hall of the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea, and paid their respects, he told the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference Chairman Wang Huning – the fourth highest ranked official in the Chinese Communist Party – that it was North Korea’s duty to remember the sacrifice of the Chinese army.
“It was a moment to recollect the preciousness of the DPRK-China friendship forged at the cost of blood,” the report attributed him as saying. “We will always remember the history when the excellent sons and daughters of the Chinese people helped our revolution at the cost of their blood and steadily and firmly carry forward the history of the DPRK-China friendship,” Kim said, in the report.
Though international media outlets characterized Kim’s day trip to be an effort to expand trade ties between Pyongyang and Beijing, the visit to the memorial hall was the most important part of the itinerary, Ri Jong Ho, who was once a high-ranking North Korean official but escaped to the South and currently lives in the U.S., told RFA.
“A bridge that stayed closed for twelve years opened only days before Kim crossed it, and on the same day the supreme leader stood before a history his regime has avoided for more than seventy years,” said Ri, questioning whether that was a coincidence or pressure from Beijing, which financed the majority of the new bridge, which lay in a state of near-completion since 2014 before finally opening for trade traffic on Oct. 15.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, left, poses with Wang Huning, China's fourth highest-ranking official, in front of the New Yalu River Bridge that connects Dandong, China with Sinuiju, North Korea, Oct. 24, 2026.
(KCNA via KNS/AFP) There is a consensus among historians that North Korea’s survival in the Korean War was due to Beijing deploying troops to aid Pyongyang, but the story is different inside North Korea.
According to that version of history, the North Korean military under the tactical genius of Kim Jong Un’s grandfather, national founder Kim Il Sung – with only minimal support from China – was able to stave off defeat against an overwhelming force led by the U.S.
This narrative was important from Pyongyang to maintain because it aligns with the country’s founding Juche ideology of self-reliance.
“Pyongyang will present the photographs as proof of an unbreakable friendship. But those inside the Kim system will see something else: the third Kim leader, bowing in public before a history his grandfather and father suppressed,” said Ri.
“Like-minded totalitarians”
Kim’s visit to Dandong is significant because of the timing, but it is more about managing China’s concerns that North Korea is getting too close to Russia, Sydney Seiler, a senior advisor for the Korea Chair at the Washington-based Center for Strategic & International Studies, told RFA.
“Kim is acting with limited confidence, embracing like-minded totalitarian, autocratic … partners such as Russia and China while ignoring the United States, at least for now,” said Seiler. “Kim is working in a ‘safe zone’ between Moscow and Beijing, ensuring that neither side is overly concerned with Pyongyang’s relations with the other, yet still watching to see if and when national interests are threatened.”
He said that at the moment, it is not likely that any moves by Kim and Chinese President Xi Jinping to strengthen their relationship would concern Putin.
“But the opposite is not necessarily true. If Russia’s support to the DPRK enables, empowers, emboldens, and eventually encourages Kim to consider scenarios of even limited use of force toward the ROK, then the PRC will be concerned,” he said, using abbreviations for the official names of South Korea and China. “Kim getting close to the Chinese may be designed to mitigate such concerns.”
But the trip could also be the result of pressure on Kim to finally open the New Yalu River Bridge – and his country, Ri said.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un heading home via the China-North Korea Yalu River Bridge after concluding his visit to China in Dandong, Liaoning province.
(KCNA via KNS/AFP) “I believe Chinese leaders, resentful of the neglected bridge, kept pressing him to open it, and a severe economic crisis left North Korea little choice but to unlock the gate,” he said. “The bridge is open, but I suspect Kim’s fear of opening up, and of the outside information that comes with it, remains deep.”
Ri noted that the bridge had been the vision of Jang Song Thaek, the uncle of Kim Jong Un who supported North Korean economic development through close cooperation with China. Jang in 2009 negotiated to get Beijing to finance the bridge while serving in the regime of Kim Jong Un’s father, Kim Jong Il. Jang’s pro-China views caused him to fall out of favor with the younger Kim and he was executed by firing squad in the early years of his rule following his father’s death.
Message to Washington?
The fact that Kim was able to get into a car and drive to China is intended to point out the lack of effectiveness of sanctions, Hong Min, a senior research fellow at the Seoul-based Korea Institute for National Unification, told RFA.
“The trip implies that ‘one-day shuttle diplomacy’ is possible,” said Hong. “North Korea and China intend to continue close strategic communication regardless of sanctions, and it is a signal that sanctions can effectively be rendered meaningless.”
Because Kim’s visit involved many important officials on both sides, commentators in Seoul and Korea observers raised the possibility that the purpose was for the two countries to coordinate before U.S. President Donald Trump is scheduled to travel to Shenzhen, China for the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting, and the potential for a summit with Kim while he is in the region.
Ri noted that this was not confirmed and said this kind of meeting would shatter North Korea’s established internal narratives.
“For decades, Pyongyang has preached self-reliance, or juche , and insisted that it bows to no foreign power,” he said. “If its leader must first seek Beijing’s permission before sitting down with an American president, that principle would be hollowed out.”
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, right, shaking hands with Wang Huning, the fourth highest ranked member of the Chinese Communist Party in Dandong, China, Oct. 24, 2026.
(KCNA via KNS/AFP) Ri noted that Kim met with Xi Jinping himself prior to his first summit with Trump in 2018. This time he met only with “China’s No. 4.”
Such a posture would resemble a provincial lord seeking an emperor’s approval,” he said. “An ideology that taught North Koreans for three generations to despise sadae , deference to the powerful, would stand exposed as a slogan.”
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: HK aviation 'key lies in cooperation with Greater Bay'
articles.excerpt: Lawmaker Kenneth Fok called on the government on Monday to enhance cooperation with the Greater Bay Area to further enhance…
articles.fullText:
Lawmaker Kenneth Fok called on the government on Monday to enhance cooperation with the Greater Bay Area to further enhance Hong Kong’s status as an international aviation hub.

The call was among recommendations proposed by the G19 bloc of Legislative Council members.

Fok said the suggestions were made as total passenger throughput at Hong Kong International Airport had yet to get back to pre-pandemic levels.

“Compared to our competitors around the region, for example Shenzhen and Guangzhou, we are actually behind in this number,” he said.

Fok called for more collaboration between airports in the region, adding that regional collaboration had become a norm.

“I think the key is to have more collaborative effort with our regional airports and especially the Greater Bay Area,” he said.

“Can we join hands with them together in some kind of agreement between Hong Kong and mainland and then negotiate with our partners in Europe and elsewhere?

“These are the collaborative discussions that can only happen at the government-to-government level. This is very important.

"That's why I say we need to have a more open mind, a more aggressive strategy in order to implement these frameworks and strategies.”

Fok added the government could be more proactive in pitching the airport to the world to attract more foreign airlines.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: China congratulates Lula on re-election
articles.excerpt: China on Monday congratulated Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on his re-election, even as challenger Flavio Bolsonaro refused…
articles.fullText:
China on Monday congratulated Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on his re-election, even as challenger Flavio Bolsonaro refused to accept defeat.

"China has noted that Brazil's Superior Electoral Court has announced President Lula has won the second round of the Brazilian general election, and expresses its congratulations," Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said at a regular briefing, adding that Beijing was "willing to work with Brazil to continue advancing the building of a China-Brazil community with a shared future".

Asked about Bolsonaro saying he would request an annulment of the elections, Guo said: "China respects the choice of the Brazilian people."

Leftist leaders from across the Americas also congratulated Lula on his re-election.

Mexico's President Claudia Sheinbaum celebrated Lula's win in a post on X, saying: "Long live democracy, the people of Brazil won."

Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel congratulated Lula on his "historic victory that guarantees the continuity of the path of peace, sovereignty, and social justice".

Argentina's former president Cristina Kirchner, who is currently under house arrest for corruption, said on X that the Brazilian leader "knew how to awaken in his compatriots the feeling and sense needed to win".

Uruguay's President Yamandu Orsi said on X that he had spoken with Lula and "congratulated him on his victory and on the democratic celebration that an electoral process represents."

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who is the current chair of the Brics geopolitical and economic bloc, which includes Brazil, offered Lula his "heartiest congratulations."

"I look forward to working closely with him to further deepen and expand the multifaceted India-Brazil Strategic Partnership," he added.

French President Emmanuel Macron also congratulated Lula on his re-election, calling for efforts to "strengthen our strategic partnership".

"France and Brazil have much to build together," Macron said X, saying their two countries should nurture their friendship "in the service of a fairer world".

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez celebrated the Brazilian leader's re-election victory as launching a "progressive comeback", as he trails in polls before Spain's November vote.

European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen hailed Lula's re-election victory as a win for "democracy and multilateralism".

"Europe's partnership with Brazil is thriving. We will remain by your side for the years to come. Together we will keep working closely for free and open trade. A rules-based global order. And strong ambitions for our climate," she wrote on social media.

Lula received 51.8 percent of the vote compared with 48.2 percent for Bolsonaro.

Bolsonaro said he would seek to annul the vote.

Sunday's vote was marked by confusion after a Supreme Court ruling extended voting by two hours as some polling stations had already closed.

The move came at the request of Lula who complained that buses had been pulled from circulation in various cities, barring citizens from voting.

Bolsonaro also requested an extension in some regions due to heavy rains, but he described the decision as "unacceptable" and a "dirty trick".

"It is impossible to recognise the results. I am going to request the annulment of these elections," he said, stone-faced, in a brief speech in Brasilia. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Athletes honoured for historic Asian Games performance
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong, China’s top-performing athletes at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games were commended by Chief Executive John Lee on Monday for…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong, China’s top-performing athletes at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games were commended by Chief Executive John Lee on Monday for their historic performances.

The SAR achieved its best result to date at the Games in Japan, reaching new heights in both the gold medal count and the number of medals won overall.

In total, the delegation won 54 medals, comprising 11 gold, 19 silver, and 24 bronze.

Lee paid tribute to athletes during a commendation ceremony, noting that their dedication to compete through injuries and persevere when falling behind had earned everyone’s deepest respect.

He also presented certificates to the top-performing athletes, including wushu star Lydia Sham, who earned the city's first gold medal at the Games.

Lee stressed the government would continue to invest in sports development.

“During the 2026–27 financial year, the government’s resources invested in sports development reached about HK$8.1 billion, nearly a 70 percent increase compared to a decade ago,” he said.

“We allocated about HK$1 billion to the Hong Kong Sports Institute, providing comprehensive training, direct financial subsidies, and support in sports medicine and sports science.

“The government will continue to support the development of sports medicine and sports science, athlete training, and their career development. In the next five years, resources allocated to sports development will cumulatively increase by 20 percent,” Lee added.

Chief Secretary Eric Chan, Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism Rosanna Law, President of the Sports Federation & Olympic Committee of Hong Kong, China, Timothy Fok, among others, also attended the ceremony.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Ex-Japan prime minister Yasuo Fukuda dies
articles.excerpt: Former Japanese prime minister Yasuo Fukuda, who used his brief period in office to seek closer ties with Asian neighbours…
articles.fullText:
Former Japanese prime minister Yasuo Fukuda, who used his brief period in office to seek closer ties with Asian neighbours, particularly China, has died at the age of 90, the Nikkei business daily reported on Monday.

Beijing expressed condolences over his passing.

The Japanese politician, the first son of a prime minister to become premier himself, died on Thursday from heart failure, the Nikkei said.

Becoming prime minister on the sudden resignation of Shinzo Abe in 2007, Fukuda lasted less than a year – a tenure even shorter than his father Takeo's two-year stint.

A graduate in economics from Tokyo's prestigious Waseda University, Fukuda spent nearly two decades working his way up the ranks of an oil company – including a two-year posting in the United States – before resigning to become a political secretary when his father became premier in 1976.

Elected to Japan's more powerful lower house of parliament in 1990, Fukuda was chief cabinet secretary from 2000 to 2004, resigning as one of several cabinet ministers to admit not paying into the pension system.

Known for his testy manner, the bespectacled Fukuda drew criticism in 2003 for off-the-record comments in which he suggested women who dressed provocatively were asking to be raped.

When Fukuda succeeded Abe he joked he might have drawn the short straw in assuming office given the divided parliament and opposition parties' ability to delay legislation.

Frustrated with the stalled legislative process, Fukuda resigned in 2008, the second of six prime ministers to quit after only around a year in office.

Known as a diplomatic dove, Fukuda made several visits to China after leaving office in an effort to improve often fraught relations.

Speaking at a regular briefing on Monday, Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun called Fukuda an old friend of the Chinese people who held the "correct view" of history.

Guo praised him for making significant contributions to the development of bilateral relations, citing the China-Japan Joint Statement on All-round Promotion of Strategic Relationship of Mutual Benefit that was issued in 2008 when he was prime minister.

Fukuda leaves a son, Tatsuo, who is also a lawmaker and has been viewed as a potential future prime minister. (Reuters/RTHK)

articles.title: Xi opens Party plenum on governance
articles.excerpt: President Xi Jinping opened the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC)…
articles.fullText:
President Xi Jinping opened the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) in Beijing on Monday.

Xi, who is also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, delivered a work report on behalf of the Politburo and explained a draft decision by the Central Committee on major issues concerning strengthening Party self-governance.

The draft decision summarises the achievements and experience of full and rigorous Party self-governance in the new era in a truth-seeking manner, and offers in-depth analysis of the situation and tasks concerning Party building at present and for the future.

It also sets out strategic plans for strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance, according to a Politburo meeting in September that submitted the document to the plenum for review.

The plenary session will last till Thursday.

The fifth plenum comes ahead of a major Party congress next year, where Xi is expected to oversee a leadership reshuffle.

State media published an article ahead of the gathering, based on a speech Xi gave in January in which he railed against "two-faced" officials who appear to comply with central directives but "inwardly resist", pursue "individualism" and are "politically opportunistic". (Xinhua/AFP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Doncic erupts for 52 as Lakers maintain perfect start
articles.excerpt: Luka Doncic scored a monster 52 points as the Los Angeles Lakers maintained their perfect start to life after LeBron…
articles.fullText:
Luka Doncic scored a monster 52 points as the Los Angeles Lakers maintained their perfect start to life after LeBron James with a 132-123 win over the Utah Jazz.

Now the undisputed superstar of the Lakers since James departed this summer for Philadelphia, Doncic also provided 10 assists and eight rebounds in a masterful performance, with eight three-pointers and two steals.

Doncic was supported by Austin Reaves, who had 29 points, as the visitors pulled decisively clear in the last four minutes of a game they had trailed for long periods.

"It's one of the best feelings... down the stretch, tight game, hitting those threes," said Doncic.

"Played the basketball we know how to play. We are learning our lesson...we cannot start games like this any more."

It was the first 50-point game by an NBA player this season. Slovenian point guard Doncic was the league's top scorer last season.

After cruising to comfortable opening wins against the Golden State Warriors and city rival Clippers, the Lakers overcame their first real adversity of the nascent season in Salt Lake City.

Utah led nearly the entire first half, pulling as many as 18 points clear, with Finland's Lauri Markkanen on scintillating form.

But the Lakers rallied. A Doncic three-point pull-up shot with seconds remaining in the second quarter gave Los Angeles a slender lead at the interval.

The Jazz had inched back in front with just over four minutes remaining, when another Doncic trey tied up the score 116-116.

From there Doncic and Reaves were relentless, outscoring the entire Jazz offence in the final quarter between them, as the new-look Lakers moved to a perfect 3-0 start.

"We have a tight group. I think everybody new that came, they feel very welcome here. That's what we want," said Doncic. (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: Antonelli on brink of title with US Grand Prix victory
articles.excerpt: Kimi Antonelli moved to within striking distance of his first world championship title as he powered to an emphatic victory…
articles.fullText:
Kimi Antonelli moved to within striking distance of his first world championship title as he powered to an emphatic victory at the US Grand Prix in Austin on Sunday.

It was his ninth win of the season and with his only rivals Mercedes teammate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finishing eighth and fourth respectively, the 20-year-old Italian needs just to come in ninth in next week's race in Mexico to become the youngest ever Formula One champion.

He is also set to become the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

Antonelli finished over 13 seconds ahead of the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc with Red Bull's Max Verstappen completing the podium.

Antonelli started the race in pole position and after a clean start already had a 2sec lead by the end of the opening lap, at which point the result never seemed in doubt, mechanical failure and pit stop disasters notwithstanding.

Verstappen was beaten off the start by Leclerc, who started in third, but the four-time world champion wasted no time in reclaiming second spot. Leclerc, however, overtook him in the latter part of the race and Verstappen was left hanging on for third as Hamilton also closed.

Antonelli would have become the youngest ever champion, smashing the current record of Sebastian Vettel who was 23 years and 133 days when he won his fist title in 2010, if Russell had finished lower than eighth and Hamilton failed to make the top four.

Russell, who has had some terrible luck all season, was hit with a 5sec penalty for running off the track on the opening lap and struggled to get past McLaren's Oscar Piastri who came in seventh.

Lando Norris, the outgoing champion, was running second until the closing laps when his tyres appeared to give up and he had to settle for fifth with Isack Hadjar sixth in the second Red Bull. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Mbappe double helps Real down Barca in Clasico
articles.excerpt: Kylian Mbappe struck twice to earn Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid a 2-1 Clasico victory over La Liga leaders Barcelona on…
articles.fullText:
Kylian Mbappe struck twice to earn Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid a 2-1 Clasico victory over La Liga leaders Barcelona on Sunday at Camp Nou, cutting the gap to three points.

French superstar Mbappe opened the scoring before the interval and then slotted home late on to inflict Barca's first domestic defeat of the campaign after Raphinha had equalised for the champions.

Real Madrid remain third, behind Atletico Madrid and Hansi Flick's Barca, who had won their first nine games before a chastening week.

The Catalans suffered a second straight defeat after losing on Tuesday against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League.

Mourinho was delighted with his team's display in his first Clasico back at the helm of Madrid.

"My team had an extraordinary game, very organised, good concentration, with courage to play out from the back against a team that presses you a lot," Mourinho told reporters.

"We had chances for the second goal... obviously Barca had a strong reaction but we were calm and organised and at 1-1 we never lost our tranquility."

Barca had won six of the seven previous Clasicos since Flick arrived but were surprisingly subdued against Mourinho's side.

"In general we didn't have a great game, in the first half we weren't ourselves, there were a lot of things we could have done better," Barcelona midfielder Pedri told DAZN.

"We wanted to win the Clasico in front of our fans, but the season is very long... a league is not won here."

Los Blancos, without suspended winger Vinicius Junior, won their fifth straight game across all competitions and are finding their footing under veteran Portuguese coach Mourinho.

After two trophyless seasons Madrid turned back to Mourinho to try and stop Barca's dominance, and this result will give them hope they are on the right track.

The opening period of the game was cagey, with few opportunities.

Barca defender Pau Cubarsi twice reacted well to shut down Mbappe, while Real Madrid's Marc Cucurella took a rapid liking for Lamine Yamal's shirt, constantly grabbing at the 19-year-old winger.

Anthony Gordon, playing in his first Clasico since joining Barcelona from Newcastle, backheeled the ball to Raphinha, who fired narrowly wide as Barca threatened.

The hosts were dealt a setback when young defender Xavi Espart pulled up hurt and needed to be replaced by Alejandro Balde before the half-hour mark.

Andriy Lunin, playing in goal for Madrid after Thibaut Courtois pulled out of the squad with flu, saved at his near post from Gordon before the visitors took the lead.

Mbappe scored his 10th league goal of the season and also his easiest, with Barca's Gerard Martin clearing a cross straight at the Frenchman, who deflected it into the net.

Barca responded by carving out a glorious chance for an equaliser but teenage sensation Yamal for once miscued in front of goal, firing wide when poised to level.

The game opened up and Yan Diomande came close to doubling Madrid's lead before half-time, drilling into the side-netting.

Martin redeemed himself early in the second half as he held off Jude Bellingham, who could neither beat the defender nor find a free Mbappe.

Raphinha, who had a quiet first half, pulled Barcelona level just after the hour mark.

Pedri fed the Brazilian, La Liga's top goalscorer with 13, who fired through Bellingham's legs and Lunin could not keep the shot out.

The Ukrainian goalkeeper did make a superb save to deny Martin at a corner, as Barcelona flowed forward with the wind finally in their sails.

Yamal bent an effort wide with Lunin at full stretch and Barca substitute Frenkie de Jong had a shot desperately blocked by Dean Huijsen.

There was a sting in the tail for the Catalans though as substitute Gabriel Jesus lost possession and Madrid raced through on goal.

Eduardo Camavinga beat Cubarsi and unselfishly cut the ball back for Mbappe to tuck home his second of the night into an empty net with Joan Garcia drawn out of position.

It brought up a century of goals since Mbappe joined Madrid from PSG in 2024, although the trophies to match have not yet followed. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Man United lose again as Liverpool climb to fourth
articles.excerpt: Michael Carrick was pushed to the brink of being sacked after Manchester United slumped to a miserable 3-0 home defeat…
articles.fullText:
Michael Carrick was pushed to the brink of being sacked after Manchester United slumped to a miserable 3-0 home defeat against Bournemouth, while Alexander Isak extended his hot streak in Liverpool's 2-0 win against Brighton on Sunday.

Carrick's bold decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes backfired as defeat stretched United's winless run to eight games and left them 16th in the Premier League, just one point above the relegation zone.

For the third time in four seasons, the Cherries won by a three-goal margin at Old Trafford as strikes from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson secured a fully deserved victory for Marco Rose's side.

Fernandes was critical of Carrick's tactics in a 4-1 Champions League thrashing at Como on Wednesday.

The United boss said the decision to leave out last season's Premier League Player of the Year was a "purely football" driven, but it was hard to believe Fernandes was not being punished as he was left on the bench for the entire match.

Carrick was taunted with chants of "you're getting sacked in the morning" from the Bournemouth fans.

But on this evidence, dismissing another manager is far from a quick fix for a club that has fallen dramatically from grace since Alex Ferguson's retirement after winning their most recent English title 13 years ago.

A strong finish to last season during Carrick's interim spell in charge secured third place in the Premier League.

Yet with just one win against promoted Ipswich, United have taken just seven points from eight league games so far this season – their lowest tally at this stage of a season since 1986-87.

United's players were booed off by the few frustrated fans that remained inside Old Trafford at the end of their heaviest home defeat since 2024.

United's co-owners the Glazer family and Jim Ratcliffe were also targeted for angry chants, although Carrick largely avoided the fans' ire.

It is unlikely that sympathy vote will spare the former United midfielder from the axe.

At Anfield, Liverpool struck twice in quick succession in the first half, with Pascal Gross's own goal followed by Isak's latest strike.

Isak has netted six times in seven league games this season and has three goals in his last four matches.

After a turbulent debut season following his acrimonious move from Newcastle, the Sweden striker is finally beginning to repay his £125 million fee.

It was a welcome first taste of top-flight success at Anfield for Reds boss Andoni Iraola, who had failed to win his first three league games on Merseyside since arriving from Bournemouth in the close season.

The Spaniard, who had won Champions League and League Cup games at Anfield, has led Liverpool to four successive victories in all competitions since the chastening 3-0 home defeat against Manchester City.

Liverpool have climbed to fourth place, just one point behind third-placed Brighton after inflicting the high-flying Seagulls' second league loss this term.

The rampant Reds are six points behind leaders City as they eye a potential title challenge.

William Osula and Harvey Barnes scored in the second half as Newcastle piled pressure on Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage with a 2-0 win at Selhurst Park.

Thrashed 5-0 at rivals Brighton last weekend, 17th-placed Palace have won just twice in eight league games under Sage, who arrived from Lens in the close season to replace Oliver Glasner.

Hull's unbeaten home record remains intact but the Tigers have not tasted victory for seven games after a 1-1 draw with Brentford at the MKM Stadium.

Oli McBurnie's 24th-minute penalty, awarded when Aaron Hickey fouled Tim Iroegbunam, put Hull ahead, but Dango Ouattara equalised in the 63rd minute.

Elsewhere on the pitch, Sunderland hosted Leeds to a 0-0 draw. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Ensure smooth flow at boundary checkpoints: CS
articles.excerpt: Chief Secretary Eric Chan on Sunday instructed government departments to ensure the smooth flow of travellers at boundary control points…
articles.fullText:
Chief Secretary Eric Chan on Sunday instructed government departments to ensure the smooth flow of travellers at boundary control points.

His comments come after footage circulated on social media showing what appeared to be long queues at the checkpoint of mostly seven seaters waiting to cross into Shenzhen after midnight.

The tailback stretched all the way to San Tin Highway at one point.

Large numbers of northbound travellers were also stuck in urban areas, with dozens of people lining up for cross-border coach services in Mong Kok.

Many of them had come to Hong Kong for Halloween festivities or a concert in Kai Tak.

Hong Kong Non-Franchised Bus Association chairman Eddie Choi explained that private cars with permits for other checkpoints all diverted to Huanggang after midnight, since it is the only 24-hour crossing to Shenzhen.

Timothy Chui, executive director of the Hong Kong Tourism Association, said there could be even more cross-border revellers next weekend.

He suggested creating dedicated lanes for buses and coaches around the port facility.

Writing on Facebook, the chief secretary said he paid a visit to the Shenzhen Bay and Huanggang control points following a visit to Dongguan.

Chan said he directed the Security Bureau to continue ensuring that port operations remain safe, efficient and orderly.

Authorities were told to proactively assess and forecast passenger traffic, and open additional inspection counters and vehicle lanes ahead of peak periods.

Chan also encouraged travellers to consider staying overnight in the SAR for a more comfortable and fulfilling experience.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: John Catlin wins HK golf open in dominant fashion
articles.excerpt: John Catlin of the United States on Sunday claimed victory at the Hong Kong Open, winning at the iconic Fanling…
articles.fullText:
John Catlin of the United States on Sunday claimed victory at the Hong Kong Open, winning at the iconic Fanling golf course for the seventh Asian Tour trophy of his career.

The California native carded a sizzling six-under-par 64 in round four to finish 20-under overall, holding off local favourite Matthew Cheung and Finland's Kalle Samooja by five strokes.

Thailand's Jazz Janewattananond and Nick Voke of New Zealand finished tied for fourth at 14-under.

It's Catlin's first triumph on the Asian circuit since the 2024 Saudi Open, and adds to victories in Thailand, Macau, and Malaysia.

Catlin went into the final round locked in a tense four-way tie for the lead at 14-under-par alongside compatriot Caleb Surratt, India's Anirban Lahiri, and Thomas Pieters of Belgium.

But a brilliant performance on the 18th-hole sand solidified his place at the top of the leaderboard.

"There were so many great players, and there was a four-way tie for the lead... anything can happen," Catlin told reporters after the win.

"I just tried to focus on what I can control. I didn't know what anyone else was doing, and I didn't look at the leaderboard until I came down the 18th," he added.

"I just tried to keep focused on the shot at hand, and keep trying to execute good golf shots. History has shown me that it's not over until it's over, and so I just kept pushing forward, giving every shot my full undivided attention. And it paid off... I've got this beautiful trophy here."

Victory in the SAR also came with another milestone for Catlin, who is ranked 447 in the world.

With the Asian Tour tournament a part of The Open Qualifying Series, his strong showing in Fanling earned him a highly coveted qualifying ticket to the 155th edition of the prestigious event, which will be played at the historic Old Course in St Andrews next July.

It also guarantees him his maiden qualification for the Masters Tournament in Augusta, Georgia next year.

"It's kind of a dream come true," Catlin said.

"From the time I can remember, I started playing golf when I was three years old, and my goal was always to play in the Masters. This is my thirteenth year as a professional golfer, and I hadn't had the chance to do so. You just never really know if its going to happen."

articles.title: Families enjoy day out at HK golf open finale
articles.excerpt: Hundreds of fans enjoyed a day out with their families at the Fanling Golf Course on Sunday for the final…
articles.fullText:
Hundreds of fans enjoyed a day out with their families at the Fanling Golf Course on Sunday for the final day of Hong Kong Open action.

The four-day event, which is marking its historic 65th edition, teed off on Thursday to much fanfare as the sport's biggest stars descended upon the SAR.

Hans, a local resident attending the tournament for the second time with his kids, told RTHK that the Hong Kong Open is a great opportunity for families to get up close and personal with some of the world's top athletes.

"It's a great event, walking around with the kids... getting close with the different golf professionals," he said.

"It's an awesome experience, being so close to the professional players and also they do a good job of bringing the fan village together," he added. "It's fun for the kids."

Hans also commended the event's fan-friendly atmosphere, saying the interactive stalls, games, and entertainment made the tournament stand out from other sporting events.

Another local fan, Leon – who is attending the event for the sixth year in a row – echoed the sentiment.

"Personally, I play golf and I'm a member of the club. [This event] has such a nice outdoor area for the kids, every year we take them over and have some fun," he told RTHK.

He also pointed out that there were many elements of Hong Kong culture on display at the fan village.

"[Besides] the golf, we have Hong Kong culture, cultural stuff... which is very fun for the kids. I'd definitely recommend it."

Bryant Lu, captain of the Hong Kong Golf Club, said that the competition is a great opportunity for all sports fans to get a taste of a different side of the bustling city.

"I think what we offer is a very unique experience," he told reporters outside the course's clubhouse.

"Being a golfing event we have outdoors... and we can come all the way up to the Northern Metropolis. I think this is the new future for Hong Kong, and hosting an event here not only brings people to play golf but [they can] also experience what changes the Northern Metropolis brings to Hong Kong, I think that's very important.

"I think coming up here you can experience a different side of Hong Kong – beautiful trees, nice grounds, fresh air, and lots of smiling faces."

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Brewers down Rays to take a 2-0 World Series lead
articles.excerpt: The Milwaukee Brewers staged another trademark comeback to defeat the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 and take a commanding 2-0 lead…
articles.fullText:
The Milwaukee Brewers staged another trademark comeback to defeat the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 and take a commanding 2-0 lead in the best-of-seven World Series on Saturday.

The top-seeded Brewers recovered from 4-0 down after an early Tampa Bay onslaught to complete a rally that edges Milwaukee closer to a first Major League Baseball crown.

The win marked the seventh time during this season's playoffs that the Brewers have come from behind to win.

Outfielder Sal Frelick blasted a 408-foot home run in the sixth inning to tie it up for Milwaukee at 4-4 before Cooper Pratt's single in the seventh added what turned out to be the winning run for Brice Turang.

"As long as there's game left we have a chance — and I think we've all bought into that," Pratt said.

"We're never out of it. And when there's still innings on the board we've still got a chance," Pratt added.

Tampa Bay will have the weight of history against them as the series heads back to Florida for game three on Monday.

Only 10 teams have ever recovered from 2-0 down to win the World Series.

Rays manager Kevin Cash believes home-field advantage for the next three games could give Tampa Bay a path back into the series.

"These Milwaukee fans have been really loud. I know our fans are going to be really loud and excited to see us come back and kind of reset ourselves a little bit," Cash said.

"We've got a really good pitcher going, as do they. A lot of confidence in this club to respond. They've done it all season long and they'll continue to do it."

The Rays surged into a commanding 4-0 lead in the top of the first inning with Yandy Diaz scooting to second base after a throwing error by Brewers shortstop Pratt.

Chandler Simpson singled soon afterwards to bring Diaz home and give the Rays a 1-0 lead.

Simpson then used his speed to steal second base and when Junior Caminero drove into the left field, Simpson raced home to score.

The Rays made it 4-0 when catcher Liam Hicks bludgeoned a towering 411-foot two-run homer into the upper deck of right centre-field to further rock the Brewers.

Milwaukee were quick to hit back in the bottom of the inning, with William Contreras singling on a ground ball to score Jackson Chourio.

Garrett Mitchell's single to right field allowed Jake Bauers to score to trim the Rays advantage to two runs.

Milwaukee knocked Tampa Bay starter Drew Rasmussen out of the game in the fourth inning and then pounced with Frelick's home run in the sixth, before Pratt's single in the seventh gave the Brewers the lead.

Brewers reliever Aaron Ashby grabbed the final five outs to secure victory. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Transfusion service brings learning
articles.excerpt: A group of SPHRC Kung Yik She Secondary School students recently received a different kind of biology lesson as they…
articles.fullText:
A group of SPHRC Kung Yik She Secondary School students recently received a different kind of biology lesson as they ventured outside of the classroom on a visit to the Yuen Long Blood Donor Centre.

The Hong Kong Red Cross Blood Transfusion Service expanded its “A Biology Class outside of the Classroom” scheme this year. Originally run exclusively at the service’s headquarters, it is now offered at all donor centres, making it much more accessible to school groups.

Real-life settings
Hong Kong Red Cross Blood Transfusion Service Advanced Practice Nurse Lee Wing-sze explained that guided tours, which last an hour, give students the chance to learn in a relaxed and engaging mode.

“As blood-related knowledge is a part of the senior secondary biology curriculum, we integrate these topics into the visit, allowing students to learn within a real-life setting.”

Giving blood
The tour consists of three parts. First, interactive games and information boards are used to introduce basic concepts such as blood types, donor eligibility, and how blood saves lives.

Students then tour the haemoglobin testing area, donation area and blood processing area, learning about overall workflows and the professional equipment involved.

Finally, staff answer questions on the spot to alleviate anxiety and dispel any fears before students make their own decisions on whether to donate blood.

Secondary school student Ryan Yip said that before he experienced the tour, he felt stressed about giving blood.

“I think this whole process is kind of frightening, but after the nurses told me the process is safe and it is all under standard conditions, I think that really comforted me and gave me some confidence to be a voluntary blood donor.”

Another secondary school student, Kelvin To, said he would urge his friends to donate blood after learning about how donations save lives.

Saving lives
The service’s Head of Blood Collection & Donor Recruitment Department Dr Jacky Kong said that establishing a solid foundation of blood-related knowledge is crucial to encouraging teenagers to become blood donors in the long run.

“We believe that interaction with our staff and blood donors is very important for them to be exposed to why blood donation is important for the public.”

The service reaches out to secondary schools across Hong Kong and, to date, has arranged talks or donor centre visits for more than 60 schools in the current academic year.

SPHRC Kung Yik She Secondary School Principal Liu Siu-lin said she fully supports the lessons the service provides as they allow students to witness first-hand how blood is processed and transformed into life-saving products.

“This unique lesson shows that science is not just about cold data, but about saving lives.”

articles.title: CS attends talent event in Dongguan
articles.excerpt: Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki today attended an opening ceremony for two initiatives promoting the Greater Bay Area (GBA) in Dongguan…
articles.fullText:
Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki today attended an opening ceremony for two initiatives promoting the Greater Bay Area (GBA) in Dongguan – namely the fourth GBA High-quality Talent Development Conference and the third GBA Doctoral and Postdoctoral Innovation and Entrepreneurship Competition.

Addressing the ceremony, he said Hong Kong will continue to attract the talent required for its own and the country's development, and will work with other GBA cities to advance the alignment of rules and mechanisms that facilitate the flow of talent within the area.

Mr Chan outlined that Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan proactively aligns with the National 15th Five-Year Plan and promotes the integrated development of education, technology and talent. He added that the Northern Metropolis University Town will closely connect Hong Kong's strengths in basic research and internationalised education with both the innovation and technology (I&T) and talent resources of the broader GBA.

After the ceremony, Mr Chan and Secretary for Labour and Welfare Chris Sun toured the exhibition hall and visited the Hong Kong Talent Engage booth.

Yesterday, Mr Chan and his delegation visited a key I&T enterprise in Dongguan to better understand the local model of fostering co-operation between the spheres of scientific research, innovation, and talent development. They subsequently toured the City University of Hong Kong (Dongguan) to learn about synergies between Hong Kong and Dongguan in higher education and talent cultivation, and to explore ways of strengthening complementarity between the two places.

Mr Chan and Mr Sun concluded their visit to Dongguan this morning and returned to Hong Kong in the afternoon.

articles.title: Kim makes visit to China via new cross-border bridge
articles.excerpt: Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) leader Kim Jong-un visited the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday, crossing a…
articles.fullText:
Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) leader Kim Jong-un visited the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday, crossing a newly opened bridge.

Upon his arrival, Kim was met by China's top political advisor Wang Huning, who conveyed greetings from President Xi Jinping, according to Xinhua news agency.

Kim crossed via the New Yalu River Bridge, a major border crossing that officially opened last week, deepening economic ties between China and the DPRK.

The three-kilometre bridge is the most significant land border crossing between both countries.

During a meeting, ​Wang, chairman of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, told Kim that China was ⁠ready to use the bridge's opening to expand personnel exchanges and economic and trade cooperation, Xinhua said.

CCTV reported that Kim took part in a memorial service to pay tribute to martyrs of the Chinese People's Volunteer Army and visited an automobile factory.

His visit came a day before the anniversary of China joining the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea, in 1950.

Wang saw Kim off at the bridge at the end of the trip, Xinhua reported. (Agencies)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Live K-pop show makes South Korea more real to former North Korean arts troupe singer
articles.excerpt: “I really am in the South now,” said Cho Mi-young - at her first K-pop show - 22 years after…
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Korean .
A white tiger entered the courtyard outside the National Museum in Seoul. He mugged for the camera and darted up the steps. At the top were the six members of BOYNEXTDOOR, wearing quasi-traditional outfits that mixed elements of hanbok with modern formal wear and a tinge of “bad boy” biker gear.
As they danced in unison and sang the opening lines of their hit single “Animal,” the crowd went wild.
Sitting in the audience was Cho Mi-young – born in Chongjin, North Korea – who arrived with her family in the South in 2004.
Mi-young can’t contain herself. “You’re so amazing!” she cries out, as the monitors show the young men dominating the courtyard with their precise dance moves.
Cho is in the audience at an episode of KBS Music Bank, a Friday night K-pop showcase program with all the latest acts. It has been the start of the K-pop weekend for most of its 28-year runtime. Surprisingly, it’s her first time ever seeing a live K-pop performance in person after 22 years in the South.
Tickets to studio tapings of KBS Music Bank are hard to come by. Fans either have to know someone, know someone who knows someone, or enter the ticket lottery. The episode she’s watching on Oct. 16 is special - it’s a live broadcast and the biggest boy bands, girl bands, and boy-girl bands are plying their craft on an outdoor stage on the grounds of the National Museum of Korea, which the show’s special intro vignette called the “beating heart of Korean culture.”
When the opening act was finished, the show’s hosts began introducing this week’s lineup, as Cho and the rest of the audience settled in. Many more K-pop groups and solo artists would take the stage in front of them on a night they would likely all remember forever.
“I’ve seen it a lot on TV, but today is the first time I’ve seen it with my own eyes,” Cho told Radio Free Asia. “Seeing such beautiful and handsome people dancing and singing right in front of me, moving like that, is absolutely mesmerizing.”
Cho is no stranger to music, or to the stage. In North Korea she had been a vocalist for a state-run provincial arts troupe. After settling in the South, Cho was a fixture in Seoul’s burgeoning musical theater scene and she toured as an accordion player. She later transitioned into broadcasting, at one point even co-hosting the RFA Korean webseries “ Northboy Northgirl .”
At present, she runs a content production company and maintains an active presence both online and in traditional media.
Cho Mi-young watches a live broadcast of KBS Music Bank at the National Museum of Korea in Seoul, Oct. 16, 2026.
(RFA) But today, she’s just a fangirl in a sea of other diehards, most of whom are screaming the names of the idols on stage.
Music in isolation
On the night of her first live K-pop concert, Cho reminisced about how she first encountered South Korean music in North Korea. At the time, she didn’t have access to what most would describe as K-pop today; instead she took in a lot of trot – a unique South Korean genre that mixes Western foxtrot dance rhythms with pentatonic minor scale melodies. Most young South Koreans consider trot to be music their grandparents like.
But after arriving in the South, she became a huge fan of South Korean love ballads, much slower than the catchiest K-pop numbers, but thicker in emotion. Music occupied much of her daily life in the South early on, as she scanned the radio for something new to listen to.
Today’s performances on the Music Bank stage were a far cry from her own back in North Korea. For one, everyone on stage just seems happy to be there, she said.
“When I performed in North Korea, I was always stiff,” she said. “When we were on stage, we performed with the mindset of conveying the Party’s voice, so I don’t think I ever had the thought that we were actually enjoying our own music.”
Several more musical acts came and went and then the undistorted electric guitar of indie rock band Jannabi’s Kim Do-hyung echoed through the air as vocalist Choi Jung-hoon sang the first few lyrics of “Thoughts on an Autumn Night.”
“Even on that distant shining star up there… love must be alive singing its song.”
The song struck a chord with Cho. Performed by just one singer and one guitarist it was a bit of a shift from the rest of the evening’s heavily choreographed bangers.
“The lyrical melody seems to have a bit of North Korean sensibility to it.”
She sat there, transfixed by Jannabi’s intimate, scaled down performance on the stage and quietly sang along.
“I really am in the South now”
When it was all over, Cho talked about her experience on the show, but it wasn’t only the dazzle of the K-pop acts that caught her eye. She was also amazed by the devoted fans, who sang along with every lyric from memory and chanted in pre-arranged cheers in unison. She thought back to how strange that seemed when she first arrived.
“I didn’t understand it in the past. But as I’ve lived here longer, I’ve come to understand the fans and their pre-prepared chants,” she said. “I think maybe next time, I might enjoy it even more if I learned those.”
The best performance of the evening, according to Cho, was by a co-ed group called AllDay Project. She thought they looked cool in their all-black outfits, some in furs, others in biker leather – almost like warriors.
But as an artist, Cho’s thoughts naturally turned to the massive effort that must have gone on behind the scenes. The meticulous choreography alone must take many months of practice, she said.
She recalled how she herself had put in a lot of effort as a singer back in North Korea.
“Even in North Korea, artists are trained very strictly in a Spartan manner,” she said. “In terms of the sheer volume of training, it might be difficult to see a significant difference between the North and South.”
But she noted that the payoff in the South is individual success, unlike the North, where it would merely advance the goals of the state.
She said the whole evening was surreal. Back when she was in North Korea, she could maybe catch glimpses of what the music scene in the South was like, but she could never actually see it. Now she finally has seen it in person, “it sinks in that I really am in the South now.”
Cho said that she thinks any North Korean escapee would probably feel the same way.
“The emotion felt in the live setting is completely different from listening to a recording,” she said. “I think many escapees would finally feel they truly have arrived in South Korea when they go to the venue, see the singer in person, and listen to the songs live.”
Edited by Yi Yongin in Korean and Eugene Whong in English.

articles.title: China closes 3 Tibetan schools in 3 months; threatens language, cultural preservation
articles.excerpt: Shutting schools in Golog region, Qinghai province, comes three months after "ethnic unity law" enacted on July 1.
articles.fullText:
Chinese authorities have shut down three Tibetan schools in the Golog region of Qinghai province in recent months, leaving the fate of students and teachers unclear, according to sources inside Tibet.
The closures of Gangjong Grassland Girls’ School, Jasag Village Primary School and Golog Tadra Orphan School have raised concerns among Tibetans about the future of education that incorporates their language, cultural traditions and community life.
Tibetan sources who spoke to Radio Free Asia linked the closures to the Chinese government’s education policies and its promotion of the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law , which took effect on July 1, 2026. They said the shutdowns could further limit opportunities for Tibetan children to learn their mother tongue and cultural traditions.
The Chinese government has cited the high altitude of Golog and shortages of teachers and educational resources as reasons for establishing schools outside the region, saying the move would improve education. It remains unclear where students from the three closed schools will continue their studies.
Education department declines to comment
RFA contacted the education department of the Golog Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture by phone to seek details about the closures.
“We don’t know the details,” the person told RFA, saying the initial work had been carried out by the Machen County administration and that the county’s education department was responsible for the matter.
RFA also contacted the Machen County Education Department, which said it had “no authority to respond.”
Unclear future for students
Gangjong Grassland Girls’ School in Ragya Township, Machen County, was closed on Aug. 28, according to a source in Tibet who spoke to RFA on condition of anonymity for security reasons.
The school had about 450 students and 60 teachers at the time of its closure, the source said. The current situation of the students remains unclear.
Gangjong Grassland Girls’ School in an undated photo.
(Citizen photo) The source said the school had been made a government-affiliated institution, with its curriculum following the Chinese government’s education system while retaining some Tibetan-language instruction.
“Currently, the schools in the Golog region are conducting a strong patriotic reeducation campaign,” the source said, adding that Tibetans were afraid to share information because of government restrictions.
Jasag Village Primary School, which was established in 1995 with funds raised by local nomadic families and renamed Ragya Township Residential School No. 2 in 2008, was shut down in September, according to information obtained by RFA. Another source in Tibet told RFA that the situation of its students and teachers remained unclear.
“The Golog Education Department has put considerable pressure on the school’s teachers and shut down the school without providing any clear explanation,” the source said.
Golog Tadra Orphanage School was ordered to close this month, according to information obtained by RFA. Founded in 2005, it provided education and support to Tibetan orphans and disadvantaged children for two decades.
At an event marking the school’s 20th anniversary in 2025, principal Thupten Nyima of the Golog Tadra Orphan School, which provides K-12 education, said it was training more than 1,000 students. Some graduates had gone on to work in government positions and as teachers, he said.
Nyima addressed students and teachers in a recent video posted to social media, saying, “Don’t be sad, students and teachers. If we are bound by karma and fate, all the teachers and students gathered here will sing a song of joy together.”
It is unclear if Nyima’s remarks were made around the time the school was ordered to close.
Gangjong Grassland Girls’ School in an undated photo.
(Citizen photo) Critics warn of cultural impact
Dr. Gyal Lo, a Tibetan educational sociologist, said the closures marked a significant change in the Chinese government’s education policy in Tibet.
“The Chinese government sees schools where Tibetans can organize themselves to learn and teach their own culture as a thorn in its side. That is why these schools are being abolished,” he told RFA.
“After Xi Jinping visited Qinghai, the school established by Jigme Gyaltsen was closed , and a new secondary school was built in the eastern part of Ziling,” he said.
Gyal Lo said the closures could distance children from Tibetan traditions and customs practiced in their communities and place them in state-run boarding schools where Chinese is the language of instruction.
“The first impact of the Chinese government’s school closures is that children are distanced from the Tibetan traditions and customs practiced in their homeland. Secondly, when these children enter state-run boarding schools, the entire curriculum is taught in Chinese and is under the government’s control,” he said.
He argued that the policies could affect the transmission of Tibetan identity across generations.
“The aim is to turn the entire Tibetan people into Chinese. This is not limited to a small area; it is a plan with far-reaching consequences,” Gyal Lo told RFA. “The ultimate goal is to turn the younger generation of Tibetans into Chinese through different methods and policies implemented in different regions.”
He also emphasized the role of families in preserving the Tibetan language.
“According to language education theory, a language cannot be passed on to the next generation without being taught within the family. The foundation for preserving the mother tongue and passing it on to the next generation must be laid at home,” he said.
Tenzin Lekshey, spokesperson for the Central Tibetan Administration in Dharamsala, India, said Tibetan schools and monasteries played an important role in preserving the community’s language, culture, traditions and identity.
“The Chinese government is doing all this out of fear. Tibetan schools and monasteries established inside Tibet aim to preserve and protect the rich Tibetan language, culture, traditions and identity. But the Chinese government views these institutions as a hindrance rather than a benefit,” he told RFA.
Ragya Geshe Lobsang Palden, a former political prisoner, said the new ethnic unity law had coincided with the closure of several Tibetan schools, some of which had already been brought under government control.
“These schools could not be shut down before because it was not legally appropriate to do so. Now, with the new Ethnic Unity Law in effect since July, many schools have been closing down,” he told RFA.
“However, many of these schools had already been converted into government-affiliated schools several years ago,” he added.
Dawa Tashi, a researcher at the Tibetan Centre for Human Rights and Democracy in Dharamsala, also linked the closures to the new law, saying it formalized policies that threatened Tibetan cultural and linguistic identity.
A former Tibetan political prisoner who visited Gangjong Grassland Girls’ School in 2006 said many of its graduates had gone on to serve their communities. The source requested anonymity for security reasons.
“I remember speaking with a teacher at the school in 2006 who told me that several teachers had been summoned by Chinese authorities. The teacher anticipated that the school might eventually be closed,” the source told RFA.
New government boarding schools
The closures come amid a broader restructuring of education in Golog, where authorities have promoted Chinese-language education and campaigns emphasizing national unity.
